9.8: ו Vav And He will judge the world in righteousness; He will render justice for the peoples with equity.
9.9: ו Vav Yahweh also will be a stronghold for the oppressed, A stronghold in times of distress;
9.10: ו Vav And those who know Your name will put their trust in You, For You, O Yahweh, have not forsaken those who seek You.
9.11: ז Zayin Sing praises to Yahweh, who abides in Zion; Declare among the peoples His acts.
9.12: For He who requires blood remembers them; He does not forget the cry of the afflicted.
9.13: ח Heth Be gracious to me, O Yahweh; See my affliction from those who hate me, You who lift me up from the gates of death,
9.14: That I may recount all Your praises, That in the gates of the daughter of Zion I may rejoice in Your salvation.
9.15: ט Teth The nations have sunk down in the pit which they have made; In the net which they hid, their own foot has been caught.
9.16: Yahweh has made Himself known; He has executed judgment. In the work of his own hands the wicked is snared. Higgaion Selah.
9.17: י Yodh The wicked will return to Sheol, Even all the nations who forget God.
9.18: כ Kaph For the needy will not always be forgotten, Nor the hope of the afflicted perish forever.
9.19: Arise, O Yahweh, do not let man prevail; Let the nations be judged before You.
9.20: Put them in fear, O Yahweh; Let the nations know that they are but men. Selah.

35.1: Of David.Contend, O Yahweh, with those who contend with me; Fight against those who fight against me.
35.2: Take hold of shield and large shield And rise up for my help.
35.3: Draw also the spear and the battle‑axe to meet those who pursue me; Say to my soul, “I am your salvation.”
35.4: Let those be ashamed and dishonored who seek my life; Let those who devise evil against me be turned back and humiliated.
35.5: Let them be like chaff before the wind, With the angel of Yahweh driving them on.
35.6: Let their way be dark and slippery, With the angel of Yahweh pursuing them.
35.7: For without cause they hid their net for me; Without cause they dug a pit for my soul.
35.8: Let destruction, which he does not know, come upon him, And let the net, which he hid, catch him; Let him fall into it in destruction.
35.9: And my soul shall rejoice in Yahweh; It shall be joyful in His salvation.
35.10: All my bones will say, “Yahweh, who is like You, Who delivers the afflicted from him who is too strong for him, And the afflicted and the needy from him who robs him?”
35.11: Malicious witnesses rise up, Who ask me of things that I do not know.
35.12: They repay me evil for good, It is bereavement to my soul.
35.13: But as for me, when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth; I humbled my soul with fasting, And my prayer kept returning to my bosom.
35.14: I walked about as though it were my friend or brother; I bowed down mourning, as one who sorrows for a mother.
35.15: But at my stumbling they were glad and gathered themselves together; The smiters whom I did not know gathered together against me, They tore at me and never were silent.
35.16: Amongst the godless jesters at a feast, They gnashed at me with their teeth.
35.17: Lord, how long will You look on? Bring back my soul from their ravages, My only life from the lions.
35.18: I will give You thanks in the great assembly; I will praise You among a mighty people.
35.19: Let those who are wrongfully my enemies not be glad over me; Nor let those who hate me without cause wink maliciously.
35.20: For they do not speak peace, But they devise deceitful words against those who are quiet in the land.
35.21: They opened their mouth wide against me; They said, “Aha, aha, our eyes have seen it!”
35.22: You have seen it, O Yahweh, do not keep silent; O Lord, do not be far from me.
35.23: Stir up Yourself, and awake to my justice And to my cause, my God and my Lord.
35.24: Judge me, O Yahweh my God, according to Your righteousness, And do not let them be glad over me.
35.25: Do not let them say in their heart, “Aha, our desire!” Do not let them say, “We have swallowed him up!”
35.26: Let those be ashamed and humiliated altogether who are glad at the evil done to me; Let those be clothed with shame and dishonor who magnify themselves over me.
35.27: Let them shout for joy and be glad, who delight in my righteousness; And let them say continually, “Yahweh be magnified, Who delights in the peace of His slave.”
35.28: And my tongue shall utter Your righteousness And Your praise all day long.

74.1: A psalm of Asaph. O God, why have you rejected us so long? Why is your anger so intense against the sheep of your own pasture?
74.2: Remember that we are the people you chose long ago, the tribe you redeemed as your own special possession! And remember Jerusalem, your home here on earth.
74.3: Walk through the awful ruins of the city; see how the enemy has destroyed your sanctuary.
74.4: There your enemies shouted their victorious battle cries; there they set up their battle standards.
74.5: They swung their axes like woodcutters in a forest.
74.6: With axes and picks, they smashed the carved paneling.
74.7: They burned your sanctuary to the ground. They defiled the place that bears your name.
74.8: Then they thought, “Let’s destroy everything!” So they burned down all the places where God was worshiped.
74.9: We no longer see your miraculous signs. All the prophets are gone, and no one can tell us when it will end.
74.10: How long, O God, will you allow our enemies to insult you? Will you let them dishonor your name forever?
74.11: Why do you hold back your strong right hand? Unleash your powerful fist and destroy them.
74.12: You, O God, are my king from ages past, bringing salvation to the earth.
74.13: You split the sea by your strength and smashed the heads of the sea monsters.
74.14: You crushed the heads of Leviathan and let the desert animals eat him.
74.15: You caused the springs and streams to gush forth, and you dried up rivers that never run dry.
74.16: Both day and night belong to you; you made the starlight and the sun.
74.17: You set the boundaries of the earth, and you made both summer and winter.
74.18: See how these enemies insult you, Lord. A foolish nation has dishonored your name.
74.19: Don’t let these wild beasts destroy your turtledoves. Don’t forget your suffering people forever.
74.20: Remember your covenant promises, for the land is full of darkness and violence!
74.21: Don’t let the downtrodden be humiliated again. Instead, let the poor and needy praise your name.
74.22: Arise, O God, and defend your cause. Remember how these fools insult you all day long.
74.23: Don’t overlook what your enemies have said or their growing uproar.

23.1: A psalm of David. The Lord is my shepherd; I have all that I need.
23.2: He lets me rest in green meadows; he leads me beside peaceful streams.
23.3: He renews my strength. He guides me along right paths, bringing honor to his name.
23.4: Even when I walk through the darkest valley, I will not be afraid, for you are close beside me. Your rod and your staff protect and comfort me.
23.5: You prepare a feast for me in the presence of my enemies. You honor me by anointing my head with oil. My cup overflows with blessings.
23.6: Surely your goodness and unfailing love will pursue me all the days of my life, and I will live in the house of the Lord forever.

35.1: A psalm of David. O Lord, oppose those who oppose me. Fight those who fight against me.
35.2: Put on your armor, and take up your shield. Prepare for battle, and come to my aid.
35.3: Lift up your spear and javelin against those who pursue me. Let me hear you say, “I will give you victory!”
35.4: Bring shame and disgrace on those trying to kill me; turn them back and humiliate those who want to harm me.
35.5: Blow them away like chaff in the wind— a wind sent by the angel of the Lord.
35.6: Make their path dark and slippery, with the angel of the Lord pursuing them.
35.7: I did them no wrong, but they laid a trap for me. I did them no wrong, but they dug a pit to catch me.
35.8: So let sudden ruin come upon them! Let them be caught in the trap they set for me! Let them be destroyed in the pit they dug for me.
35.9: Then I will rejoice in the Lord. I will be glad because he rescues me.
35.10: With every bone in my body I will praise him: “Lord, who can compare with you? Who else rescues the helpless from the strong? Who else protects the helpless and poor from those who rob them?”
35.11: Malicious witnesses testify against me. They accuse me of crimes I know nothing about.
35.12: They repay me evil for good. I am sick with despair.
35.13: Yet when they were ill, I grieved for them. I denied myself by fasting for them, but my prayers returned unanswered.
35.14: I was sad, as though they were my friends or family, as if I were grieving for my own mother.
35.15: But they are glad now that I am in trouble; they gleefully join together against me. I am attacked by people I don’t even know; they slander me constantly.
35.16: They mock me and call me names; they snarl at me.
35.17: How long, O Lord, will you look on and do nothing? Rescue me from their fierce attacks. Protect my life from these lions!
35.18: Then I will thank you in front of the great assembly. I will praise you before all the people.
35.19: Don’t let my treacherous enemies rejoice over my defeat. Don’t let those who hate me without cause gloat over my sorrow.
35.20: They don’t talk of peace; they plot against innocent people who mind their own business.
35.21: They shout, “Aha! Aha! With our own eyes we saw him do it!”
35.22: O Lord, you know all about this. Do not stay silent. Do not abandon me now, O Lord.
35.23: Wake up! Rise to my defense! Take up my case, my God and my Lord.
35.24: Declare me not guilty, O Lord my God, for you give justice. Don’t let my enemies laugh about me in my troubles.
35.25: Don’t let them say, “Look, we got what we wanted! Now we will eat him alive!”
35.26: May those who rejoice at my troubles be humiliated and disgraced. May those who triumph over me be covered with shame and dishonor.
35.27: But give great joy to those who came to my defense. Let them continually say, “Great is the Lord, who delights in blessing his servant with peace!”
35.28: Then I will proclaim your justice, and I will praise you all day long.

62.1: For Jeduthun, the choir director: A psalm of David. I wait quietly before God, for my victory comes from him.
62.2: He alone is my rock and my salvation, my fortress where I will never be shaken.
62.3: So many enemies against one man— all of them trying to kill me. To them I’m just a broken-down wall or a tottering fence.
62.4: They plan to topple me from my high position. They delight in telling lies about me. They praise me to my face but curse me in their hearts. Interlude
62.5: Let all that I am wait quietly before God, for my hope is in him.
62.6: He alone is my rock and my salvation, my fortress where I will not be shaken.
62.7: My victory and honor come from God alone. He is my refuge, a rock where no enemy can reach me.
62.8: O my people, trust in him at all times. Pour out your heart to him, for God is our refuge. Interlude
62.9: Common people are as worthless as a puff of wind, and the powerful are not what they appear to be. If you weigh them on the scales, together they are lighter than a breath of air.
62.10: Don’t make your living by extortion or put your hope in stealing. And if your wealth increases, don’t make it the center of your life.
62.11: God has spoken plainly, and I have heard it many times: Power, O God, belongs to you
62.12: unfailing love, O Lord, is yours. Surely you repay all people according to what they have done.

9.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David, to be sung to the tune “Death of the Son.” I will praise you, Lord, with all my heart; I will tell of all the marvelous things you have done.
9.2: I will be filled with joy because of you. I will sing praises to your name, O Most High.
9.3: My enemies retreated; they staggered and died when you appeared.
9.4: For you have judged in my favor; from your throne you have judged with fairness.
9.5: You have rebuked the nations and destroyed the wicked; you have erased their names forever.
9.6: The enemy is finished, in endless ruins; the cities you uprooted are now forgotten.
9.7: But the Lord reigns forever, executing judgment from his throne.
9.8: He will judge the world with justice and rule the nations with fairness.
9.9: The Lord is a shelter for the oppressed, a refuge in times of trouble.
9.10: Those who know your name trust in you, for you, O Lord, do not abandon those who search for you.
9.11: Sing praises to the Lord who reigns in Jerusalem. Tell the world about his unforgettable deeds.
9.12: For he who avenges murder cares for the helpless. He does not ignore the cries of those who suffer.
9.13: Lord, have mercy on me. See how my enemies torment me. Snatch me back from the jaws of death.
9.14: Save me so I can praise you publicly at Jerusalem’s gates, so I can rejoice that you have rescued me.
9.15: The nations have fallen into the pit they dug for others. Their own feet have been caught in the trap they set.
9.16: The Lord is known for his justice. The wicked are trapped by their own deeds. Quiet Interlude
9.17: The wicked will go down to the grave. This is the fate of all the nations who ignore God.
9.18: But the needy will not be ignored forever; the hopes of the poor will not always be crushed.
9.19: Arise, O Lord! Do not let mere mortals defy you! Judge the nations!
9.20: Make them tremble in fear, O Lord. Let the nations know they are merely human. Interlude

141.1: A psalm of David. O Lord, I am calling to you. Please hurry! Listen when I cry to you for help!
141.2: Accept my prayer as incense offered to you, and my upraised hands as an evening offering.
141.3: Take control of what I say, O Lord, and guard my lips.
141.4: Don’t let me drift toward evil or take part in acts of wickedness. Don’t let me share in the delicacies of those who do wrong.
141.5: Let the godly strike me! It will be a kindness! If they correct me, it is soothing medicine. Don’t let me refuse it. But I pray constantly against the wicked and their deeds.
141.6: When their leaders are thrown down from a cliff, the wicked will listen to my words and find them true.
141.7: Like rocks brought up by a plow, the bones of the wicked will lie scattered without burial.
141.8: I look to you for help, O Sovereign Lord. You are my refuge; don’t let them kill me.
141.9: Keep me from the traps they have set for me, from the snares of those who do wrong.
141.10: Let the wicked fall into their own nets, but let me escape.

19.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David. The heavens proclaim the glory of God. The skies display his craftsmanship.
19.2: Day after day they continue to speak; night after night they make him known.
19.3: They speak without a sound or word; their voice is never heard.
19.4: Yet their message has gone throughout the earth, and their words to all the world. God has made a home in the heavens for the sun.
19.5: It bursts forth like a radiant bridegroom after his wedding. It rejoices like a great athlete eager to run the race.
19.6: The sun rises at one end of the heavens and follows its course to the other end. Nothing can hide from its heat.
19.7: The instructions of the Lord are perfect, reviving the soul. The decrees of the Lord are trustworthy, making wise the simple.
19.8: The commandments of the Lord are right, bringing joy to the heart. The commands of the Lord are clear, giving insight for living.
19.9: Reverence for the Lord is pure, lasting forever. The laws of the Lord are true; each one is fair.
19.10: They are more desirable than gold, even the finest gold. They are sweeter than honey, even honey dripping from the comb.
19.11: They are a warning to your servant, a great reward for those who obey them.
19.12: How can I know all the sins lurking in my heart? Cleanse me from these hidden faults.
19.13: Keep your servant from deliberate sins! Don’t let them control me. Then I will be free of guilt and innocent of great sin.
19.14: May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be pleasing to you, O Lord, my rock and my redeemer.

116.1: I love the Lord because he hears my voice and my prayer for mercy.
116.2: Because he bends down to listen, I will pray as long as I have breath!
116.3: Death wrapped its ropes around me; the terrors of the grave overtook me. I saw only trouble and sorrow.
116.4: Then I called on the name of the Lord: “Please, Lord, save me!”
116.5: How kind the Lord is! How good he is! So merciful, this God of ours!
116.6: The Lord protects those of childlike faith; I was facing death, and he saved me.
116.7: Let my soul be at rest again, for the Lord has been good to me.
116.8: He has saved me from death, my eyes from tears, my feet from stumbling.
116.9: And so I walk in the Lord’s presence as I live here on earth!
116.10: I believed in you, so I said, “I am deeply troubled, Lord.”
116.11: In my anxiety I cried out to you, “These people are all liars!”
116.12: What can I offer the Lord for all he has done for me?
116.13: I will lift up the cup of salvation and praise the Lord’s name for saving me.
116.14: I will keep my promises to the Lord in the presence of all his people.
116.15: The Lord cares deeply when his loved ones die.
116.16: O Lord, I am your servant; yes, I am your servant, born into your household; you have freed me from my chains.
116.17: I will offer you a sacrifice of thanksgiving and call on the name of the Lord.
116.18: I will fulfill my vows to the Lord in the presence of all his people—
116.19: in the house of the Lord in the heart of Jerusalem. Praise the Lord!

100.1: A psalm of thanksgiving. Shout with joy to the Lord, all the earth!
100.2: Worship the Lord with gladness. Come before him, singing with joy.
100.3: Acknowledge that the Lord is God! He made us, and we are his. We are his people, the sheep of his pasture.
100.4: Enter his gates with thanksgiving; go into his courts with praise. Give thanks to him and praise his name.
100.5: For the Lord is good. His unfailing love continues forever, and his faithfulness continues to each generation.

58.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David, to be sung to the tune “Do Not Destroy!” Justice—do you rulers know the meaning of the word? Do you judge the people fairly?
58.2: No! You plot injustice in your hearts. You spread violence throughout the land.
58.3: These wicked people are born sinners; even from birth they have lied and gone their own way.
58.4: They spit venom like deadly snakes; they are like cobras that refuse to listen,
58.5: ignoring the tunes of the snake charmers, no matter how skillfully they play.
58.6: Break off their fangs, O God! Smash the jaws of these lions, O Lord!
58.7: May they disappear like water into thirsty ground. Make their weapons useless in their hands.
58.8: May they be like snails that dissolve into slime, like a stillborn child who will never see the sun.
58.9: God will sweep them away, both young and old, faster than a pot heats over burning thorns.
58.10: The godly will rejoice when they see injustice avenged. They will wash their feet in the blood of the wicked.
58.11: Then at last everyone will say, “There truly is a reward for those who live for God; surely there is a God who judges justly here on earth.”

120.1: A song for pilgrims ascending to Jerusalem. I took my troubles to the Lord; I cried out to him, and he answered my prayer.
120.2: Rescue me, O Lord, from liars and from all deceitful people.
120.3: O deceptive tongue, what will God do to you? How will he increase your punishment?
120.4: You will be pierced with sharp arrows and burned with glowing coals.
120.5: How I suffer in far-off Meshech. It pains me to live in distant Kedar.
120.6: I am tired of living among people who hate peace.
120.7: I search for peace; but when I speak of peace, they want war!

78.1: A psalm of Asaph. O my people, listen to my instructions. Open your ears to what I am saying,
78.2: for I will speak to you in a parable. I will teach you hidden lessons from our past—
78.3: stories we have heard and known, stories our ancestors handed down to us.
78.4: We will not hide these truths from our children; we will tell the next generation about the glorious deeds of the Lord, about his power and his mighty wonders.
78.5: For he issued his laws to Jacob; he gave his instructions to Israel. He commanded our ancestors to teach them to their children,
78.6: so the next generation might know them— even the children not yet born— and they in turn will teach their own children.
78.7: So each generation should set its hope anew on God, not forgetting his glorious miracles and obeying his commands.
78.8: Then they will not be like their ancestors— stubborn, rebellious, and unfaithful, refusing to give their hearts to God.
78.9: The warriors of Ephraim, though armed with bows, turned their backs and fled on the day of battle.
78.10: They did not keep God’s covenant and refused to live by his instructions.
78.11: They forgot what he had done— the great wonders he had shown them,
78.12: the miracles he did for their ancestors on the plain of Zoan in the land of Egypt.
78.13: For he divided the sea and led them through, making the water stand up like walls!
78.14: In the daytime he led them by a cloud, and all night by a pillar of fire.
78.15: He split open the rocks in the wilderness to give them water, as from a gushing spring.
78.16: He made streams pour from the rock, making the waters flow down like a river!
78.17: Yet they kept on sinning against him, rebelling against the Most High in the desert.
78.18: They stubbornly tested God in their hearts, demanding the foods they craved.
78.19: They even spoke against God himself, saying, “God can’t give us food in the wilderness.
78.20: Yes, he can strike a rock so water gushes out, but he can’t give his people bread and meat.”
78.21: When the Lord heard them, he was furious. The fire of his wrath burned against Jacob. Yes, his anger rose against Israel,
78.22: for they did not believe God or trust him to care for them.
78.23: But he commanded the skies to open; he opened the doors of heaven.
78.24: He rained down manna for them to eat; he gave them bread from heaven.
78.25: They ate the food of angels! God gave them all they could hold.
78.26: He released the east wind in the heavens and guided the south wind by his mighty power.
78.27: He rained down meat as thick as dust— birds as plentiful as the sand on the seashore!
78.28: He caused the birds to fall within their camp and all around their tents.
78.29: The people ate their fill. He gave them what they craved.
78.30: But before they satisfied their craving, while the meat was yet in their mouths,
78.31: the anger of God rose against them, and he killed their strongest men. He struck down the finest of Israel’s young men.
78.32: But in spite of this, the people kept sinning. Despite his wonders, they refused to trust him.
78.33: So he ended their lives in failure, their years in terror.
78.34: When God began killing them, they finally sought him. They repented and took God seriously.
78.35: Then they remembered that God was their rock, that God Most High was their redeemer.
78.36: But all they gave him was lip service; they lied to him with their tongues.
78.37: Their hearts were not loyal to him. They did not keep his covenant.
78.38: Yet he was merciful and forgave their sins and did not destroy them all. Many times he held back his anger and did not unleash his fury!
78.39: For he remembered that they were merely mortal, gone like a breath of wind that never returns.
78.40: Oh, how often they rebelled against him in the wilderness and grieved his heart in that dry wasteland.
78.41: Again and again they tested God’s patience and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
78.42: They did not remember his power and how he rescued them from their enemies.
78.43: They did not remember his miraculous signs in Egypt, his wonders on the plain of Zoan.
78.44: For he turned their rivers into blood, so no one could drink from the streams.
78.45: He sent vast swarms of flies to consume them and hordes of frogs to ruin them.
78.46: He gave their crops to caterpillars; their harvest was consumed by locusts.
78.47: He destroyed their grapevines with hail and shattered their sycamore-figs with sleet.
78.48: He abandoned their cattle to the hail, their livestock to bolts of lightning.
78.49: He loosed on them his fierce anger— all his fury, rage, and hostility. He dispatched against them a band of destroying angels.
78.50: He turned his anger against them; he did not spare the Egyptians’ lives but ravaged them with the plague.
78.51: He killed the oldest son in each Egyptian family, the flower of youth throughout the land of Egypt.
78.52: But he led his own people like a flock of sheep, guiding them safely through the wilderness.
78.53: He kept them safe so they were not afraid; but the sea covered their enemies.
78.54: He brought them to the border of his holy land, to this land of hills he had won for them.
78.55: He drove out the nations before them; he gave them their inheritance by lot. He settled the tribes of Israel into their homes.
78.56: But they kept testing and rebelling against God Most High. They did not obey his laws.
78.57: They turned back and were as faithless as their parents. They were as undependable as a crooked bow.
78.58: They angered God by building shrines to other gods; they made him jealous with their idols.
78.59: When God heard them, he was very angry, and he completely rejected Israel.
78.60: Then he abandoned his dwelling at Shiloh, the Tabernacle where he had lived among the people.
78.61: He allowed the Ark of his might to be captured; he surrendered his glory into enemy hands.
78.62: He gave his people over to be butchered by the sword, because he was so angry with his own people—his special possession.
78.63: Their young men were killed by fire; their young women died before singing their wedding songs.
78.64: Their priests were slaughtered, and their widows could not mourn their deaths.
78.65: Then the Lord rose up as though waking from sleep, like a warrior aroused from a drunken stupor.
78.66: He routed his enemies and sent them to eternal shame.
78.67: But he rejected Joseph’s descendants; he did not choose the tribe of Ephraim.
78.68: He chose instead the tribe of Judah, and Mount Zion, which he loved.
78.69: There he built his sanctuary as high as the heavens, as solid and enduring as the earth.
78.70: He chose his servant David, calling him from the sheep pens.
78.71: He took David from tending the ewes and lambs and made him the shepherd of Jacob’s descendants— God’s own people, Israel.
78.72: He cared for them with a true heart and led them with skillful hands.

97.1: The Lord is king! Let the earth rejoice! Let the farthest coastlands be glad.
97.2: Dark clouds surround him. Righteousness and justice are the foundation of his throne.
97.3: Fire spreads ahead of him and burns up all his foes.
97.4: His lightning flashes out across the world. The earth sees and trembles.
97.5: The mountains melt like wax before the Lord, before the Lord of all the earth.
97.6: The heavens proclaim his righteousness; every nation sees his glory.
97.7: Those who worship idols are disgraced— all who brag about their worthless gods— for every god must bow to him.
97.8: Jerusalem has heard and rejoiced, and all the towns of Judah are glad because of your justice, O Lord!
97.9: For you, O Lord, are supreme over all the earth; you are exalted far above all gods.
97.10: You who love the Lord, hate evil! He protects the lives of his godly people and rescues them from the power of the wicked.
97.11: Light shines on the godly, and joy on those whose hearts are right.
97.12: May all who are godly rejoice in the Lord and praise his holy name!

39.1: For Jeduthun, the choir director: A psalm of David. I said to myself, “I will watch what I do and not sin in what I say. I will hold my tongue when the ungodly are around me.”
39.2: But as I stood there in silence— not even speaking of good things— the turmoil within me grew worse.
39.3: The more I thought about it, the hotter I got, igniting a fire of words:
39.4: “Lord, remind me how brief my time on earth will be. Remind me that my days are numbered— how fleeting my life is.
39.5: You have made my life no longer than the width of my hand. My entire lifetime is just a moment to you; at best, each of us is but a breath.” Interlude
39.6: We are merely moving shadows, and all our busy rushing ends in nothing. We heap up wealth, not knowing who will spend it.
39.7: And so, Lord, where do I put my hope? My only hope is in you.
39.8: Rescue me from my rebellion. Do not let fools mock me.
39.9: I am silent before you; I won’t say a word, for my punishment is from you.
39.10: But please stop striking me! I am exhausted by the blows from your hand.
39.11: When you discipline us for our sins, you consume like a moth what is precious to us. Each of us is but a breath. Interlude
39.12: Hear my prayer, O Lord! Listen to my cries for help! Don’t ignore my tears. For I am your guest— a traveler passing through, as my ancestors were before me.
39.13: Leave me alone so I can smile again before I am gone and exist no more.

136.1: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good! His faithful love endures forever.
136.2: Give thanks to the God of gods. His faithful love endures forever.
136.3: Give thanks to the Lord of lords. His faithful love endures forever.
136.4: Give thanks to him who alone does mighty miracles. His faithful love endures forever.
136.5: Give thanks to him who made the heavens so skillfully. His faithful love endures forever.
136.6: Give thanks to him who placed the earth among the waters. His faithful love endures forever.
136.7: Give thanks to him who made the heavenly lights— His faithful love endures forever.
136.8: the sun to rule the day, His faithful love endures forever.
136.9: and the moon and stars to rule the night. His faithful love endures forever.
136.10: Give thanks to him who killed the firstborn of Egypt. His faithful love endures forever.
136.11: He brought Israel out of Egypt. His faithful love endures forever.
136.12: He acted with a strong hand and powerful arm. His faithful love endures forever.
136.13: Give thanks to him who parted the Red Sea. His faithful love endures forever.
136.14: He led Israel safely through, His faithful love endures forever.
136.15: but he hurled Pharaoh and his army into the Red Sea. His faithful love endures forever.
136.16: Give thanks to him who led his people through the wilderness. His faithful love endures forever.
136.17: Give thanks to him who struck down mighty kings. His faithful love endures forever.
136.18: He killed powerful kings— His faithful love endures forever.
136.19: Sihon king of the Amorites, His faithful love endures forever.
136.20: and Og king of Bashan. His faithful love endures forever.
136.21: God gave the land of these kings as an inheritance— His faithful love endures forever.
136.22: a special possession to his servant Israel. His faithful love endures forever.
136.23: He remembered us in our weakness. His faithful love endures forever.
136.24: He saved us from our enemies. His faithful love endures forever.
136.25: He gives food to every living thing. His faithful love endures forever.
136.26: Give thanks to the God of heaven. His faithful love endures forever.

81.1: For the choir director: A psalm of Asaph, to be accompanied by a stringed instrument. Sing praises to God, our strength. Sing to the God of Jacob.
81.2: Sing! Beat the tambourine. Play the sweet lyre and the harp.
81.3: Blow the ram’s horn at new moon, and again at full moon to call a festival!
81.4: For this is required by the decrees of Israel; it is a regulation of the God of Jacob.
81.5: He made it a law for Israel when he attacked Egypt to set us free. I heard an unknown voice say,
81.6: “Now I will take the load from your shoulders; I will free your hands from their heavy tasks.
81.7: You cried to me in trouble, and I saved you; I answered out of the thundercloud and tested your faith when there was no water at Meribah. Interlude
81.8: “Listen to me, O my people, while I give you stern warnings. O Israel, if you would only listen to me!
81.9: You must never have a foreign god; you must not bow down before a false god.
81.10: For it was I, the Lord your God, who rescued you from the land of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it with good things.
81.11: “But no, my people wouldn’t listen. Israel did not want me around.
81.12: So I let them follow their own stubborn desires, living according to their own ideas.
81.13: Oh, that my people would listen to me! Oh, that Israel would follow me, walking in my paths!
81.14: How quickly I would then subdue their enemies! How soon my hands would be upon their foes!
81.15: Those who hate the Lord would cringe before him; they would be doomed forever.
81.16: But I would feed you with the finest wheat. I would satisfy you with wild honey from the rock.”

5.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David, to be accompanied by the flute. O Lord, hear me as I pray; pay attention to my groaning.
5.2: Listen to my cry for help, my King and my God, for I pray to no one but you.
5.3: Listen to my voice in the morning, Lord. Each morning I bring my requests to you and wait expectantly.
5.4: O God, you take no pleasure in wickedness; you cannot tolerate the sins of the wicked.
5.5: Therefore, the proud may not stand in your presence, for you hate all who do evil.
5.6: You will destroy those who tell lies. The Lord detests murderers and deceivers.
5.7: Because of your unfailing love, I can enter your house; I will worship at your Temple with deepest awe.
5.8: Lead me in the right path, O Lord, or my enemies will conquer me. Make your way plain for me to follow.
5.9: My enemies cannot speak a truthful word. Their deepest desire is to destroy others. Their talk is foul, like the stench from an open grave. Their tongues are filled with flattery.
5.10: O God, declare them guilty. Let them be caught in their own traps. Drive them away because of their many sins, for they have rebelled against you.
5.11: But let all who take refuge in you rejoice; let them sing joyful praises forever. Spread your protection over them, that all who love your name may be filled with joy.
5.12: For you bless the godly, O Lord; you surround them with your shield of love.

15.1: A psalm of David. Who may worship in your sanctuary, Lord? Who may enter your presence on your holy hill?
15.2: Those who lead blameless lives and do what is right, speaking the truth from sincere hearts.
15.3: Those who refuse to gossip or harm their neighbors or speak evil of their friends.
15.4: Those who despise flagrant sinners, and honor the faithful followers of the Lord, and keep their promises even when it hurts.
15.5: Those who lend money without charging interest, and who cannot be bribed to lie about the innocent. Such people will stand firm forever.

42.1: For the choir director: A psalm of the descendants of Korah. As the deer longs for streams of water, so I long for you, O God.
42.2: I thirst for God, the living God. When can I go and stand before him?
42.3: Day and night I have only tears for food, while my enemies continually taunt me, saying, “Where is this God of yours?”
42.4: My heart is breaking as I remember how it used to be: I walked among the crowds of worshipers, leading a great procession to the house of God, singing for joy and giving thanks amid the sound of a great celebration!
42.5: Why am I discouraged? Why is my heart so sad? I will put my hope in God! I will praise him again— my Savior and
42.6: my God! Now I am deeply discouraged, but I will remember you— even from distant Mount Hermon, the source of the Jordan, from the land of Mount Mizar.
42.7: I hear the tumult of the raging seas as your waves and surging tides sweep over me.
42.8: But each day the Lord pours his unfailing love upon me, and through each night I sing his songs, praying to God who gives me life.
42.9: “O God my rock,” I cry, “why have you forgotten me? Why must I wander around in grief, oppressed by my enemies?”
42.10: Their taunts break my bones. They scoff, “Where is this God of yours?”
42.11: Why am I discouraged? Why is my heart so sad? I will put my hope in God! I will praise him again— my Savior and my God!

54.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David, regarding the time the Ziphites came and said to Saul, “We know where David is hiding.” To be accompanied by stringed instruments. Come with great power, O God, and rescue me! Defend me with your might.
54.2: Listen to my prayer, O God. Pay attention to my plea.
54.3: For strangers are attacking me; violent people are trying to kill me. They care nothing for God. Interlude
54.4: But God is my helper. The Lord keeps me alive!
54.5: May the evil plans of my enemies be turned against them. Do as you promised and put an end to them.
54.6: I will sacrifice a voluntary offering to you; I will praise your name, O Lord, for it is good.
54.7: For you have rescued me from my troubles and helped me to triumph over my enemies.

55.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David, to be accompanied by stringed instruments. Listen to my prayer, O God. Do not ignore my cry for help!
55.2: Please listen and answer me, for I am overwhelmed by my troubles.
55.3: My enemies shout at me, making loud and wicked threats. They bring trouble on me and angrily hunt me down.
55.4: My heart pounds in my chest. The terror of death assaults me.
55.5: Fear and trembling overwhelm me, and I can’t stop shaking.
55.6: Oh, that I had wings like a dove; then I would fly away and rest!
55.7: I would fly far away to the quiet of the wilderness. Interlude
55.8: How quickly I would escape— far from this wild storm of hatred.
55.9: Confuse them, Lord, and frustrate their plans, for I see violence and conflict in the city.
55.10: Its walls are patrolled day and night against invaders, but the real danger is wickedness within the city.
55.11: Everything is falling apart; threats and cheating are rampant in the streets.
55.12: It is not an enemy who taunts me— I could bear that. It is not my foes who so arrogantly insult me— I could have hidden from them.
55.13: Instead, it is you—my equal, my companion and close friend.
55.14: What good fellowship we once enjoyed as we walked together to the house of God.
55.15: Let death stalk my enemies; let the grave swallow them alive, for evil makes its home within them.
55.16: But I will call on God, and the Lord will rescue me.
55.17: Morning, noon, and night I cry out in my distress, and the Lord hears my voice.
55.18: He ransoms me and keeps me safe from the battle waged against me, though many still oppose me.
55.19: God, who has ruled forever, will hear me and humble them. Interlude For my enemies refuse to change their ways; they do not fear God.
55.20: As for my companion, he betrayed his friends; he broke his promises.
55.21: His words are as smooth as butter, but in his heart is war. His words are as soothing as lotion, but underneath are daggers!
55.22: Give your burdens to the Lord, and he will take care of you. He will not permit the godly to slip and fall.
55.23: But you, O God, will send the wicked down to the pit of destruction. Murderers and liars will die young, but I am trusting you to save me.

43.1: Declare me innocent, O God! Defend me against these ungodly people. Rescue me from these unjust liars.
43.2: For you are God, my only safe haven. Why have you tossed me aside? Why must I wander around in grief, oppressed by my enemies?
43.3: Send out your light and your truth; let them guide me. Let them lead me to your holy mountain, to the place where you live.
43.4: There I will go to the altar of God, to God—the source of all my joy. I will praise you with my harp, O God, my God!
43.5: Why am I discouraged? Why is my heart so sad? I will put my hope in God! I will praise him again— my Savior and my God!

14.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David. Only fools say in their hearts, “There is no God.” They are corrupt, and their actions are evil; not one of them does good!
14.2: The Lord looks down from heaven on the entire human race; he looks to see if anyone is truly wise, if anyone seeks God.
14.3: But no, all have turned away; all have become corrupt. No one does good, not a single one!
14.4: Will those who do evil never learn? They eat up my people like bread and wouldn’t think of praying to the Lord.
14.5: Terror will grip them, for God is with those who obey him.
14.6: The wicked frustrate the plans of the oppressed, but the Lord will protect his people.
14.7: Who will come from Mount Zion to rescue Israel? When the Lord restores his people, Jacob will shout with joy, and Israel will rejoice.

137.1: Beside the rivers of Babylon, we sat and wept as we thought of Jerusalem.
137.2: We put away our harps, hanging them on the branches of poplar trees.
137.3: For our captors demanded a song from us. Our tormentors insisted on a joyful hymn: “Sing us one of those songs of Jerusalem!”
137.4: But how can we sing the songs of the Lord while in a pagan land?
137.5: If I forget you, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget how to play the harp.
137.6: May my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth if I fail to remember you, if I don’t make Jerusalem my greatest joy.
137.7: O Lord, remember what the Edomites did on the day the armies of Babylon captured Jerusalem. “Destroy it!” they yelled. “Level it to the ground!”
137.8: O Babylon, you will be destroyed. Happy is the one who pays you back for what you have done to us.
137.9: Happy is the one who takes your babies and smashes them against the rocks!

4.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David, to be accompanied by stringed instruments. Answer me when I call to you, O God who declares me innocent. Free me from my troubles. Have mercy on me and hear my prayer.
4.2: How long will you people ruin my reputation? How long will you make groundless accusations? How long will you continue your lies? Interlude
4.3: You can be sure of this: The Lord set apart the godly for himself. The Lord will answer when I call to him.
4.4: Don’t sin by letting anger control you. Think about it overnight and remain silent. Interlude
4.5: Offer sacrifices in the right spirit, and trust the Lord.
4.6: Many people say, “Who will show us better times?” Let your face smile on us, Lord.
4.7: You have given me greater joy than those who have abundant harvests of grain and new wine.
4.8: In peace I will lie down and sleep, for you alone, O Lord, will keep me safe.

80.1: For the choir director: A psalm of Asaph, to be sung to the tune “Lilies of the Covenant.” Please listen, O Shepherd of Israel, you who lead Joseph’s descendants like a flock. O God, enthroned above the cherubim, display your radiant glory
80.2: to Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh. Show us your mighty power. Come to rescue us!
80.3: Turn us again to yourself, O God. Make your face shine down upon us. Only then will we be saved.
80.4: O Lord God of Heaven’s Armies, how long will you be angry with our prayers?
80.5: You have fed us with sorrow and made us drink tears by the bucketful.
80.6: You have made us the scorn of neighboring nations. Our enemies treat us as a joke.
80.7: Turn us again to yourself, O God of Heaven’s Armies. Make your face shine down upon us. Only then will we be saved.
80.8: You brought us from Egypt like a grapevine; you drove away the pagan nations and transplanted us into your land.
80.9: You cleared the ground for us, and we took root and filled the land.
80.10: Our shade covered the mountains; our branches covered the mighty cedars.
80.11: We spread our branches west to the Mediterranean Sea; our shoots spread east to the Euphrates River.
80.12: But now, why have you broken down our walls so that all who pass by may steal our fruit?
80.13: The wild boar from the forest devours it, and the wild animals feed on it.
80.14: Come back, we beg you, O God of Heaven’s Armies. Look down from heaven and see our plight. Take care of this grapevine
80.15: that you yourself have planted, this son you have raised for yourself.
80.16: For we are chopped up and burned by our enemies. May they perish at the sight of your frown.
80.17: Strengthen the man you love, the son of your choice.
80.18: Then we will never abandon you again. Revive us so we can call on your name once more.
80.19: Turn us again to yourself, O Lord God of Heaven’s Armies. Make your face shine down upon us. Only then will we be saved.

38.1: A psalm of David, asking God to remember him. O Lord, don’t rebuke me in your anger or discipline me in your rage!
38.2: Your arrows have struck deep, and your blows are crushing me.
38.3: Because of your anger, my whole body is sick; my health is broken because of my sins.
38.4: My guilt overwhelms me— it is a burden too heavy to bear.
38.5: My wounds fester and stink because of my foolish sins.
38.6: I am bent over and racked with pain. All day long I walk around filled with grief.
38.7: A raging fever burns within me, and my health is broken.
38.8: I am exhausted and completely crushed. My groans come from an anguished heart.
38.9: You know what I long for, Lord; you hear my every sigh.
38.10: My heart beats wildly, my strength fails, and I am going blind.
38.11: My loved ones and friends stay away, fearing my disease. Even my own family stands at a distance.
38.12: Meanwhile, my enemies lay traps to kill me. Those who wish me harm make plans to ruin me. All day long they plan their treachery.
38.13: But I am deaf to all their threats. I am silent before them as one who cannot speak.
38.14: I choose to hear nothing, and I make no reply.
38.15: For I am waiting for you, O Lord. You must answer for me, O Lord my God.
38.16: I prayed, “Don’t let my enemies gloat over me or rejoice at my downfall.”
38.17: I am on the verge of collapse, facing constant pain.
38.18: But I confess my sins; I am deeply sorry for what I have done.
38.19: I have many aggressive enemies; they hate me without reason.
38.20: They repay me evil for good and oppose me for pursuing good.
38.21: Do not abandon me, O Lord. Do not stand at a distance, my God.
38.22: Come quickly to help me, O Lord my savior.

121.1: A song for pilgrims ascending to Jerusalem. I look up to the mountains— does my help come from there?
121.2: My help comes from the Lord, who made heaven and earth!
121.3: He will not let you stumble; the one who watches over you will not slumber.
121.4: Indeed, he who watches over Israel never slumbers or sleeps.
121.5: The Lord himself watches over you! The Lord stands beside you as your protective shade.
121.6: The sun will not harm you by day, nor the moon at night.
121.7: The Lord keeps you from all harm and watches over your life.
121.8: The Lord keeps watch over you as you come and go, both now and forever.

79.1: A psalm of Asaph. O God, pagan nations have conquered your land, your special possession. They have defiled your holy Temple and made Jerusalem a heap of ruins.
79.2: They have left the bodies of your servants as food for the birds of heaven. The flesh of your godly ones has become food for the wild animals.
79.3: Blood has flowed like water all around Jerusalem; no one is left to bury the dead.
79.4: We are mocked by our neighbors, an object of scorn and derision to those around us.
79.5: O Lord, how long will you be angry with us? Forever? How long will your jealousy burn like fire?
79.6: Pour out your wrath on the nations that refuse to acknowledge you— on kingdoms that do not call upon your name.
79.7: For they have devoured your people Israel, making the land a desolate wilderness.
79.8: Do not hold us guilty for the sins of our ancestors! Let your compassion quickly meet our needs, for we are on the brink of despair.
79.9: Help us, O God of our salvation! Help us for the glory of your name. Save us and forgive our sins for the honor of your name.
79.10: Why should pagan nations be allowed to scoff, asking, “Where is their God?” Show us your vengeance against the nations, for they have spilled the blood of your servants.
79.11: Listen to the moaning of the prisoners. Demonstrate your great power by saving those condemned to die.
79.12: O Lord, pay back our neighbors seven times for the scorn they have hurled at you.
79.13: Then we your people, the sheep of your pasture, will thank you forever and ever, praising your greatness from generation to generation.

96.1: Sing a new song to the Lord! Let the whole earth sing to the Lord!
96.2: Sing to the Lord; praise his name. Each day proclaim the good news that he saves.
96.3: Publish his glorious deeds among the nations. Tell everyone about the amazing things he does.
96.4: Great is the Lord! He is most worthy of praise! He is to be feared above all gods.
96.5: The gods of other nations are mere idols, but the Lord made the heavens!
96.6: Honor and majesty surround him; strength and beauty fill his sanctuary.
96.7: O nations of the world, recognize the Lord; recognize that the Lord is glorious and strong.
96.8: Give to the Lord the glory he deserves! Bring your offering and come into his courts.
96.9: Worship the Lord in all his holy splendor. Let all the earth tremble before him.
96.10: Tell all the nations, “The Lord reigns!” The world stands firm and cannot be shaken. He will judge all peoples fairly.
96.11: Let the heavens be glad, and the earth rejoice! Let the sea and everything in it shout his praise!
96.12: Let the fields and their crops burst out with joy! Let the trees of the forest sing for joy
96.13: before the Lord, for he is coming! He is coming to judge the earth. He will judge the world with justice, and the nations with his truth.

101.1: A psalm of David. I will sing of your love and justice, Lord. I will praise you with songs.
101.2: I will be careful to live a blameless life— when will you come to help me? I will lead a life of integrity in my own home.
101.3: I will refuse to look at anything vile and vulgar. I hate all who deal crookedly; I will have nothing to do with them.
101.4: I will reject perverse ideas and stay away from every evil.
101.5: I will not tolerate people who slander their neighbors. I will not endure conceit and pride.
101.6: I will search for faithful people to be my companions. Only those who are above reproach will be allowed to serve me.
101.7: I will not allow deceivers to serve in my house, and liars will not stay in my presence.
101.8: My daily task will be to ferret out the wicked and free the city of the Lord from their grip.

59.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David, regarding the time Saul sent soldiers to watch David’s house in order to kill him. To be sung to the tune “Do Not Destroy!” Rescue me from my enemies, O God. Protect me from those who have come to destroy me.
59.2: Rescue me from these criminals; save me from these murderers.
59.3: They have set an ambush for me. Fierce enemies are out there waiting, Lord, though I have not sinned or offended them.
59.4: I have done nothing wrong, yet they prepare to attack me. Wake up! See what is happening and help me!
59.5: O Lord God of Heaven’s Armies, the God of Israel, wake up and punish those hostile nations. Show no mercy to wicked traitors. Interlude
59.6: They come out at night, snarling like vicious dogs as they prowl the streets.
59.7: Listen to the filth that comes from their mouths; their words cut like swords. “After all, who can hear us?” they sneer.
59.8: But Lord, you laugh at them. You scoff at all the hostile nations.
59.9: You are my strength; I wait for you to rescue me, for you, O God, are my fortress.
59.10: In his unfailing love, my God will stand with me. He will let me look down in triumph on all my enemies.
59.11: Don’t kill them, for my people soon forget such lessons; stagger them with your power, and bring them to their knees, O Lord our shield.
59.12: Because of the sinful things they say, because of the evil that is on their lips, let them be captured by their pride, their curses, and their lies.
59.13: Destroy them in your anger! Wipe them out completely! Then the whole world will know that God reigns in Israel. Interlude
59.14: My enemies come out at night, snarling like vicious dogs as they prowl the streets.
59.15: They scavenge for food but go to sleep unsatisfied.
59.16: But as for me, I will sing about your power. Each morning I will sing with joy about your unfailing love. For you have been my refuge, a place of safety when I am in distress.
59.17: O my Strength, to you I sing praises, for you, O God, are my refuge, the God who shows me unfailing love.

117.1: Praise the Lord, all you nations. Praise him, all you people of the earth.
117.2: For his unfailing love for us is powerful; the Lord’s faithfulness endures forever. Praise the Lord!

140.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David. O Lord, rescue me from evil people. Protect me from those who are violent,
140.2: those who plot evil in their hearts and stir up trouble all day long.
140.3: Their tongues sting like a snake; the venom of a viper drips from their lips. Interlude
140.4: O Lord, keep me out of the hands of the wicked. Protect me from those who are violent, for they are plotting against me.
140.5: The proud have set a trap to catch me; they have stretched out a net; they have placed traps all along the way. Interlude
140.6: I said to the Lord, “You are my God!” Listen, O Lord, to my cries for mercy!
140.7: O Sovereign Lord, the strong one who rescued me, you protected me on the day of battle.
140.8: Lord, do not let evil people have their way. Do not let their evil schemes succeed, or they will become proud. Interlude
140.9: Let my enemies be destroyed by the very evil they have planned for me.
140.10: Let burning coals fall down on their heads. Let them be thrown into the fire or into watery pits from which they can’t escape.
140.11: Don’t let liars prosper here in our land. Cause great disasters to fall on the violent.
140.12: But I know the Lord will help those they persecute; he will give justice to the poor.
140.13: Surely righteous people are praising your name; the godly will live in your presence.

18.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David, the servant of the Lord. He sang this song to the Lord on the day the Lord rescued him from all his enemies and from Saul. He sang: I love you, Lord; you are my strength.
18.2: The Lord is my rock, my fortress, and my savior; my God is my rock, in whom I find protection. He is my shield, the power that saves me, and my place of safety.
18.3: I called on the Lord, who is worthy of praise, and he saved me from my enemies.
18.4: The ropes of death entangled me; floods of destruction swept over me.
18.5: The grave wrapped its ropes around me; death laid a trap in my path.
18.6: But in my distress I cried out to the Lord; yes, I prayed to my God for help. He heard me from his sanctuary; my cry to him reached his ears.
18.7: Then the earth quaked and trembled. The foundations of the mountains shook; they quaked because of his anger.
18.8: Smoke poured from his nostrils; fierce flames leaped from his mouth. Glowing coals blazed forth from him.
18.9: He opened the heavens and came down; dark storm clouds were beneath his feet.
18.10: Mounted on a mighty angelic being, he flew, soaring on the wings of the wind.
18.11: He shrouded himself in darkness, veiling his approach with dark rain clouds.
18.12: Thick clouds shielded the brightness around him and rained down hail and burning coals.
18.13: The Lord thundered from heaven; the voice of the Most High resounded amid the hail and burning coals.
18.14: He shot his arrows and scattered his enemies; great bolts of lightning flashed, and they were confused.
18.15: Then at your command, O Lord, at the blast of your breath, the bottom of the sea could be seen, and the foundations of the earth were laid bare.
18.16: He reached down from heaven and rescued me; he drew me out of deep waters.
18.17: He rescued me from my powerful enemies, from those who hated me and were too strong for me.
18.18: They attacked me at a moment when I was in distress, but the Lord supported me.
18.19: He led me to a place of safety; he rescued me because he delights in me.
18.20: The Lord rewarded me for doing right; he restored me because of my innocence.
18.21: For I have kept the ways of the Lord; I have not turned from my God to follow evil.
18.22: I have followed all his regulations; I have never abandoned his decrees.
18.23: I am blameless before God; I have kept myself from sin.
18.24: The Lord rewarded me for doing right. He has seen my innocence.
18.25: To the faithful you show yourself faithful; to those with integrity you show integrity.
18.26: To the pure you show yourself pure, but to the crooked you show yourself shrewd.
18.27: You rescue the humble, but you humiliate the proud.
18.28: You light a lamp for me. The Lord, my God, lights up my darkness.
18.29: In your strength I can crush an army; with my God I can scale any wall.
18.30: God’s way is perfect. All the Lord’s promises prove true. He is a shield for all who look to him for protection.
18.31: For who is God except the Lord? Who but our God is a solid rock?
18.32: God arms me with strength, and he makes my way perfect.
18.33: He makes me as surefooted as a deer, enabling me to stand on mountain heights.
18.34: He trains my hands for battle; he strengthens my arm to draw a bronze bow.
18.35: You have given me your shield of victory. Your right hand supports me; your help has made me great.
18.36: You have made a wide path for my feet to keep them from slipping.
18.37: I chased my enemies and caught them; I did not stop until they were conquered.
18.38: I struck them down so they could not get up; they fell beneath my feet.
18.39: You have armed me with strength for the battle; you have subdued my enemies under my feet.
18.40: You placed my foot on their necks. I have destroyed all who hated me.
18.41: They called for help, but no one came to their rescue. They even cried to the Lord, but he refused to answer.
18.42: I ground them as fine as dust in the wind. I swept them into the gutter like dirt.
18.43: You gave me victory over my accusers. You appointed me ruler over nations; people I don’t even know now serve me.
18.44: As soon as they hear of me, they submit; foreign nations cringe before me.
18.45: They all lose their courage and come trembling from their strongholds.
18.46: The Lord lives! Praise to my Rock! May the God of my salvation be exalted!
18.47: He is the God who pays back those who harm me; he subdues the nations under me
18.48: and rescues me from my enemies. You hold me safe beyond the reach of my enemies; you save me from violent opponents.
18.49: For this, O Lord, I will praise you among the nations; I will sing praises to your name.
18.50: You give great victories to your king; you show unfailing love to your anointed, to David and all his descendants forever.

63.1: A psalm of David, regarding a time when David was in the wilderness of Judah. O God, you are my God; I earnestly search for you. My soul thirsts for you; my whole body longs for you in this parched and weary land where there is no water.
63.2: I have seen you in your sanctuary and gazed upon your power and glory.
63.3: Your unfailing love is better than life itself; how I praise you!
63.4: I will praise you as long as I live, lifting up my hands to you in prayer.
63.5: You satisfy me more than the richest feast. I will praise you with songs of joy.
63.6: I lie awake thinking of you, meditating on you through the night.
63.7: Because you are my helper, I sing for joy in the shadow of your wings.
63.8: I cling to you; your strong right hand holds me securely.
63.9: But those plotting to destroy me will come to ruin. They will go down into the depths of the earth.
63.10: They will die by the sword and become the food of jackals.
63.11: But the king will rejoice in God. All who swear to tell the truth will praise him, while liars will be silenced.

8.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David, to be accompanied by a stringed instrument. O Lord, our Lord, your majestic name fills the earth! Your glory is higher than the heavens.
8.2: You have taught children and infants to tell of your strength, silencing your enemies and all who oppose you.
8.3: When I look at the night sky and see the work of your fingers— the moon and the stars you set in place—
8.4: what are mere mortals that you should think about them, human beings that you should care for them?
8.5: Yet you made them only a little lower than God and crowned them with glory and honor.
8.6: You gave them charge of everything you made, putting all things under their authority—
8.7: the flocks and the herds and all the wild animals,
8.8: the birds in the sky, the fish in the sea, and everything that swims the ocean currents.
8.9: O Lord, our Lord, your majestic name fills the earth!

34.1: A psalm of David, regarding the time he pretended to be insane in front of Abimelech, who sent him away. I will praise the Lord at all times. I will constantly speak his praises.
34.2: I will boast only in the Lord; let all who are helpless take heart.
34.3: Come, let us tell of the Lord’s greatness; let us exalt his name together.
34.4: I prayed to the Lord, and he answered me. He freed me from all my fears.
34.5: Those who look to him for help will be radiant with joy; no shadow of shame will darken their faces.
34.6: In my desperation I prayed, and the Lord listened; he saved me from all my troubles.
34.7: For the angel of the Lord is a guard; he surrounds and defends all who fear him.
34.8: Taste and see that the Lord is good. Oh, the joys of those who take refuge in him!
34.9: Fear the Lord, you his godly people, for those who fear him will have all they need.
34.10: Even strong young lions sometimes go hungry, but those who trust in the Lord will lack no good thing.
34.11: Come, my children, and listen to me, and I will teach you to fear the Lord.
34.12: Does anyone want to live a life that is long and prosperous?
34.13: Then keep your tongue from speaking evil and your lips from telling lies!
34.14: Turn away from evil and do good. Search for peace, and work to maintain it.
34.15: The eyes of the Lord watch over those who do right; his ears are open to their cries for help.
34.16: But the Lord turns his face against those who do evil; he will erase their memory from the earth.
34.17: The Lord hears his people when they call to him for help. He rescues them from all their troubles.
34.18: The Lord is close to the brokenhearted; he rescues those whose spirits are crushed.
34.19: The righteous person faces many troubles, but the Lord comes to the rescue each time.
34.20: For the Lord protects the bones of the righteous; not one of them is broken!
34.21: Calamity will surely destroy the wicked, and those who hate the righteous will be punished.
34.22: But the Lord will redeem those who serve him. No one who takes refuge in him will be condemned.

22.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David, to be sung to the tune “Doe of the Dawn.” My God, my God, why have you abandoned me? Why are you so far away when I groan for help?
22.2: Every day I call to you, my God, but you do not answer. Every night I lift my voice, but I find no relief.
22.3: Yet you are holy, enthroned on the praises of Israel.
22.4: Our ancestors trusted in you, and you rescued them.
22.5: They cried out to you and were saved. They trusted in you and were never disgraced.
22.6: But I am a worm and not a man. I am scorned and despised by all!
22.7: Everyone who sees me mocks me. They sneer and shake their heads, saying,
22.8: “Is this the one who relies on the Lord? Then let the Lord save him! If the Lord loves him so much, let the Lord rescue him!”
22.9: Yet you brought me safely from my mother’s womb and led me to trust you at my mother’s breast.
22.10: I was thrust into your arms at my birth. You have been my God from the moment I was born.
22.11: Do not stay so far from me, for trouble is near, and no one else can help me.
22.12: My enemies surround me like a herd of bulls; fierce bulls of Bashan have hemmed me in!
22.13: Like lions they open their jaws against me, roaring and tearing into their prey.
22.14: My life is poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint. My heart is like wax, melting within me.
22.15: My strength has dried up like sunbaked clay. My tongue sticks to the roof of my mouth. You have laid me in the dust and left me for dead.
22.16: My enemies surround me like a pack of dogs; an evil gang closes in on me. They have pierced my hands and feet.
22.17: I can count all my bones. My enemies stare at me and gloat.
22.18: They divide my garments among themselves and throw dice for my clothing.
22.19: O Lord, do not stay far away! You are my strength; come quickly to my aid!
22.20: Save me from the sword; spare my precious life from these dogs.
22.21: Snatch me from the lion’s jaws and from the horns of these wild oxen.
22.22: I will proclaim your name to my brothers and sisters. I will praise you among your assembled people.
22.23: Praise the Lord, all you who fear him! Honor him, all you descendants of Jacob! Show him reverence, all you descendants of Israel!
22.24: For he has not ignored or belittled the suffering of the needy. He has not turned his back on them, but has listened to their cries for help.
22.25: I will praise you in the great assembly. I will fulfill my vows in the presence of those who worship you.
22.26: The poor will eat and be satisfied. All who seek the Lord will praise him. Their hearts will rejoice with everlasting joy.
22.27: The whole earth will acknowledge the Lord and return to him. All the families of the nations will bow down before him.
22.28: For royal power belongs to the Lord. He rules all the nations.
22.29: Let the rich of the earth feast and worship. Bow before him, all who are mortal, all whose lives will end as dust.
22.30: Our children will also serve him. Future generations will hear about the wonders of the Lord.
22.31: His righteous acts will be told to those not yet born. They will hear about everything he has done.

75.1: For the choir director: A psalm of Asaph. A song to be sung to the tune “Do Not Destroy!” We thank you, O God! We give thanks because you are near. People everywhere tell of your wonderful deeds.
75.2: God says, “At the time I have planned, I will bring justice against the wicked.
75.3: When the earth quakes and its people live in turmoil, I am the one who keeps its foundations firm. Interlude
75.4: “I warned the proud, ‘Stop your boasting!’ I told the wicked, ‘Don’t raise your fists!
75.5: Don’t raise your fists in defiance at the heavens or speak with such arrogance.’”
75.6: For no one on earth—from east or west, or even from the wilderness— should raise a defiant fist.
75.7: It is God alone who judges; he decides who will rise and who will fall.
75.8: For the Lord holds a cup in his hand that is full of foaming wine mixed with spices. He pours out the wine in judgment, and all the wicked must drink it, draining it to the dregs.
75.9: But as for me, I will always proclaim what God has done; I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.
75.10: For God says, “I will break the strength of the wicked, but I will increase the power of the godly.”

126.1: A song for pilgrims ascending to Jerusalem. When the Lord brought back his exiles to Jerusalem, it was like a dream!
126.2: We were filled with laughter, and we sang for joy. And the other nations said, “What amazing things the Lord has done for them.”
126.3: Yes, the Lord has done amazing things for us! What joy!
126.4: Restore our fortunes, Lord, as streams renew the desert.
126.5: Those who plant in tears will harvest with shouts of joy.
126.6: They weep as they go to plant their seed, but they sing as they return with the harvest.

91.1: Those who live in the shelter of the Most High will find rest in the shadow of the Almighty.
91.2: This I declare about the Lord: He alone is my refuge, my place of safety; he is my God, and I trust him.
91.3: For he will rescue you from every trap and protect you from deadly disease.
91.4: He will cover you with his feathers. He will shelter you with his wings. His faithful promises are your armor and protection.
91.5: Do not be afraid of the terrors of the night, nor the arrow that flies in the day.
91.6: Do not dread the disease that stalks in darkness, nor the disaster that strikes at midday.
91.7: Though a thousand fall at your side, though ten thousand are dying around you, these evils will not touch you.
91.8: Just open your eyes, and see how the wicked are punished.
91.9: If you make the Lord your refuge, if you make the Most High your shelter,
91.10: no evil will conquer you; no plague will come near your home.
91.11: For he will order his angels to protect you wherever you go.
91.12: They will hold you up with their hands so you won’t even hurt your foot on a stone.
91.13: You will trample upon lions and cobras; you will crush fierce lions and serpents under your feet!
91.14: The Lord says, “I will rescue those who love me. I will protect those who trust in my name.
91.15: When they call on me, I will answer; I will be with them in trouble. I will rescue and honor them.
91.16: I will reward them with a long life and give them my salvation.”

29.1: A psalm of David. Honor the Lord, you heavenly beings; honor the Lord for his glory and strength.
29.2: Honor the Lord for the glory of his name. Worship the Lord in the splendor of his holiness.
29.3: The voice of the Lord echoes above the sea. The God of glory thunders. The Lord thunders over the mighty sea.
29.4: The voice of the Lord is powerful; the voice of the Lord is majestic.
29.5: The voice of the Lord splits the mighty cedars; the Lord shatters the cedars of Lebanon.
29.6: He makes Lebanon’s mountains skip like a calf; he makes Mount Hermon leap like a young wild ox.
29.7: The voice of the Lord strikes with bolts of lightning.
29.8: The voice of the Lord makes the barren wilderness quake; the Lord shakes the wilderness of Kadesh.
29.9: The voice of the Lord twists mighty oaks and strips the forests bare. In his Temple everyone shouts, “Glory!”
29.10: The Lord rules over the floodwaters. The Lord reigns as king forever.
29.11: The Lord gives his people strength. The Lord blesses them with peace.

130.1: A song for pilgrims ascending to Jerusalem. From the depths of despair, O Lord, I call for your help.
130.2: Hear my cry, O Lord. Pay attention to my prayer.
130.3: Lord, if you kept a record of our sins, who, O Lord, could ever survive?
130.4: But you offer forgiveness, that we might learn to fear you.
130.5: I am counting on the Lord; yes, I am counting on him. I have put my hope in his word.
130.6: I long for the Lord more than sentries long for the dawn, yes, more than sentries long for the dawn.
130.7: O Israel, hope in the Lord; for with the Lord there is unfailing love. His redemption overflows.
130.8: He himself will redeem Israel from every kind of sin.

68.1: For the choir director: A song. A psalm of David. Rise up, O God, and scatter your enemies. Let those who hate God run for their lives.
68.2: Blow them away like smoke. Melt them like wax in a fire. Let the wicked perish in the presence of God.
68.3: But let the godly rejoice. Let them be glad in God’s presence. Let them be filled with joy.
68.4: Sing praises to God and to his name! Sing loud praises to him who rides the clouds. His name is the Lord— rejoice in his presence!
68.5: Father to the fatherless, defender of widows— this is God, whose dwelling is holy.
68.6: God places the lonely in families; he sets the prisoners free and gives them joy. But he makes the rebellious live in a sun-scorched land.
68.7: O God, when you led your people out from Egypt, when you marched through the dry wasteland, Interlude
68.8: the earth trembled, and the heavens poured down rain before you, the God of Sinai, before God, the God of Israel.
68.9: You sent abundant rain, O God, to refresh the weary land.
68.10: There your people finally settled, and with a bountiful harvest, O God, you provided for your needy people.
68.11: The Lord gives the word, and a great army brings the good news.
68.12: Enemy kings and their armies flee, while the women of Israel divide the plunder.
68.13: Even those who lived among the sheepfolds found treasures— doves with wings of silver and feathers of gold.
68.14: The Almighty scattered the enemy kings like a blowing snowstorm on Mount Zalmon.
68.15: The mountains of Bashan are majestic, with many peaks stretching high into the sky.
68.16: Why do you look with envy, O rugged mountains, at Mount Zion, where God has chosen to live, where the Lord himself will live forever?
68.17: Surrounded by unnumbered thousands of chariots, the Lord came from Mount Sinai into his sanctuary.
68.18: When you ascended to the heights, you led a crowd of captives. You received gifts from the people, even from those who rebelled against you. Now the Lord God will live among us there.
68.19: Praise the Lord; praise God our savior! For each day he carries us in his arms. Interlude
68.20: Our God is a God who saves! The Sovereign Lord rescues us from death.
68.21: But God will smash the heads of his enemies, crushing the skulls of those who love their guilty ways.
68.22: The Lord says, “I will bring my enemies down from Bashan; I will bring them up from the depths of the sea.
68.23: You, my people, will wash your feet in their blood, and even your dogs will get their share!”
68.24: Your procession has come into view, O God— the procession of my God and King as he goes into the sanctuary.
68.25: Singers are in front, musicians behind; between them are young women playing tambourines.
68.26: Praise God, all you people of Israel; praise the Lord, the source of Israel’s life.
68.27: Look, the little tribe of Benjamin leads the way. Then comes a great throng of rulers from Judah and all the rulers of Zebulun and Naphtali.
68.28: Summon your might, O God. Display your power, O God, as you have in the past.
68.29: The kings of the earth are bringing tribute to your Temple in Jerusalem.
68.30: Rebuke these enemy nations— these wild animals lurking in the reeds, this herd of bulls among the weaker calves. Make them bring bars of silver in humble tribute. Scatter the nations that delight in war.
68.31: Let Egypt come with gifts of precious metals; let Ethiopia bring tribute to God.
68.32: Sing to God, you kingdoms of the earth. Sing praises to the Lord. Interlude
68.33: Sing to the one who rides across the ancient heavens, his mighty voice thundering from the sky.
68.34: Tell everyone about God’s power. His majesty shines down on Israel; his strength is mighty in the heavens.
68.35: God is awesome in his sanctuary. The God of Israel gives power and strength to his people. Praise be to God!

87.1: A song. A psalm of the descendants of Korah. On the holy mountain stands the city founded by the Lord.
87.2: He loves the city of Jerusalem more than any other city in Israel.
87.3: O city of God, what glorious things are said of you! Interlude
87.4: I will count Egypt and Babylon among those who know me— also Philistia and Tyre, and even distant Ethiopia. They have all become citizens of Jerusalem!
87.5: Regarding Jerusalem it will be said, “Everyone enjoys the rights of citizenship there.” And the Most High will personally bless this city.
87.6: When the Lord registers the nations, he will say, “They have all become citizens of Jerusalem.” Interlude
87.7: The people will play flutes and sing, “The source of my life springs from Jerusalem!”

3.1: A psalm of David, regarding the time David fled from his son Absalom. O Lord, I have so many enemies; so many are against me.
3.2: So many are saying, “God will never rescue him!” Interlude
3.3: But you, O Lord, are a shield around me; you are my glory, the one who holds my head high.
3.4: I cried out to the Lord, and he answered me from his holy mountain. Interlude
3.5: I lay down and slept, yet I woke up in safety, for the Lord was watching over me.
3.6: I am not afraid of ten thousand enemies who surround me on every side.
3.7: Arise, O Lord! Rescue me, my God! Slap all my enemies in the face! Shatter the teeth of the wicked!
3.8: Victory comes from you, O Lord. May you bless your people. Interlude

13.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David. O Lord, how long will you forget me? Forever? How long will you look the other way?
13.2: How long must I struggle with anguish in my soul, with sorrow in my heart every day? How long will my enemy have the upper hand?
13.3: Turn and answer me, O Lord my God! Restore the sparkle to my eyes, or I will die.
13.4: Don’t let my enemies gloat, saying, “We have defeated him!” Don’t let them rejoice at my downfall.
13.5: But I trust in your unfailing love. I will rejoice because you have rescued me.
13.6: I will sing to the Lord because he is good to me.

44.1: For the choir director: A psalm of the descendants of Korah. O God, we have heard it with our own ears— our ancestors have told us of all you did in their day, in days long ago:
44.2: You drove out the pagan nations by your power and gave all the land to our ancestors. You crushed their enemies and set our ancestors free.
44.3: They did not conquer the land with their swords; it was not their own strong arm that gave them victory. It was your right hand and strong arm and the blinding light from your face that helped them, for you loved them.
44.4: You are my King and my God. You command victories for Israel.
44.5: Only by your power can we push back our enemies; only in your name can we trample our foes.
44.6: I do not trust in my bow; I do not count on my sword to save me.
44.7: You are the one who gives us victory over our enemies; you disgrace those who hate us.
44.8: O God, we give glory to you all day long and constantly praise your name. Interlude
44.9: But now you have tossed us aside in dishonor. You no longer lead our armies to battle.
44.10: You make us retreat from our enemies and allow those who hate us to plunder our land.
44.11: You have butchered us like sheep and scattered us among the nations.
44.12: You sold your precious people for a pittance, making nothing on the sale.
44.13: You let our neighbors mock us. We are an object of scorn and derision to those around us.
44.14: You have made us the butt of their jokes; they shake their heads at us in scorn.
44.15: We can’t escape the constant humiliation; shame is written across our faces.
44.16: All we hear are the taunts of our mockers. All we see are our vengeful enemies.
44.17: All this has happened though we have not forgotten you. We have not violated your covenant.
44.18: Our hearts have not deserted you. We have not strayed from your path.
44.19: Yet you have crushed us in the jackal’s desert home. You have covered us with darkness and death.
44.20: If we had forgotten the name of our God or spread our hands in prayer to foreign gods,
44.21: God would surely have known it, for he knows the secrets of every heart.
44.22: But for your sake we are killed every day; we are being slaughtered like sheep.
44.23: Wake up, O Lord! Why do you sleep? Get up! Do not reject us forever.
44.24: Why do you look the other way? Why do you ignore our suffering and oppression?
44.25: We collapse in the dust, lying face down in the dirt.
44.26: Rise up! Help us! Ransom us because of your unfailing love.
