52.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David, regarding the time Doeg the Edomite said to Saul, “David has gone to see Ahimelech.” Why do you boast about your crimes, great warrior? Don’t you realize God’s justice continues forever?
52.2: All day long you plot destruction. Your tongue cuts like a sharp razor; you’re an expert at telling lies.
52.3: You love evil more than good and lies more than truth. Interlude
52.4: You love to destroy others with your words, you liar!
52.5: But God will strike you down once and for all. He will pull you from your home and uproot you from the land of the living. Interlude
52.6: The righteous will see it and be amazed. They will laugh and say,
52.7: “Look what happens to mighty warriors who do not trust in God. They trust their wealth instead and grow more and more bold in their wickedness.”
52.8: But I am like an olive tree, thriving in the house of God. I will always trust in God’s unfailing love.
52.9: I will praise you forever, O God, for what you have done. I will trust in your good name in the presence of your faithful people.

72.1: A psalm of Solomon. Give your love of justice to the king, O God, and righteousness to the king’s son.
72.2: Help him judge your people in the right way; let the poor always be treated fairly.
72.3: May the mountains yield prosperity for all, and may the hills be fruitful.
72.4: Help him to defend the poor, to rescue the children of the needy, and to crush their oppressors.
72.5: May they fear you as long as the sun shines, as long as the moon remains in the sky. Yes, forever!
72.6: May the king’s rule be refreshing like spring rain on freshly cut grass, like the showers that water the earth.
72.7: May all the godly flourish during his reign. May there be abundant prosperity until the moon is no more.
72.8: May he reign from sea to sea, and from the Euphrates River to the ends of the earth.
72.9: Desert nomads will bow before him; his enemies will fall before him in the dust.
72.10: The western kings of Tarshish and other distant lands will bring him tribute. The eastern kings of Sheba and Seba will bring him gifts.
72.11: All kings will bow before him, and all nations will serve him.
72.12: He will rescue the poor when they cry to him; he will help the oppressed, who have no one to defend them.
72.13: He feels pity for the weak and the needy, and he will rescue them.
72.14: He will redeem them from oppression and violence, for their lives are precious to him.
72.15: Long live the king! May the gold of Sheba be given to him. May the people always pray for him and bless him all day long.
72.16: May there be abundant grain throughout the land, flourishing even on the hilltops. May the fruit trees flourish like the trees of Lebanon, and may the people thrive like grass in a field.
72.17: May the king’s name endure forever; may it continue as long as the sun shines. May all nations be blessed through him and bring him praise.
72.18: Praise the Lord God, the God of Israel, who alone does such wonderful things.
72.19: Praise his glorious name forever! Let the whole earth be filled with his glory. Amen and amen!
72.20: (This ends the prayers of David son of Jesse.)

25.1: A psalm of David. O Lord, I give my life to you.
25.2: I trust in you, my God! Do not let me be disgraced, or let my enemies rejoice in my defeat.
25.3: No one who trusts in you will ever be disgraced, but disgrace comes to those who try to deceive others.
25.4: Show me the right path, O Lord; point out the road for me to follow.
25.5: Lead me by your truth and teach me, for you are the God who saves me. All day long I put my hope in you.
25.6: Remember, O Lord, your compassion and unfailing love, which you have shown from long ages past.
25.7: Do not remember the rebellious sins of my youth. Remember me in the light of your unfailing love, for you are merciful, O Lord.
25.8: The Lord is good and does what is right; he shows the proper path to those who go astray.
25.9: He leads the humble in doing right, teaching them his way.
25.10: The Lord leads with unfailing love and faithfulness all who keep his covenant and obey his demands.
25.11: For the honor of your name, O Lord, forgive my many, many sins.
25.12: Who are those who fear the Lord? He will show them the path they should choose.
25.13: They will live in prosperity, and their children will inherit the land.
25.14: The Lord is a friend to those who fear him. He teaches them his covenant.
25.15: My eyes are always on the Lord, for he rescues me from the traps of my enemies.
25.16: Turn to me and have mercy, for I am alone and in deep distress.
25.17: My problems go from bad to worse. Oh, save me from them all!
25.18: Feel my pain and see my trouble. Forgive all my sins.
25.19: See how many enemies I have and how viciously they hate me!
25.20: Protect me! Rescue my life from them! Do not let me be disgraced, for in you I take refuge.
25.21: May integrity and honesty protect me, for I put my hope in you.
25.22: O God, ransom Israel from all its troubles.

33.1: Let the godly sing for joy to the Lord; it is fitting for the pure to praise him.
33.2: Praise the Lord with melodies on the lyre; make music for him on the ten-stringed harp.
33.3: Sing a new song of praise to him; play skillfully on the harp, and sing with joy.
33.4: For the word of the Lord holds true, and we can trust everything he does.
33.5: He loves whatever is just and good; the unfailing love of the Lord fills the earth.
33.6: The Lord merely spoke, and the heavens were created. He breathed the word, and all the stars were born.
33.7: He assigned the sea its boundaries and locked the oceans in vast reservoirs.
33.8: Let the whole world fear the Lord, and let everyone stand in awe of him.
33.9: For when he spoke, the world began! It appeared at his command.
33.10: The Lord frustrates the plans of the nations and thwarts all their schemes.
33.11: But the Lord’s plans stand firm forever; his intentions can never be shaken.
33.12: What joy for the nation whose God is the Lord, whose people he has chosen as his inheritance.
33.13: The Lord looks down from heaven and sees the whole human race.
33.14: From his throne he observes all who live on the earth.
33.15: He made their hearts, so he understands everything they do.
33.16: The best-equipped army cannot save a king, nor is great strength enough to save a warrior.
33.17: Don’t count on your warhorse to give you victory— for all its strength, it cannot save you.
33.18: But the Lord watches over those who fear him, those who rely on his unfailing love.
33.19: He rescues them from death and keeps them alive in times of famine.
33.20: We put our hope in the Lord. He is our help and our shield.
33.21: In him our hearts rejoice, for we trust in his holy name.
33.22: Let your unfailing love surround us, Lord, for our hope is in you alone.

64.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David. O God, listen to my complaint. Protect my life from my enemies’ threats.
64.2: Hide me from the plots of this evil mob, from this gang of wrongdoers.
64.3: They sharpen their tongues like swords and aim their bitter words like arrows.
64.4: They shoot from ambush at the innocent, attacking suddenly and fearlessly.
64.5: They encourage each other to do evil and plan how to set their traps in secret. “Who will ever notice?” they ask.
64.6: As they plot their crimes, they say, “We have devised the perfect plan!” Yes, the human heart and mind are cunning.
64.7: But God himself will shoot them with his arrows, suddenly striking them down.
64.8: Their own tongues will ruin them, and all who see them will shake their heads in scorn.
64.9: Then everyone will be afraid; they will proclaim the mighty acts of God and realize all the amazing things he does.
64.10: The godly will rejoice in the Lord and find shelter in him. And those who do what is right will praise him.

147.1: Praise the Lord! How good to sing praises to our God! How delightful and how fitting!
147.2: The Lord is rebuilding Jerusalem and bringing the exiles back to Israel.
147.3: He heals the brokenhearted and bandages their wounds.
147.4: He counts the stars and calls them all by name.
147.5: How great is our Lord! His power is absolute! His understanding is beyond comprehension!
147.6: The Lord supports the humble, but he brings the wicked down into the dust.
147.7: Sing out your thanks to the Lord; sing praises to our God with a harp.
147.8: He covers the heavens with clouds, provides rain for the earth, and makes the grass grow in mountain pastures.
147.9: He gives food to the wild animals and feeds the young ravens when they cry.
147.10: He takes no pleasure in the strength of a horse or in human might.
147.11: No, the Lord’s delight is in those who fear him, those who put their hope in his unfailing love.
147.12: Glorify the Lord, O Jerusalem! Praise your God, O Zion!
147.13: For he has strengthened the bars of your gates and blessed your children within your walls.
147.14: He sends peace across your nation and satisfies your hunger with the finest wheat.
147.15: He sends his orders to the world— how swiftly his word flies!
147.16: He sends the snow like white wool; he scatters frost upon the ground like ashes.
147.17: He hurls the hail like stones. Who can stand against his freezing cold?
147.18: Then, at his command, it all melts. He sends his winds, and the ice thaws.
147.19: He has revealed his words to Jacob, his decrees and regulations to Israel.
147.20: He has not done this for any other nation; they do not know his regulations. Praise the Lord!

110.1: A psalm of David. The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit in the place of honor at my right hand until I humble your enemies, making them a footstool under your feet.”
110.2: The Lord will extend your powerful kingdom from Jerusalem; you will rule over your enemies.
110.3: When you go to war, your people will serve you willingly. You are arrayed in holy garments, and your strength will be renewed each day like the morning dew.
110.4: The Lord has taken an oath and will not break his vow: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”
110.5: The Lord stands at your right hand to protect you. He will strike down many kings when his anger erupts.
110.6: He will punish the nations and fill their lands with corpses; he will shatter heads over the whole earth.
110.7: But he himself will be refreshed from brooks along the way. He will be victorious.

48.1: A song. A psalm of the descendants of Korah. How great is the Lord, how deserving of praise, in the city of our God, which sits on his holy mountain!
48.2: It is high and magnificent; the whole earth rejoices to see it! Mount Zion, the holy mountain, is the city of the great King!
48.3: God himself is in Jerusalem’s towers, revealing himself as its defender.
48.4: The kings of the earth joined forces and advanced against the city.
48.5: But when they saw it, they were stunned; they were terrified and ran away.
48.6: They were gripped with terror and writhed in pain like a woman in labor.
48.7: You destroyed them like the mighty ships of Tarshish shattered by a powerful east wind.
48.8: We had heard of the city’s glory, but now we have seen it ourselves— the city of the Lord of Heaven’s Armies. It is the city of our God; he will make it safe forever. Interlude
48.9: O God, we meditate on your unfailing love as we worship in your Temple.
48.10: As your name deserves, O God, you will be praised to the ends of the earth. Your strong right hand is filled with victory.
48.11: Let the people on Mount Zion rejoice. Let all the towns of Judah be glad because of your justice.
48.12: Go, inspect the city of Jerusalem. Walk around and count the many towers.
48.13: Take note of the fortified walls, and tour all the citadels, that you may describe them to future generations.
48.14: For that is what God is like. He is our God forever and ever, and he will guide us until we die.

106.1: Praise the Lord! Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good! His faithful love endures forever.
106.2: Who can list the glorious miracles of the Lord? Who can ever praise him enough?
106.3: There is joy for those who deal justly with others and always do what is right.
106.4: Remember me, Lord, when you show favor to your people; come near and rescue me.
106.5: Let me share in the prosperity of your chosen ones. Let me rejoice in the joy of your people; let me praise you with those who are your heritage.
106.6: Like our ancestors, we have sinned. We have done wrong! We have acted wickedly!
106.7: Our ancestors in Egypt were not impressed by the Lord’s miraculous deeds. They soon forgot his many acts of kindness to them. Instead, they rebelled against him at the Red Sea.
106.8: Even so, he saved them— to defend the honor of his name and to demonstrate his mighty power.
106.9: He commanded the Red Sea to dry up. He led Israel across the sea as if it were a desert.
106.10: So he rescued them from their enemies and redeemed them from their foes.
106.11: Then the water returned and covered their enemies; not one of them survived.
106.12: Then his people believed his promises. Then they sang his praise.
106.13: Yet how quickly they forgot what he had done! They wouldn’t wait for his counsel!
106.14: In the wilderness their desires ran wild, testing God’s patience in that dry wasteland.
106.15: So he gave them what they asked for, but he sent a plague along with it.
106.16: The people in the camp were jealous of Moses and envious of Aaron, the Lord’s holy priest.
106.17: Because of this, the earth opened up; it swallowed Dathan and buried Abiram and the other rebels.
106.18: Fire fell upon their followers; a flame consumed the wicked.
106.19: The people made a calf at Mount Sinai; they bowed before an image made of gold.
106.20: They traded their glorious God for a statue of a grass-eating bull.
106.21: They forgot God, their savior, who had done such great things in Egypt—
106.22: such wonderful things in the land of Ham, such awesome deeds at the Red Sea.
106.23: So he declared he would destroy them. But Moses, his chosen one, stepped between the Lord and the people. He begged him to turn from his anger and not destroy them.
106.24: The people refused to enter the pleasant land, for they wouldn’t believe his promise to care for them.
106.25: Instead, they grumbled in their tents and refused to obey the Lord.
106.26: Therefore, he solemnly swore that he would kill them in the wilderness,
106.27: that he would scatter their descendants among the nations, exiling them to distant lands.
106.28: Then our ancestors joined in the worship of Baal at Peor; they even ate sacrifices offered to the dead!
106.29: They angered the Lord with all these things, so a plague broke out among them.
106.30: But Phinehas had the courage to intervene, and the plague was stopped.
106.31: So he has been regarded as a righteous man ever since that time.
106.32: At Meribah, too, they angered the Lord, causing Moses serious trouble.
106.33: They made Moses angry, and he spoke foolishly.
106.34: Israel failed to destroy the nations in the land, as the Lord had commanded them.
106.35: Instead, they mingled among the pagans and adopted their evil customs.
106.36: They worshiped their idols, which led to their downfall.
106.37: They even sacrificed their sons and their daughters to the demons.
106.38: They shed innocent blood, the blood of their sons and daughters. By sacrificing them to the idols of Canaan, they polluted the land with murder.
106.39: They defiled themselves by their evil deeds, and their love of idols was adultery in the Lord’s sight.
106.40: That is why the Lord’s anger burned against his people, and he abhorred his own special possession.
106.41: He handed them over to pagan nations, and they were ruled by those who hated them.
106.42: Their enemies crushed them and brought them under their cruel power.
106.43: Again and again he rescued them, but they chose to rebel against him, and they were finally destroyed by their sin.
106.44: Even so, he pitied them in their distress and listened to their cries.
106.45: He remembered his covenant with them and relented because of his unfailing love.
106.46: He even caused their captors to treat them with kindness.
106.47: Save us, O Lord our God! Gather us back from among the nations, so we can thank your holy name and rejoice and praise you.
106.48: Praise the Lord, the God of Israel, who lives from everlasting to everlasting! Let all the people say, “Amen!” Praise the Lord!

150.1: Praise the Lord! Praise God in his sanctuary; praise him in his mighty heaven!
150.2: Praise him for his mighty works; praise his unequaled greatness!
150.3: Praise him with a blast of the ram’s horn; praise him with the lyre and harp!
150.4: Praise him with the tambourine and dancing; praise him with strings and flutes!
150.5: Praise him with a clash of cymbals; praise him with loud clanging cymbals.
150.6: Let everything that breathes sing praises to the Lord! Praise the Lord!

107.1: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good! His faithful love endures forever.
107.2: Has the Lord redeemed you? Then speak out! Tell others he has redeemed you from your enemies.
107.3: For he has gathered the exiles from many lands, from east and west, from north and south.
107.4: Some wandered in the wilderness, lost and homeless.
107.5: Hungry and thirsty, they nearly died.
107.6: “Lord, help!” they cried in their trouble, and he rescued them from their distress.
107.7: He led them straight to safety, to a city where they could live.
107.8: Let them praise the Lord for his great love and for the wonderful things he has done for them.
107.9: For he satisfies the thirsty and fills the hungry with good things.
107.10: Some sat in darkness and deepest gloom, imprisoned in iron chains of misery.
107.11: They rebelled against the words of God, scorning the counsel of the Most High.
107.12: That is why he broke them with hard labor; they fell, and no one was there to help them.
107.13: “Lord, help!” they cried in their trouble, and he saved them from their distress.
107.14: He led them from the darkness and deepest gloom; he snapped their chains.
107.15: Let them praise the Lord for his great love and for the wonderful things he has done for them.
107.16: For he broke down their prison gates of bronze; he cut apart their bars of iron.
107.17: Some were fools; they rebelled and suffered for their sins.
107.18: They couldn’t stand the thought of food, and they were knocking on death’s door.
107.19: “Lord, help!” they cried in their trouble, and he saved them from their distress.
107.20: He sent out his word and healed them, snatching them from the door of death.
107.21: Let them praise the Lord for his great love and for the wonderful things he has done for them.
107.22: Let them offer sacrifices of thanksgiving and sing joyfully about his glorious acts.
107.23: Some went off to sea in ships, plying the trade routes of the world.
107.24: They, too, observed the Lord’s power in action, his impressive works on the deepest seas.
107.25: He spoke, and the winds rose, stirring up the waves.
107.26: Their ships were tossed to the heavens and plunged again to the depths; the sailors cringed in terror.
107.27: They reeled and staggered like drunkards and were at their wits’ end.
107.28: “Lord, help!” they cried in their trouble, and he saved them from their distress.
107.29: He calmed the storm to a whisper and stilled the waves.
107.30: What a blessing was that stillness as he brought them safely into harbor!
107.31: Let them praise the Lord for his great love and for the wonderful things he has done for them.
107.32: Let them exalt him publicly before the congregation and before the leaders of the nation.
107.33: He changes rivers into deserts, and springs of water into dry, thirsty land.
107.34: He turns the fruitful land into salty wastelands, because of the wickedness of those who live there.
107.35: But he also turns deserts into pools of water, the dry land into springs of water.
107.36: He brings the hungry to settle there and to build their cities.
107.37: They sow their fields, plant their vineyards, and harvest their bumper crops.
107.38: How he blesses them! They raise large families there, and their herds of livestock increase.
107.39: When they decrease in number and become impoverished through oppression, trouble, and sorrow,
107.40: the Lord pours contempt on their princes, causing them to wander in trackless wastelands.
107.41: But he rescues the poor from trouble and increases their families like flocks of sheep.
107.42: The godly will see these things and be glad, while the wicked are struck silent.
107.43: Those who are wise will take all this to heart; they will see in our history the faithful love of the Lord.

111.1: Praise the Lord! I will thank the Lord with all my heart as I meet with his godly people.
111.2: How amazing are the deeds of the Lord! All who delight in him should ponder them.
111.3: Everything he does reveals his glory and majesty. His righteousness never fails.
111.4: He causes us to remember his wonderful works. How gracious and merciful is our Lord!
111.5: He gives food to those who fear him; he always remembers his covenant.
111.6: He has shown his great power to his people by giving them the lands of other nations.
111.7: All he does is just and good, and all his commandments are trustworthy.
111.8: They are forever true, to be obeyed faithfully and with integrity.
111.9: He has paid a full ransom for his people. He has guaranteed his covenant with them forever. What a holy, awe-inspiring name he has!
111.10: Fear of the Lord is the foundation of true wisdom. All who obey his commandments will grow in wisdom. Praise him forever!

49.1: For the choir director: A psalm of the descendants of Korah. Listen to this, all you people! Pay attention, everyone in the world!
49.2: High and low, rich and poor—listen!
49.3: For my words are wise, and my thoughts are filled with insight.
49.4: I listen carefully to many proverbs and solve riddles with inspiration from a harp.
49.5: Why should I fear when trouble comes, when enemies surround me?
49.6: They trust in their wealth and boast of great riches.
49.7: Yet they cannot redeem themselves from death by paying a ransom to God.
49.8: Redemption does not come so easily, for no one can ever pay enough
49.9: to live forever and never see the grave.
49.10: Those who are wise must finally die, just like the foolish and senseless, leaving all their wealth behind.
49.11: The grave is their eternal home, where they will stay forever. They may name their estates after themselves,
49.12: but their fame will not last. They will die, just like animals.
49.13: This is the fate of fools, though they are remembered as being wise. Interlude
49.14: Like sheep, they are led to the grave, where death will be their shepherd. In the morning the godly will rule over them. Their bodies will rot in the grave, far from their grand estates.
49.15: But as for me, God will redeem my life. He will snatch me from the power of the grave. Interlude
49.16: So don’t be dismayed when the wicked grow rich and their homes become ever more splendid.
49.17: For when they die, they take nothing with them. Their wealth will not follow them into the grave.
49.18: In this life they consider themselves fortunate and are applauded for their success.
49.19: But they will die like all before them and never again see the light of day.
49.20: People who boast of their wealth don’t understand; they will die, just like animals.

146.1: Praise the Lord! Let all that I am praise the Lord.
146.2: I will praise the Lord as long as I live. I will sing praises to my God with my dying breath.
146.3: Don’t put your confidence in powerful people; there is no help for you there.
146.4: When they breathe their last, they return to the earth, and all their plans die with them.
146.5: But joyful are those who have the God of Israel as their helper, whose hope is in the Lord their God.
146.6: He made heaven and earth, the sea, and everything in them. He keeps every promise forever.
146.7: He gives justice to the oppressed and food to the hungry. The Lord frees the prisoners.
146.8: The Lord opens the eyes of the blind. The Lord lifts up those who are weighed down. The Lord loves the godly.
146.9: The Lord protects the foreigners among us. He cares for the orphans and widows, but he frustrates the plans of the wicked.
146.10: The Lord will reign forever. He will be your God, O Jerusalem, throughout the generations. Praise the Lord!

65.1: For the choir director: A song. A psalm of David. What mighty praise, O God, belongs to you in Zion. We will fulfill our vows to you,
65.2: for you answer our prayers. All of us must come to you.
65.3: Though we are overwhelmed by our sins, you forgive them all.
65.4: What joy for those you choose to bring near, those who live in your holy courts. What festivities await us inside your holy Temple.
65.5: You faithfully answer our prayers with awesome deeds, O God our savior. You are the hope of everyone on earth, even those who sail on distant seas.
65.6: You formed the mountains by your power and armed yourself with mighty strength.
65.7: You quieted the raging oceans with their pounding waves and silenced the shouting of the nations.
65.8: Those who live at the ends of the earth stand in awe of your wonders. From where the sun rises to where it sets, you inspire shouts of joy.
65.9: You take care of the earth and water it, making it rich and fertile. The river of God has plenty of water; it provides a bountiful harvest of grain, for you have ordered it so.
65.10: You drench the plowed ground with rain, melting the clods and leveling the ridges. You soften the earth with showers and bless its abundant crops.
65.11: You crown the year with a bountiful harvest; even the hard pathways overflow with abundance.
65.12: The grasslands of the wilderness become a lush pasture, and the hillsides blossom with joy.
65.13: The meadows are clothed with flocks of sheep, and the valleys are carpeted with grain. They all shout and sing for joy!

32.1: A psalm of David. Oh, what joy for those whose disobedience is forgiven, whose sin is put out of sight!
32.2: Yes, what joy for those whose record the Lord has cleared of guilt, whose lives are lived in complete honesty!
32.3: When I refused to confess my sin, my body wasted away, and I groaned all day long.
32.4: Day and night your hand of discipline was heavy on me. My strength evaporated like water in the summer heat. Interlude
32.5: Finally, I confessed all my sins to you and stopped trying to hide my guilt. I said to myself, “I will confess my rebellion to the Lord.” And you forgave me! All my guilt is gone. Interlude
32.6: Therefore, let all the godly pray to you while there is still time, that they may not drown in the floodwaters of judgment.
32.7: For you are my hiding place; you protect me from trouble. You surround me with songs of victory. Interlude
32.8: The Lord says, “I will guide you along the best pathway for your life. I will advise you and watch over you.
32.9: Do not be like a senseless horse or mule that needs a bit and bridle to keep it under control.”
32.10: Many sorrows come to the wicked, but unfailing love surrounds those who trust the Lord.
32.11: So rejoice in the Lord and be glad, all you who obey him! Shout for joy, all you whose hearts are pure!

24.1: A psalm of David. The earth is the Lord’s, and everything in it. The world and all its people belong to him.
24.2: For he laid the earth’s foundation on the seas and built it on the ocean depths.
24.3: Who may climb the mountain of the Lord? Who may stand in his holy place?
24.4: Only those whose hands and hearts are pure, who do not worship idols and never tell lies.
24.5: They will receive the Lord’s blessing and have a right relationship with God their savior.
24.6: Such people may seek you and worship in your presence, O God of Jacob. Interlude
24.7: Open up, ancient gates! Open up, ancient doors, and let the King of glory enter.
24.8: Who is the King of glory? The Lord, strong and mighty; the Lord, invincible in battle.
24.9: Open up, ancient gates! Open up, ancient doors, and let the King of glory enter.
24.10: Who is the King of glory? The Lord of Heaven’s Armies— he is the King of glory. Interlude

73.1: A psalm of Asaph. Truly God is good to Israel, to those whose hearts are pure.
73.2: But as for me, I almost lost my footing. My feet were slipping, and I was almost gone.
73.3: For I envied the proud when I saw them prosper despite their wickedness.
73.4: They seem to live such painless lives; their bodies are so healthy and strong.
73.5: They don’t have troubles like other people; they’re not plagued with problems like everyone else.
73.6: They wear pride like a jeweled necklace and clothe themselves with cruelty.
73.7: These fat cats have everything their hearts could ever wish for!
73.8: They scoff and speak only evil; in their pride they seek to crush others.
73.9: They boast against the very heavens, and their words strut throughout the earth.
73.10: And so the people are dismayed and confused, drinking in all their words.
73.11: “What does God know?” they ask. “Does the Most High even know what’s happening?”
73.12: Look at these wicked people— enjoying a life of ease while their riches multiply.
73.13: Did I keep my heart pure for nothing? Did I keep myself innocent for no reason?
73.14: I get nothing but trouble all day long; every morning brings me pain.
73.15: If I had really spoken this way to others, I would have been a traitor to your people.
73.16: So I tried to understand why the wicked prosper. But what a difficult task it is!
73.17: Then I went into your sanctuary, O God, and I finally understood the destiny of the wicked.
73.18: Truly, you put them on a slippery path and send them sliding over the cliff to destruction.
73.19: In an instant they are destroyed, completely swept away by terrors.
73.20: When you arise, O Lord, you will laugh at their silly ideas as a person laughs at dreams in the morning.
73.21: Then I realized that my heart was bitter, and I was all torn up inside.
73.22: I was so foolish and ignorant— I must have seemed like a senseless animal to you.
73.23: Yet I still belong to you; you hold my right hand.
73.24: You guide me with your counsel, leading me to a glorious destiny.
73.25: Whom have I in heaven but you? I desire you more than anything on earth.
73.26: My health may fail, and my spirit may grow weak, but God remains the strength of my heart; he is mine forever.
73.27: Those who desert him will perish, for you destroy those who abandon you.
73.28: But as for me, how good it is to be near God! I have made the Sovereign Lord my shelter, and I will tell everyone about the wonderful things you do.

53.1: For the choir director: A meditation; a psalm of David. Only fools say in their hearts, “There is no God.” They are corrupt, and their actions are evil; not one of them does good!
53.2: God looks down from heaven on the entire human race; he looks to see if anyone is truly wise, if anyone seeks God.
53.3: But no, all have turned away; all have become corrupt. No one does good, not a single one!
53.4: Will those who do evil never learn? They eat up my people like bread and wouldn’t think of praying to God.
53.5: Terror will grip them, terror like they have never known before. God will scatter the bones of your enemies. You will put them to shame, for God has rejected them.
53.6: Who will come from Mount Zion to rescue Israel? When God restores his people, Jacob will shout with joy, and Israel will rejoice.

45.1: For the choir director: A love song to be sung to the tune “Lilies.” A psalm of the descendants of Korah. Beautiful words stir my heart. I will recite a lovely poem about the king, for my tongue is like the pen of a skillful poet.
45.2: You are the most handsome of all. Gracious words stream from your lips. God himself has blessed you forever.
45.3: Put on your sword, O mighty warrior! You are so glorious, so majestic!
45.4: In your majesty, ride out to victory, defending truth, humility, and justice. Go forth to perform awe-inspiring deeds!
45.5: Your arrows are sharp, piercing your enemies’ hearts. The nations fall beneath your feet.
45.6: Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever. You rule with a scepter of justice.
45.7: You love justice and hate evil. Therefore God, your God, has anointed you, pouring out the oil of joy on you more than on anyone else.
45.8: Myrrh, aloes, and cassia perfume your robes. In ivory palaces the music of strings entertains you.
45.9: Kings’ daughters are among your noble women. At your right side stands the queen, wearing jewelry of finest gold from Ophir!
45.10: Listen to me, O royal daughter; take to heart what I say. Forget your people and your family far away.
45.11: For your royal husband delights in your beauty; honor him, for he is your lord.
45.12: The princess of Tyre will shower you with gifts. The wealthy will beg your favor.
45.13: The bride, a princess, looks glorious in her golden gown.
45.14: In her beautiful robes, she is led to the king, accompanied by her bridesmaids.
45.15: What a joyful and enthusiastic procession as they enter the king’s palace!
45.16: Your sons will become kings like their father. You will make them rulers over many lands.
45.17: I will bring honor to your name in every generation. Therefore, the nations will praise you forever and ever.

12.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David, to be accompanied by an eight-stringed instrument. Help, O Lord, for the godly are fast disappearing! The faithful have vanished from the earth!
12.2: Neighbors lie to each other, speaking with flattering lips and deceitful hearts.
12.3: May the Lord cut off their flattering lips and silence their boastful tongues.
12.4: They say, “We will lie to our hearts’ content. Our lips are our own—who can stop us?”
12.5: The Lord replies, “I have seen violence done to the helpless, and I have heard the groans of the poor. Now I will rise up to rescue them, as they have longed for me to do.”
12.6: The Lord’s promises are pure, like silver refined in a furnace, purified seven times over.
12.7: Therefore, Lord, we know you will protect the oppressed, preserving them forever from this lying generation,
12.8: even though the wicked strut about, and evil is praised throughout the land.

131.1: A song for pilgrims ascending to Jerusalem. A psalm of David. Lord, my heart is not proud; my eyes are not haughty. I don’t concern myself with matters too great or too awesome for me to grasp.
131.2: Instead, I have calmed and quieted myself, like a weaned child who no longer cries for its mother’s milk. Yes, like a weaned child is my soul within me.
131.3: O Israel, put your hope in the Lord— now and always.

69.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David, to be sung to the tune “Lilies.” Save me, O God, for the floodwaters are up to my neck.
69.2: Deeper and deeper I sink into the mire; I can’t find a foothold. I am in deep water, and the floods overwhelm me.
69.3: I am exhausted from crying for help; my throat is parched. My eyes are swollen with weeping, waiting for my God to help me.
69.4: Those who hate me without cause outnumber the hairs on my head. Many enemies try to destroy me with lies, demanding that I give back what I didn’t steal.
69.5: O God, you know how foolish I am; my sins cannot be hidden from you.
69.6: Don’t let those who trust in you be ashamed because of me, O Sovereign Lord of Heaven’s Armies. Don’t let me cause them to be humiliated, O God of Israel.
69.7: For I endure insults for your sake; humiliation is written all over my face.
69.8: Even my own brothers pretend they don’t know me; they treat me like a stranger.
69.9: Passion for your house has consumed me, and the insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.
69.10: When I weep and fast, they scoff at me.
69.11: When I dress in burlap to show sorrow, they make fun of me.
69.12: I am the favorite topic of town gossip, and all the drunks sing about me.
69.13: But I keep praying to you, Lord, hoping this time you will show me favor. In your unfailing love, O God, answer my prayer with your sure salvation.
69.14: Rescue me from the mud; don’t let me sink any deeper! Save me from those who hate me, and pull me from these deep waters.
69.15: Don’t let the floods overwhelm me, or the deep waters swallow me, or the pit of death devour me.
69.16: Answer my prayers, O Lord, for your unfailing love is wonderful. Take care of me, for your mercy is so plentiful.
69.17: Don’t hide from your servant; answer me quickly, for I am in deep trouble!
69.18: Come and redeem me; free me from my enemies.
69.19: You know of my shame, scorn, and disgrace. You see all that my enemies are doing.
69.20: Their insults have broken my heart, and I am in despair. If only one person would show some pity; if only one would turn and comfort me.
69.21: But instead, they give me poison for food; they offer me sour wine for my thirst.
69.22: Let the bountiful table set before them become a snare and their prosperity become a trap.
69.23: Let their eyes go blind so they cannot see, and make their bodies shake continually.
69.24: Pour out your fury on them; consume them with your burning anger.
69.25: Let their homes become desolate and their tents be deserted.
69.26: To the one you have punished, they add insult to injury; they add to the pain of those you have hurt.
69.27: Pile their sins up high, and don’t let them go free.
69.28: Erase their names from the Book of Life; don’t let them be counted among the righteous.
69.29: I am suffering and in pain. Rescue me, O God, by your saving power.
69.30: Then I will praise God’s name with singing, and I will honor him with thanksgiving.
69.31: For this will please the Lord more than sacrificing cattle, more than presenting a bull with its horns and hooves.
69.32: The humble will see their God at work and be glad. Let all who seek God’s help be encouraged.
69.33: For the Lord hears the cries of the needy; he does not despise his imprisoned people.
69.34: Praise him, O heaven and earth, the seas and all that move in them.
69.35: For God will save Jerusalem and rebuild the towns of Judah. His people will live there and settle in their own land.
69.36: The descendants of those who obey him will inherit the land, and those who love him will live there in safety.

2.1: Why are the nations so angry? Why do they waste their time with futile plans?
2.2: The kings of the earth prepare for battle; the rulers plot together against the Lord and against his anointed one.
2.3: “Let us break their chains,” they cry, “and free ourselves from slavery to God.”
2.4: But the one who rules in heaven laughs. The Lord scoffs at them.
2.5: Then in anger he rebukes them, terrifying them with his fierce fury.
2.6: For the Lord declares, “I have placed my chosen king on the throne in Jerusalem, on my holy mountain.”
2.7: The king proclaims the Lord’s decree: “The Lord said to me, ‘You are my son. Today I have become your Father.
2.8: Only ask, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance, the whole earth as your possession.
2.9: You will break them with an iron rod and smash them like clay pots.’”
2.10: Now then, you kings, act wisely! Be warned, you rulers of the earth!
2.11: Serve the Lord with reverent fear, and rejoice with trembling.
2.12: Submit to God’s royal son, or he will become angry, and you will be destroyed in the midst of all your activities— for his anger flares up in an instant. But what joy for all who take refuge in him!

86.1: A prayer of David. Bend down, O Lord, and hear my prayer; answer me, for I need your help.
86.2: Protect me, for I am devoted to you. Save me, for I serve you and trust you. You are my God.
86.3: Be merciful to me, O Lord, for I am calling on you constantly.
86.4: Give me happiness, O Lord, for I give myself to you.
86.5: O Lord, you are so good, so ready to forgive, so full of unfailing love for all who ask for your help.
86.6: Listen closely to my prayer, O Lord; hear my urgent cry.
86.7: I will call to you whenever I’m in trouble, and you will answer me.
86.8: No pagan god is like you, O Lord. None can do what you do!
86.9: All the nations you made will come and bow before you, Lord; they will praise your holy name.
86.10: For you are great and perform wonderful deeds. You alone are God.
86.11: Teach me your ways, O Lord, that I may live according to your truth! Grant me purity of heart, so that I may honor you.
86.12: With all my heart I will praise you, O Lord my God. I will give glory to your name forever,
86.13: for your love for me is very great. You have rescued me from the depths of death.
86.14: O God, insolent people rise up against me; a violent gang is trying to kill me. You mean nothing to them.
86.15: But you, O Lord, are a God of compassion and mercy, slow to get angry and filled with unfailing love and faithfulness.
86.16: Look down and have mercy on me. Give your strength to your servant; save me, the son of your servant.
86.17: Send me a sign of your favor. Then those who hate me will be put to shame, for you, O Lord, help and comfort me.

28.1: A psalm of David. I pray to you, O Lord, my rock. Do not turn a deaf ear to me. For if you are silent, I might as well give up and die.
28.2: Listen to my prayer for mercy as I cry out to you for help, as I lift my hands toward your holy sanctuary.
28.3: Do not drag me away with the wicked— with those who do evil— those who speak friendly words to their neighbors while planning evil in their hearts.
28.4: Give them the punishment they so richly deserve! Measure it out in proportion to their wickedness. Pay them back for all their evil deeds! Give them a taste of what they have done to others.
28.5: They care nothing for what the Lord has done or for what his hands have made. So he will tear them down, and they will never be rebuilt!
28.6: Praise the Lord! For he has heard my cry for mercy.
28.7: The Lord is my strength and shield. I trust him with all my heart. He helps me, and my heart is filled with joy. I burst out in songs of thanksgiving.
28.8: The Lord gives his people strength. He is a safe fortress for his anointed king.
28.9: Save your people! Bless Israel, your special possession. Lead them like a shepherd, and carry them in your arms forever.

127.1: A song for pilgrims ascending to Jerusalem. A psalm of Solomon. Unless the Lord builds a house, the work of the builders is wasted. Unless the Lord protects a city, guarding it with sentries will do no good.
127.2: It is useless for you to work so hard from early morning until late at night, anxiously working for food to eat; for God gives rest to his loved ones.
127.3: Children are a gift from the Lord; they are a reward from him.
127.4: Children born to a young man are like arrows in a warrior’s hands.
127.5: How joyful is the man whose quiver is full of them! He will not be put to shame when he confronts his accusers at the city gates.

90.1: A prayer of Moses, the man of God. Lord, through all the generations you have been our home!
90.2: Before the mountains were born, before you gave birth to the earth and the world, from beginning to end, you are God.
90.3: You turn people back to dust, saying, “Return to dust, you mortals!”
90.4: For you, a thousand years are as a passing day, as brief as a few night hours.
90.5: You sweep people away like dreams that disappear. They are like grass that springs up in the morning.
90.6: In the morning it blooms and flourishes, but by evening it is dry and withered.
90.7: We wither beneath your anger; we are overwhelmed by your fury.
90.8: You spread out our sins before you— our secret sins—and you see them all.
90.9: We live our lives beneath your wrath, ending our years with a groan.
90.10: Seventy years are given to us! Some even live to eighty. But even the best years are filled with pain and trouble; soon they disappear, and we fly away.
90.11: Who can comprehend the power of your anger? Your wrath is as awesome as the fear you deserve.
90.12: Teach us to realize the brevity of life, so that we may grow in wisdom.
90.13: O Lord, come back to us! How long will you delay? Take pity on your servants!
90.14: Satisfy us each morning with your unfailing love, so we may sing for joy to the end of our lives.
90.15: Give us gladness in proportion to our former misery! Replace the evil years with good.
90.16: Let us, your servants, see you work again; let our children see your glory.
90.17: And may the Lord our God show us his approval and make our efforts successful. Yes, make our efforts successful!

50.1: A psalm of Asaph. The Lord, the Mighty One, is God, and he has spoken; he has summoned all humanity from where the sun rises to where it sets.
50.2: From Mount Zion, the perfection of beauty, God shines in glorious radiance.
50.3: Our God approaches, and he is not silent. Fire devours everything in his way, and a great storm rages around him.
50.4: He calls on the heavens above and earth below to witness the judgment of his people.
50.5: “Bring my faithful people to me— those who made a covenant with me by giving sacrifices.”
50.6: Then let the heavens proclaim his justice, for God himself will be the judge. Interlude
50.7: “O my people, listen as I speak. Here are my charges against you, O Israel: I am God, your God!
50.8: I have no complaint about your sacrifices or the burnt offerings you constantly offer.
50.9: But I do not need the bulls from your barns or the goats from your pens.
50.10: For all the animals of the forest are mine, and I own the cattle on a thousand hills.
50.11: I know every bird on the mountains, and all the animals of the field are mine.
50.12: If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for all the world is mine and everything in it.
50.13: Do I eat the meat of bulls? Do I drink the blood of goats?
50.14: Make thankfulness your sacrifice to God, and keep the vows you made to the Most High.
50.15: Then call on me when you are in trouble, and I will rescue you, and you will give me glory.”
50.16: But God says to the wicked: “Why bother reciting my decrees and pretending to obey my covenant?
50.17: For you refuse my discipline and treat my words like trash.
50.18: When you see thieves, you approve of them, and you spend your time with adulterers.
50.19: Your mouth is filled with wickedness, and your tongue is full of lies.
50.20: You sit around and slander your brother— your own mother’s son.
50.21: While you did all this, I remained silent, and you thought I didn’t care. But now I will rebuke you, listing all my charges against you.
50.22: Repent, all of you who forget me, or I will tear you apart, and no one will help you.
50.23: But giving thanks is a sacrifice that truly honors me. If you keep to my path, I will reveal to you the salvation of God.”

108.1: A song. A psalm of David. My heart is confident in you, O God; no wonder I can sing your praises with all my heart!
108.2: Wake up, lyre and harp! I will wake the dawn with my song.
108.3: I will thank you, Lord, among all the people. I will sing your praises among the nations.
108.4: For your unfailing love is higher than the heavens. Your faithfulness reaches to the clouds.
108.5: Be exalted, O God, above the highest heavens. May your glory shine over all the earth.
108.6: Now rescue your beloved people. Answer and save us by your power.
108.7: God has promised this by his holiness: “I will divide up Shechem with joy. I will measure out the valley of Succoth.
108.8: Gilead is mine, and Manasseh, too. Ephraim, my helmet, will produce my warriors, and Judah, my scepter, will produce my kings.
108.9: But Moab, my washbasin, will become my servant, and I will wipe my feet on Edom and shout in triumph over Philistia.”
108.10: Who will bring me into the fortified city? Who will bring me victory over Edom?
108.11: Have you rejected us, O God? Will you no longer march with our armies?
108.12: Oh, please help us against our enemies, for all human help is useless.
108.13: With God’s help we will do mighty things, for he will trample down our foes.

46.1: For the choir director: A song of the descendants of Korah, to be sung by soprano voices. God is our refuge and strength, always ready to help in times of trouble.
46.2: So we will not fear when earthquakes come and the mountains crumble into the sea.
46.3: Let the oceans roar and foam. Let the mountains tremble as the waters surge! Interlude
46.4: A river brings joy to the city of our God, the sacred home of the Most High.
46.5: God dwells in that city; it cannot be destroyed. From the very break of day, God will protect it.
46.6: The nations are in chaos, and their kingdoms crumble! God’s voice thunders, and the earth melts!
46.7: The Lord of Heaven’s Armies is here among us; the God of Israel is our fortress. Interlude
46.8: Come, see the glorious works of the Lord: See how he brings destruction upon the world.
46.9: He causes wars to end throughout the earth. He breaks the bow and snaps the spear; he burns the shields with fire.
46.10: “Be still, and know that I am God! I will be honored by every nation. I will be honored throughout the world.”
46.11: The Lord of Heaven’s Armies is here among us; the God of Israel is our fortress. Interlude

11.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David. I trust in the Lord for protection. So why do you say to me, “Fly like a bird to the mountains for safety!
11.2: The wicked are stringing their bows and fitting their arrows on the bowstrings. They shoot from the shadows at those whose hearts are right.
11.3: The foundations of law and order have collapsed. What can the righteous do?”
11.4: But the Lord is in his holy Temple; the Lord still rules from heaven. He watches everyone closely, examining every person on earth.
11.5: The Lord examines both the righteous and the wicked. He hates those who love violence.
11.6: He will rain down blazing coals and burning sulfur on the wicked, punishing them with scorching winds.
11.7: For the righteous Lord loves justice. The virtuous will see his face.

149.1: Praise the Lord! Sing to the Lord a new song. Sing his praises in the assembly of the faithful.
149.2: O Israel, rejoice in your Maker. O people of Jerusalem, exult in your King.
149.3: Praise his name with dancing, accompanied by tambourine and harp.
149.4: For the Lord delights in his people; he crowns the humble with victory.
149.5: Let the faithful rejoice that he honors them. Let them sing for joy as they lie on their beds.
149.6: Let the praises of God be in their mouths, and a sharp sword in their hands—
149.7: to execute vengeance on the nations and punishment on the peoples,
149.8: to bind their kings with shackles and their leaders with iron chains,
149.9: to execute the judgment written against them. This is the glorious privilege of his faithful ones. Praise the Lord!

1.1: Oh, the joys of those who do not follow the advice of the wicked, or stand around with sinners, or join in with mockers.
1.2: But they delight in the law of the Lord, meditating on it day and night.
1.3: They are like trees planted along the riverbank, bearing fruit each season. Their leaves never wither, and they prosper in all they do.
1.4: But not the wicked! They are like worthless chaff, scattered by the wind.
1.5: They will be condemned at the time of judgment. Sinners will have no place among the godly.
1.6: For the Lord watches over the path of the godly, but the path of the wicked leads to destruction.

85.1: For the choir director: A psalm of the descendants of Korah. Lord, you poured out blessings on your land! You restored the fortunes of Israel.
85.2: You forgave the guilt of your people— yes, you covered all their sins. Interlude
85.3: You held back your fury. You kept back your blazing anger.
85.4: Now restore us again, O God of our salvation. Put aside your anger against us once more.
85.5: Will you be angry with us always? Will you prolong your wrath to all generations?
85.6: Won’t you revive us again, so your people can rejoice in you?
85.7: Show us your unfailing love, O Lord, and grant us your salvation.
85.8: I listen carefully to what God the Lord is saying, for he speaks peace to his faithful people. But let them not return to their foolish ways.
85.9: Surely his salvation is near to those who fear him, so our land will be filled with his glory.
85.10: Unfailing love and truth have met together. Righteousness and peace have kissed!
85.11: Truth springs up from the earth, and righteousness smiles down from heaven.
85.12: Yes, the Lord pours down his blessings. Our land will yield its bountiful harvest.
85.13: Righteousness goes as a herald before him, preparing the way for his steps.

132.1: A song for pilgrims ascending to Jerusalem. Lord, remember David and all that he suffered.
132.2: He made a solemn promise to the Lord. He vowed to the Mighty One of Israel,
132.3: “I will not go home; I will not let myself rest.
132.4: I will not let my eyes sleep nor close my eyelids in slumber
132.5: until I find a place to build a house for the Lord, a sanctuary for the Mighty One of Israel.”
132.6: We heard that the Ark was in Ephrathah; then we found it in the distant countryside of Jaar.
132.7: Let us go to the sanctuary of the Lord; let us worship at the footstool of his throne.
132.8: Arise, O Lord, and enter your resting place, along with the Ark, the symbol of your power.
132.9: May your priests be clothed in godliness; may your loyal servants sing for joy.
132.10: For the sake of your servant David, do not reject the king you have anointed.
132.11: The Lord swore an oath to David with a promise he will never take back: “I will place one of your descendants on your throne.
132.12: If your descendants obey the terms of my covenant and the laws that I teach them, then your royal line will continue forever and ever.”
132.13: For the Lord has chosen Jerusalem; he has desired it for his home.
132.14: “This is my resting place forever,” he said. “I will live here, for this is the home I desired.
132.15: I will bless this city and make it prosperous; I will satisfy its poor with food.
132.16: I will clothe its priests with godliness; its faithful servants will sing for joy.
132.17: Here I will increase the power of David; my anointed one will be a light for my people.
132.18: I will clothe his enemies with shame, but he will be a glorious king.”

93.1: The Lord is king! He is robed in majesty. Indeed, the Lord is robed in majesty and armed with strength. The world stands firm and cannot be shaken.
93.2: Your throne, O Lord, has stood from time immemorial. You yourself are from the everlasting past.
93.3: The floods have risen up, O Lord. The floods have roared like thunder; the floods have lifted their pounding waves.
93.4: But mightier than the violent raging of the seas, mightier than the breakers on the shore— the Lord above is mightier than these!
93.5: Your royal laws cannot be changed. Your reign, O Lord, is holy forever and ever.

124.1: A song for pilgrims ascending to Jerusalem. A psalm of David. What if the Lord had not been on our side? Let all Israel repeat:
124.2: What if the Lord had not been on our side when people attacked us?
124.3: They would have swallowed us alive in their burning anger.
124.4: The waters would have engulfed us; a torrent would have overwhelmed us.
124.5: Yes, the raging waters of their fury would have overwhelmed our very lives.
124.6: Praise the Lord, who did not let their teeth tear us apart!
124.7: We escaped like a bird from a hunter’s trap. The trap is broken, and we are free!
124.8: Our help is from the Lord, who made heaven and earth.

104.1: Let all that I am praise the Lord. O Lord my God, how great you are! You are robed with honor and majesty.
104.2: You are dressed in a robe of light. You stretch out the starry curtain of the heavens
104.3: you lay out the rafters of your home in the rain clouds. You make the clouds your chariot; you ride upon the wings of the wind.
104.4: The winds are your messengers; flames of fire are your servants.
104.5: You placed the world on its foundation so it would never be moved.
104.6: You clothed the earth with floods of water, water that covered even the mountains.
104.7: At your command, the water fled; at the sound of your thunder, it hurried away.
104.8: Mountains rose and valleys sank to the levels you decreed.
104.9: Then you set a firm boundary for the seas, so they would never again cover the earth.
104.10: You make springs pour water into the ravines, so streams gush down from the mountains.
104.11: They provide water for all the animals, and the wild donkeys quench their thirst.
104.12: The birds nest beside the streams and sing among the branches of the trees.
104.13: You send rain on the mountains from your heavenly home, and you fill the earth with the fruit of your labor.
104.14: You cause grass to grow for the livestock and plants for people to use. You allow them to produce food from the earth—
104.15: wine to make them glad, olive oil to soothe their skin, and bread to give them strength.
104.16: The trees of the Lord are well cared for— the cedars of Lebanon that he planted.
104.17: There the birds make their nests, and the storks make their homes in the cypresses.
104.18: High in the mountains live the wild goats, and the rocks form a refuge for the hyraxes.
104.19: You made the moon to mark the seasons, and the sun knows when to set.
104.20: You send the darkness, and it becomes night, when all the forest animals prowl about.
104.21: Then the young lions roar for their prey, stalking the food provided by God.
104.22: At dawn they slink back into their dens to rest.
104.23: Then people go off to their work, where they labor until evening.
104.24: O Lord, what a variety of things you have made! In wisdom you have made them all. The earth is full of your creatures.
104.25: Here is the ocean, vast and wide, teeming with life of every kind, both large and small.
104.26: See the ships sailing along, and Leviathan, which you made to play in the sea.
104.27: They all depend on you to give them food as they need it.
104.28: When you supply it, they gather it. You open your hand to feed them, and they are richly satisfied.
104.29: But if you turn away from them, they panic. When you take away their breath, they die and turn again to dust.
104.30: When you give them your breath, life is created, and you renew the face of the earth.
104.31: May the glory of the Lord continue forever! The Lord takes pleasure in all he has made!
104.32: The earth trembles at his glance; the mountains smoke at his touch.
104.33: I will sing to the Lord as long as I live. I will praise my God to my last breath!
104.34: May all my thoughts be pleasing to him, for I rejoice in the Lord.
104.35: Let all sinners vanish from the face of the earth; let the wicked disappear forever. Let all that I am praise the Lord. Praise the Lord!

112.1: Praise the Lord! How joyful are those who fear the Lord and delight in obeying his commands.
112.2: Their children will be successful everywhere; an entire generation of godly people will be blessed.
112.3: They themselves will be wealthy, and their good deeds will last forever.
112.4: Light shines in the darkness for the godly. They are generous, compassionate, and righteous.
112.5: Good comes to those who lend money generously and conduct their business fairly.
112.6: Such people will not be overcome by evil. Those who are righteous will be long remembered.
112.7: They do not fear bad news; they confidently trust the Lord to care for them.
112.8: They are confident and fearless and can face their foes triumphantly.
112.9: They share freely and give generously to those in need. Their good deeds will be remembered forever. They will have influence and honor.
112.10: The wicked will see this and be infuriated. They will grind their teeth in anger; they will slink away, their hopes thwarted.

145.1: A psalm of praise of David. I will exalt you, my God and King, and praise your name forever and ever.
145.2: I will praise you every day; yes, I will praise you forever.
145.3: Great is the Lord! He is most worthy of praise! No one can measure his greatness.
145.4: Let each generation tell its children of your mighty acts; let them proclaim your power.
145.5: I will meditate on your majestic, glorious splendor and your wonderful miracles.
145.6: Your awe-inspiring deeds will be on every tongue; I will proclaim your greatness.
145.7: Everyone will share the story of your wonderful goodness; they will sing with joy about your righteousness.
145.8: The Lord is merciful and compassionate, slow to get angry and filled with unfailing love.
145.9: The Lord is good to everyone. He showers compassion on all his creation.
145.10: All of your works will thank you, Lord, and your faithful followers will praise you.
145.11: They will speak of the glory of your kingdom; they will give examples of your power.
145.12: They will tell about your mighty deeds and about the majesty and glory of your reign.
145.13: For your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom. You rule throughout all generations. The Lord always keeps his promises; he is gracious in all he does.
145.14: The Lord helps the fallen and lifts those bent beneath their loads.
145.15: The eyes of all look to you in hope; you give them their food as they need it.
145.16: When you open your hand, you satisfy the hunger and thirst of every living thing.
145.17: The Lord is righteous in everything he does; he is filled with kindness.
145.18: The Lord is close to all who call on him, yes, to all who call on him in truth.
145.19: He grants the desires of those who fear him; he hears their cries for help and rescues them.
145.20: The Lord protects all those who love him, but he destroys the wicked.
145.21: I will praise the Lord, and may everyone on earth bless his holy name forever and ever.

89.1: A psalm of Ethan the Ezrahite. I will sing of the Lord’s unfailing love forever! Young and old will hear of your faithfulness.
89.2: Your unfailing love will last forever. Your faithfulness is as enduring as the heavens.
89.3: The Lord said, “I have made a covenant with David, my chosen servant. I have sworn this oath to him:
89.4: ‘I will establish your descendants as kings forever; they will sit on your throne from now until eternity.’” Interlude
89.5: All heaven will praise your great wonders, Lord; myriads of angels will praise you for your faithfulness.
89.6: For who in all of heaven can compare with the Lord? What mightiest angel is anything like the Lord?
89.7: The highest angelic powers stand in awe of God. He is far more awesome than all who surround his throne.
89.8: O Lord God of Heaven’s Armies! Where is there anyone as mighty as you, O Lord? You are entirely faithful.
89.9: You rule the oceans. You subdue their storm-tossed waves.
89.10: You crushed the great sea monster. You scattered your enemies with your mighty arm.
89.11: The heavens are yours, and the earth is yours; everything in the world is yours—you created it all.
89.12: You created north and south. Mount Tabor and Mount Hermon praise your name.
89.13: Powerful is your arm! Strong is your hand! Your right hand is lifted high in glorious strength.
89.14: Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne. Unfailing love and truth walk before you as attendants.
89.15: Happy are those who hear the joyful call to worship, for they will walk in the light of your presence, Lord.
89.16: They rejoice all day long in your wonderful reputation. They exult in your righteousness.
89.17: You are their glorious strength. It pleases you to make us strong.
89.18: Yes, our protection comes from the Lord, and he, the Holy One of Israel, has given us our king.
89.19: Long ago you spoke in a vision to your faithful people. You said, “I have raised up a warrior. I have selected him from the common people to be king.
89.20: I have found my servant David. I have anointed him with my holy oil.
89.21: I will steady him with my hand; with my powerful arm I will make him strong.
89.22: His enemies will not defeat him, nor will the wicked overpower him.
89.23: I will beat down his adversaries before him and destroy those who hate him.
89.24: My faithfulness and unfailing love will be with him, and by my authority he will grow in power.
89.25: I will extend his rule over the sea, his dominion over the rivers.
89.26: And he will call out to me, ‘You are my Father, my God, and the Rock of my salvation.’
89.27: I will make him my firstborn son, the mightiest king on earth.
89.28: I will love him and be kind to him forever; my covenant with him will never end.
89.29: I will preserve an heir for him; his throne will be as endless as the days of heaven.
89.30: But if his descendants forsake my instructions and fail to obey my regulations,
89.31: if they do not obey my decrees and fail to keep my commands,
89.32: then I will punish their sin with the rod, and their disobedience with beating.
89.33: But I will never stop loving him nor fail to keep my promise to him.
89.34: No, I will not break my covenant; I will not take back a single word I said.
89.35: I have sworn an oath to David, and in my holiness I cannot lie:
89.36: His dynasty will go on forever; his kingdom will endure as the sun.
89.37: It will be as eternal as the moon, my faithful witness in the sky!” Interlude
89.38: But now you have rejected him and cast him off. You are angry with your anointed king.
89.39: You have renounced your covenant with him; you have thrown his crown in the dust.
89.40: You have broken down the walls protecting him and ruined every fort defending him.
89.41: Everyone who comes along has robbed him, and he has become a joke to his neighbors.
89.42: You have strengthened his enemies and made them all rejoice.
89.43: You have made his sword useless and refused to help him in battle.
89.44: You have ended his splendor and overturned his throne.
89.45: You have made him old before his time and publicly disgraced him. Interlude
89.46: O Lord, how long will this go on? Will you hide yourself forever? How long will your anger burn like fire?
89.47: Remember how short my life is, how empty and futile this human existence!
89.48: No one can live forever; all will die. No one can escape the power of the grave. Interlude
89.49: Lord, where is your unfailing love? You promised it to David with a faithful pledge.
89.50: Consider, Lord, how your servants are disgraced! I carry in my heart the insults of so many people.
89.51: Your enemies have mocked me, O Lord; they mock your anointed king wherever he goes.
89.52: Praise the Lord forever! Amen and amen!

66.1: For the choir director: A song. A psalm. Shout joyful praises to God, all the earth!
66.2: Sing about the glory of his name! Tell the world how glorious he is.
66.3: Say to God, “How awesome are your deeds! Your enemies cringe before your mighty power.
66.4: Everything on earth will worship you; they will sing your praises, shouting your name in glorious songs.” Interlude
66.5: Come and see what our God has done, what awesome miracles he performs for people!
66.6: He made a dry path through the Red Sea, and his people went across on foot. There we rejoiced in him.
66.7: For by his great power he rules forever. He watches every movement of the nations; let no rebel rise in defiance. Interlude
66.8: Let the whole world bless our God and loudly sing his praises.
66.9: Our lives are in his hands, and he keeps our feet from stumbling.
66.10: You have tested us, O God; you have purified us like silver.
66.11: You captured us in your net and laid the burden of slavery on our backs.
66.12: Then you put a leader over us. We went through fire and flood, but you brought us to a place of great abundance.
66.13: Now I come to your Temple with burnt offerings to fulfill the vows I made to you—
66.14: yes, the sacred vows that I made when I was in deep trouble.
66.15: That is why I am sacrificing burnt offerings to you— the best of my rams as a pleasing aroma, and a sacrifice of bulls and male goats. Interlude
66.16: Come and listen, all you who fear God, and I will tell you what he did for me.
66.17: For I cried out to him for help, praising him as I spoke.
66.18: If I had not confessed the sin in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.
66.19: But God did listen! He paid attention to my prayer.
66.20: Praise God, who did not ignore my prayer or withdraw his unfailing love from me.

31.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David. O Lord, I have come to you for protection; don’t let me be disgraced. Save me, for you do what is right.
31.2: Turn your ear to listen to me; rescue me quickly. Be my rock of protection, a fortress where I will be safe.
31.3: You are my rock and my fortress. For the honor of your name, lead me out of this danger.
31.4: Pull me from the trap my enemies set for me, for I find protection in you alone.
31.5: I entrust my spirit into your hand. Rescue me, Lord, for you are a faithful God.
31.6: I hate those who worship worthless idols. I trust in the Lord.
31.7: I will be glad and rejoice in your unfailing love, for you have seen my troubles, and you care about the anguish of my soul.
31.8: You have not handed me over to my enemies but have set me in a safe place.
31.9: Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am in distress. Tears blur my eyes. My body and soul are withering away.
31.10: I am dying from grief; my years are shortened by sadness. Sin has drained my strength; I am wasting away from within.
31.11: I am scorned by all my enemies and despised by my neighbors— even my friends are afraid to come near me. When they see me on the street, they run the other way.
31.12: I am ignored as if I were dead, as if I were a broken pot.
31.13: I have heard the many rumors about me, and I am surrounded by terror. My enemies conspire against me, plotting to take my life.
31.14: But I am trusting you, O Lord, saying, “You are my God!”
31.15: My future is in your hands. Rescue me from those who hunt me down relentlessly.
31.16: Let your favor shine on your servant. In your unfailing love, rescue me.
31.17: Don’t let me be disgraced, O Lord, for I call out to you for help. Let the wicked be disgraced; let them lie silent in the grave.
31.18: Silence their lying lips— those proud and arrogant lips that accuse the godly.
31.19: How great is the goodness you have stored up for those who fear you. You lavish it on those who come to you for protection, blessing them before the watching world.
31.20: You hide them in the shelter of your presence, safe from those who conspire against them. You shelter them in your presence, far from accusing tongues.
31.21: Praise the Lord, for he has shown me the wonders of his unfailing love. He kept me safe when my city was under attack.
31.22: In panic I cried out, “I am cut off from the Lord!” But you heard my cry for mercy and answered my call for help.
31.23: Love the Lord, all you godly ones! For the Lord protects those who are loyal to him, but he harshly punishes the arrogant.
31.24: So be strong and courageous, all you who put your hope in the Lord!

27.1: A psalm of David. The Lord is my light and my salvation— so why should I be afraid? The Lord is my fortress, protecting me from danger, so why should I tremble?
27.2: When evil people come to devour me, when my enemies and foes attack me, they will stumble and fall.
27.3: Though a mighty army surrounds me, my heart will not be afraid. Even if I am attacked, I will remain confident.
27.4: The one thing I ask of the Lord— the thing I seek most— is to live in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, delighting in the Lord’s perfections and meditating in his Temple.
27.5: For he will conceal me there when troubles come; he will hide me in his sanctuary. He will place me out of reach on a high rock.
27.6: Then I will hold my head high above my enemies who surround me. At his sanctuary I will offer sacrifices with shouts of joy, singing and praising the Lord with music.
27.7: Hear me as I pray, O Lord. Be merciful and answer me!
27.8: My heart has heard you say, “Come and talk with me.” And my heart responds, “Lord, I am coming.”
27.9: Do not turn your back on me. Do not reject your servant in anger. You have always been my helper. Don’t leave me now; don’t abandon me, O God of my salvation!
27.10: Even if my father and mother abandon me, the Lord will hold me close.
27.11: Teach me how to live, O Lord. Lead me along the right path, for my enemies are waiting for me.
27.12: Do not let me fall into their hands. For they accuse me of things I’ve never done; with every breath they threaten me with violence.
27.13: Yet I am confident I will see the Lord’s goodness while I am here in the land of the living.
27.14: Wait patiently for the Lord. Be brave and courageous. Yes, wait patiently for the Lord.

70.1: For the choir director: A psalm of David, asking God to remember him. Please, God, rescue me! Come quickly, Lord, and help me.
70.2: May those who try to kill me be humiliated and put to shame. May those who take delight in my trouble be turned back in disgrace.
70.3: Let them be horrified by their shame, for they said, “Aha! We’ve got him now!”
70.4: But may all who search for you be filled with joy and gladness in you. May those who love your salvation repeatedly shout, “God is great!”
70.5: But as for me, I am poor and needy; please hurry to my aid, O God. You are my helper and my savior; O Lord, do not delay.

128.1: A song for pilgrims ascending to Jerusalem. How joyful are those who fear the Lord— all who follow his ways!
128.2: You will enjoy the fruit of your labor. How joyful and prosperous you will be!
128.3: Your wife will be like a fruitful grapevine, flourishing within your home. Your children will be like vigorous young olive trees as they sit around your table.
128.4: That is the Lord’s blessing for those who fear him.
128.5: May the Lord continually bless you from Zion. May you see Jerusalem prosper as long as you live.
128.6: May you live to enjoy your grandchildren. May Israel have peace!

71.1: O Lord, I have come to you for protection; don’t let me be disgraced.
71.2: Save me and rescue me, for you do what is right. Turn your ear to listen to me, and set me free.
71.3: Be my rock of safety where I can always hide. Give the order to save me, for you are my rock and my fortress.
71.4: My God, rescue me from the power of the wicked, from the clutches of cruel oppressors.
71.5: O Lord, you alone are my hope. I’ve trusted you, O Lord, from childhood.
71.6: Yes, you have been with me from birth; from my mother’s womb you have cared for me. No wonder I am always praising you!
71.7: My life is an example to many, because you have been my strength and protection.
71.8: That is why I can never stop praising you; I declare your glory all day long.
71.9: And now, in my old age, don’t set me aside. Don’t abandon me when my strength is failing.
71.10: For my enemies are whispering against me. They are plotting together to kill me.
71.11: They say, “God has abandoned him. Let’s go and get him, for no one will help him now.”
71.12: O God, don’t stay away. My God, please hurry to help me.
71.13: Bring disgrace and destruction on my accusers. Humiliate and shame those who want to harm me.
71.14: But I will keep on hoping for your help; I will praise you more and more.
71.15: I will tell everyone about your righteousness. All day long I will proclaim your saving power, though I am not skilled with words.
71.16: I will praise your mighty deeds, O Sovereign Lord. I will tell everyone that you alone are just.
71.17: O God, you have taught me from my earliest childhood, and I constantly tell others about the wonderful things you do.
71.18: Now that I am old and gray, do not abandon me, O God. Let me proclaim your power to this new generation, your mighty miracles to all who come after me.
71.19: Your righteousness, O God, reaches to the highest heavens. You have done such wonderful things. Who can compare with you, O God?
71.20: You have allowed me to suffer much hardship, but you will restore me to life again and lift me up from the depths of the earth.
71.21: You will restore me to even greater honor and comfort me once again.
71.22: Then I will praise you with music on the harp, because you are faithful to your promises, O my God. I will sing praises to you with a lyre, O Holy One of Israel.
71.23: I will shout for joy and sing your praises, for you have ransomed me.
71.24: I will tell about your righteous deeds all day long, for everyone who tried to hurt me has been shamed and humiliated.

129.1: A song for pilgrims ascending to Jerusalem. From my earliest youth my enemies have persecuted me. Let all Israel repeat this:
129.2: From my earliest youth my enemies have persecuted me, but they have never defeated me.
129.3: My back is covered with cuts, as if a farmer had plowed long furrows.
129.4: But the Lord is good; he has cut me free from the ropes of the ungodly.
129.5: May all who hate Jerusalem be turned back in shameful defeat.
129.6: May they be as useless as grass on a rooftop, turning yellow when only half grown,
129.7: ignored by the harvester, despised by the binder.
129.8: And may those who pass by refuse to give them this blessing: “The Lord bless you; we bless you in the Lord’s name.”

26.1: A psalm of David. Declare me innocent, O Lord, for I have acted with integrity; I have trusted in the Lord without wavering.
26.2: Put me on trial, Lord, and cross-examine me. Test my motives and my heart.
26.3: For I am always aware of your unfailing love, and I have lived according to your truth.
26.4: I do not spend time with liars or go along with hypocrites.
26.5: I hate the gatherings of those who do evil, and I refuse to join in with the wicked.
26.6: I wash my hands to declare my innocence. I come to your altar, O Lord,
26.7: singing a song of thanksgiving and telling of all your wonders.
26.8: I love your sanctuary, Lord, the place where your glorious presence dwells.
26.9: Don’t let me suffer the fate of sinners. Don’t condemn me along with murderers.
26.10: Their hands are dirty with evil schemes, and they constantly take bribes.
26.11: But I am not like that; I live with integrity. So redeem me and show me mercy.
26.12: Now I stand on solid ground, and I will publicly praise the Lord.

30.1: A psalm of David. A song for the dedication of the Temple. I will exalt you, Lord, for you rescued me. You refused to let my enemies triumph over me.
30.2: O Lord my God, I cried to you for help, and you restored my health.
30.3: You brought me up from the grave, O Lord. You kept me from falling into the pit of death.
30.4: Sing to the Lord, all you godly ones! Praise his holy name.
30.5: For his anger lasts only a moment, but his favor lasts a lifetime! Weeping may last through the night, but joy comes with the morning.
30.6: When I was prosperous, I said, “Nothing can stop me now!”
30.7: Your favor, O Lord, made me as secure as a mountain. Then you turned away from me, and I was shattered.
30.8: I cried out to you, O Lord. I begged the Lord for mercy, saying,
30.9: “What will you gain if I die, if I sink into the grave? Can my dust praise you? Can it tell of your faithfulness?
30.10: Hear me, Lord, and have mercy on me. Help me, O Lord.”
30.11: You have turned my mourning into joyful dancing. You have taken away my clothes of mourning and clothed me with joy,
30.12: that I might sing praises to you and not be silent. O Lord my God, I will give you thanks forever!

88.1: For the choir director: A psalm of the descendants of Korah. A song to be sung to the tune “The Suffering of Affliction.” A psalm of Heman the Ezrahite. O Lord, God of my salvation, I cry out to you by day. I come to you at night.
