52.5: Surely God will bring you down to everlasting ruin; He will snatch you up and tear you away from your tent; He will uproot you from the land of the living. Selah
52.6: The righteous will see and fear; they will mock the evildoer, saying,
52.7: “Look at the man who did not make God his refuge, but trusted in the abundance of his wealth and strengthened himself by destruction.”
52.8: But I am like an olive tree flourishing in the house of God; I trust in the loving devotion of God forever and ever.
52.9: I will praise You forever, because You have done it. I will wait on Your name— for it is good— in the presence of Your saints.

53.1: For the choirmaster. According to Mahalath. A Maskil of David.The fool says in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt; their ways are vile. There is no one who does good.
53.2: God looks down from heaven upon the sons of men to see if any understand, if any seek God.
53.3: All have turned away, they have together become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one.
53.4: Will the workers of iniquity never learn? They devour my people like bread; they refuse to call upon God.
53.5: There they are, overwhelmed with dread, where there was nothing to fear. For God has scattered the bones of those who besieged you. You put them to shame, for God has despised them.
53.6: Oh, that the salvation of Israel would come from Zion! When God restores His captive people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad!

54.1: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Maskil of David. When the Ziphites went to Saul and said, “Is David not hiding among us?”Save me, O God, by Your name, and vindicate me by Your might!
54.2: Hear my prayer, O God; listen to the words of my mouth.
54.3: For strangers rise up against me, and ruthless men seek my life— men with no regard for God. Selah
54.4: Surely God is my helper; the Lord is the sustainer of my soul.
54.5: He will reward my enemies with evil. In Your faithfulness, destroy them.
54.6: Freely I will sacrifice to You; I will praise Your name, O LORD, for it is good.
54.7: For He has delivered me from every trouble, and my eyes have looked in triumph on my foes.

55.1: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Maskil of David.Listen to my prayer, O God, and do not ignore my plea.
55.2: Attend to me and answer me. I am restless in my complaint, and distraught
55.3: at the voice of the enemy, at the pressure of the wicked. For they bring down disaster upon me and resent me in their anger.
55.4: My heart pounds within me, and the terrors of death assail me.
55.5: Fear and trembling grip me, and horror has overwhelmed me.
55.6: I said, “Oh, that I had wings like a dove! I would fly away and find rest.
55.7: How far away I would flee! In the wilderness I would remain. Selah
55.8: I would hurry to my shelter, far from this raging tempest.”
55.9: O Lord, confuse and confound their speech, for I see violence and strife in the city.
55.10: Day and night they encircle the walls, while malice and trouble lie within.
55.11: Destruction is within; oppression and deceit never leave the streets.
55.12: For it is not an enemy who insults me; that I could endure. It is not a foe who rises against me; from him I could hide.
55.13: But it is you, a man like myself, my companion and close friend.
55.14: We shared sweet fellowship together; we walked with the crowd into the house of God.
55.15: Let death seize them by surprise; let them go down to Sheol alive, for evil is with them in their homes.
55.16: But I call to God, and the LORD saves me.
55.17: Morning, noon, and night, I cry out in distress, and He hears my voice.
55.18: He redeems my soul in peace from the battle waged against me, even though many oppose me.
55.19: God will hear and humiliate them— the One enthroned for the ages— Selah because they do not change and they have no fear of God.
55.20: My companion attacks his friends; he violates his covenant.
55.21: His speech is smooth as butter, but war is in his heart. His words are softer than oil, yet they are swords unsheathed.
55.22: Cast your burden upon the LORD and He will sustain you; He will never let the righteous be shaken.
55.23: But You, O God, will bring them down to the Pit of destruction; men of bloodshed and deceit will not live out half their days. But I will trust in You.

56.1: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “A Dove on Distant Oaks.” A Miktam of David, when the Philistines seized him in Gath.Be merciful to me, O God, for men are hounding me; all day they press their attack.
56.2: My enemies pursue me all day long, for many proudly assail me.
56.3: When I am afraid, I put my trust in You.
56.4: In God, whose word I praise— in God I trust. I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
56.5: All day long they twist my words; all their thoughts are on my demise.
56.6: They conspire, they lurk, they watch my steps while they wait to take my life.
56.7: In spite of such sin, will they escape? In Your anger, O God, cast down the nations.
56.8: You have taken account of my wanderings. Put my tears in Your bottle— are they not in Your book?
56.9: Then my enemies will retreat on the day I cry for help. By this I will know that God is on my side.
56.10: In God, whose word I praise, in the LORD, whose word I praise,
56.11: in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
56.12: Your vows are upon me, O God; I will render thank offerings to You.
56.13: For You have delivered my soul from death, and my feet from stumbling, that I may walk before God in the light of life.

57.1: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Miktam of David, when he fled from Saul into the cave.Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy, for in You my soul takes refuge. In the shadow of Your wings I will take shelter until the danger has passed.
57.2: I cry out to God Most High, to God who fulfills His purpose for me.
57.3: He reaches down from heaven and saves me; He rebukes those who trample me. Selah God sends forth His loving devotion and His truth.
57.4: My soul is among the lions; I lie down with ravenous beasts— with men whose teeth are spears and arrows, whose tongues are sharp swords.
57.5: Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; may Your glory cover all the earth.
57.6: They spread a net for my feet; my soul was despondent. They dug a pit before me, but they themselves have fallen into it! Selah
57.7: My heart is steadfast, O God, my heart is steadfast. I will sing and make music.
57.8: Awake, my glory! Awake, O harp and lyre! I will awaken the dawn.
57.9: I will praise You, O Lord, among the nations; I will sing Your praises among the peoples.
57.10: For Your loving devotion reaches to the heavens, and Your faithfulness to the clouds.
57.11: Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; may Your glory cover all the earth.

58.1: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Miktam of David.Do you indeed speak justly, O rulers? Do you judge uprightly, O sons of men?
58.2: No, in your hearts you devise injustice; with your hands you mete out violence on the earth.
58.3: The wicked are estranged from the womb; the liars go astray from birth.
58.4: Their venom is like the venom of a snake, like a cobra that shuts its ears,
58.5: refusing to hear the tune of the charmer who skillfully weaves his spell.
58.6: O God, shatter their teeth in their mouths; O LORD, tear out the fangs of the lions.
58.7: May they vanish like water that runs off; when they draw the bow, may their arrows be blunted.
58.8: Like a slug that dissolves in its slime, like a woman’s stillborn child, may they never see the sun.
58.9: Before your pots can feel the burning thorns— whether green or dry— He will sweep them away.
58.10: The righteous will rejoice when they see they are avenged; they will wash their feet in the blood of the wicked.
58.11: Then men will say, “There is surely a reward for the righteous! There is surely a God who judges the earth!”

59.1: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Miktam of David, when Saul sent men to watch David’s house in order to kill him.Deliver me from my enemies, O my God; protect me from those who rise against me.
59.2: Deliver me from workers of iniquity, and save me from men of bloodshed.
59.3: See how they lie in wait for me. Fierce men conspire against me for no transgression or sin of my own, O LORD.
59.4: For no fault of my own, they move swiftly to attack me. Arise to help me, and take notice.
59.5: O LORD God of Hosts, the God of Israel, rouse Yourself to punish all the nations; show no mercy to the wicked traitors. Selah
59.6: They return in the evening, snarling like dogs and prowling around the city.
59.7: See what they spew from their mouths— sharp words from their lips: “For who can hear us?”
59.8: But You, O LORD, laugh at them; You scoff at all the nations.
59.9: I will keep watch for You, O my strength, because You, O God, are my fortress.
59.10: My God of loving devotion will come to meet me; God will let me stare down my foes.
59.11: Do not kill them, or my people will forget. Scatter them by Your power, and bring them down, O Lord, our shield.
59.12: By the sins of their mouths and the words of their lips, let them be trapped in their pride, in the curses and lies they utter.
59.13: Consume them in wrath; consume them till they are no more, so it may be known to the ends of the earth that God rules over Jacob. Selah
59.14: They return in the evening, snarling like dogs and prowling around the city.
59.15: They scavenge for food, and growl if they are not satisfied.
59.16: But I will sing of Your strength and proclaim Your loving devotion in the morning. For You are my fortress, my refuge in times of trouble.
59.17: To You, O my strength, I sing praises, for You, O God, are my fortress, my God of loving devotion.

60.1: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “The Lily of the Covenant.” A Miktam of David for instruction. When he fought Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab returned and struck down 12,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt.You have rejected us, O God; You have broken us; You have been angry; restore us!
60.2: You have shaken the land and torn it open. Heal its fractures, for it is quaking.
60.3: You have shown Your people hardship; we are staggered from the wine You made us drink.
60.4: You have raised a banner for those who fear You, that they may flee the bow. Selah
60.5: Respond and save us with Your right hand, that Your beloved may be delivered.
60.6: God has spoken from His sanctuary: “I will triumph! I will parcel out Shechem and apportion the Valley of Succoth.
60.7: Gilead is Mine, and Manasseh is Mine; Ephraim is My helmet, Judah is My scepter.
60.8: Moab is My washbasin; upon Edom I toss My sandal; over Philistia I shout in triumph.”
60.9: Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?
60.10: Have You not rejected us, O God? Will You no longer march out, O God, with our armies?
60.11: Give us aid against the enemy, for the help of man is worthless.
60.12: With God we will perform with valor, and He will trample our enemies.

61.1: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. Of David.Hear my cry, O God; attend to my prayer.
61.2: From the ends of the earth I call out to You whenever my heart is faint. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
61.3: For You have been my refuge, a tower of strength against the enemy.
61.4: Let me dwell in Your tent forever and take refuge in the shelter of Your wings. Selah
61.5: For You have heard my vows, O God; You have given me the inheritance reserved for those who fear Your name.
61.6: Increase the days of the king’s life; may his years span many generations.
61.7: May he sit enthroned in God’s presence forever; appoint Your loving devotion and Your faithfulness to guard him.
61.8: Then I will ever sing praise to Your name and fulfill my vows day by day.

62.1: For the choirmaster. According to Jeduthun. A Psalm of David.In God alone my soul finds rest; my salvation comes from Him.
62.2: He alone is my rock and my salvation. He is my fortress; I will never be shaken.
62.3: How long will you threaten a man? Will all of you throw him down like a leaning wall or a tottering fence?
62.4: They fully intend to cast him down from his lofty perch; they delight in lies; with their mouths they bless, but inwardly they curse. Selah
62.5: Rest in God alone, O my soul, for my hope comes from Him.
62.6: He alone is my rock and my salvation; He is my fortress; I will not be shaken.
62.7: My salvation and my honor rest on God, my strong rock; my refuge is in God.
62.8: Trust in Him at all times, O people; pour out your hearts before Him. God is our refuge. Selah
62.9: Lowborn men are but a vapor; the exalted are but a lie. Weighed on the scale, they go up; together they are but a vapor.
62.10: Place no trust in extortion or false hope in stolen goods. If your riches increase, do not set your heart upon them.
62.11: God has spoken once; I have heard this twice: that power belongs to God,
62.12: and loving devotion to You, O Lord. For You will repay each man according to his deeds.

63.1: A Psalm of David, when he was in the Wilderness of Judah.O God, You are my God. Earnestly I seek You; my soul thirsts for You. My body yearns for You in a dry and weary land without water.
63.2: So I have seen You in the sanctuary and beheld Your power and glory.
63.3: Because Your loving devotion is better than life, my lips will glorify You.
63.4: So I will bless You as long as I live; in Your name I will lift my hands.
63.5: My soul is satisfied as with the richest of foods; with joyful lips my mouth will praise You.
63.6: When I remember You on my bed, I think of You through the watches of the night.
63.7: For You are my help; I will sing for joy in the shadow of Your wings.
63.8: My soul clings to You; Your right hand upholds me.
63.9: But those who seek my life to destroy it will go into the depths of the earth.
63.10: They will fall to the power of the sword; they will become a portion for foxes.
63.11: But the king will rejoice in God; all who swear by Him will exult, for the mouths of liars will be shut.

64.1: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David.Hear, O God, my voice of complaint; preserve my life from dread of the enemy.
64.2: Hide me from the scheming of the wicked, from the mob of workers of iniquity,
64.3: who sharpen their tongues like swords and aim their bitter words like arrows,
64.4: ambushing the innocent in seclusion, shooting suddenly, without fear.
64.5: They hold fast to their evil purpose; they speak of hiding their snares. “Who will see them?” they say.
64.6: They devise injustice and say, “We have perfected a secret plan.” For the inner man and the heart are mysterious.
64.7: But God will shoot them with arrows; suddenly they will be wounded.
64.8: They will be made to stumble, their own tongues turned against them. All who see will shake their heads.
64.9: Then all mankind will fear and proclaim the work of God; so they will ponder what He has done.
64.10: Let the righteous rejoice in the LORD and take refuge in Him; let all the upright in heart exult.

65.1: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. A song.Praise awaits You, O God, in Zion; to You our vows will be fulfilled.
65.2: O You who listen to prayer, all people will come to You.
65.3: When iniquities prevail against me, You atone for our transgressions.
65.4: Blessed is the one You choose and bring near to dwell in Your courts! We are filled with the goodness of Your house, the holiness of Your temple.
65.5: With awesome deeds of righteousness You answer us, O God of our salvation, the hope of all the ends of the earth and of the farthest seas.
65.6: You formed the mountains by Your power, having girded Yourself with might.
65.7: You stilled the roaring of the seas, the pounding of their waves, and the tumult of the nations.
65.8: Those who live far away fear Your wonders; You make the dawn and sunset shout for joy.
65.9: You attend to the earth and water it; with abundance You enrich it. The streams of God are full of water, for You prepare our grain by providing for the earth.
65.10: You soak its furrows and level its ridges; You soften it with showers and bless its growth.
65.11: You crown the year with Your bounty, and Your paths overflow with plenty.
65.12: The pastures of the wilderness overflow; the hills are robed with joy.
65.13: The pastures are clothed with flocks, and the valleys are decked with grain. They shout in triumph; indeed, they sing.

66.1: For the choirmaster. A song. A Psalm.Make a joyful noise to God, all the earth!
66.2: Sing the glory of His name; make His praise glorious.
66.3: Say to God, “How awesome are Your deeds! So great is Your power that Your enemies cower before You.
66.4: All the earth bows down to You; they sing praise to You; they sing praise to Your name.” Selah
66.5: Come and see the works of God; how awesome are His deeds toward mankind.
66.6: He turned the sea into dry land; they passed through the waters on foot; there we rejoiced in Him.
66.7: He rules forever by His power; His eyes watch the nations. Do not let the rebellious exalt themselves. Selah
66.8: Bless our God, O peoples; let the sound of His praise be heard.
66.9: He preserves our lives and keeps our feet from slipping.
66.10: For You, O God, have tested us; You have refined us like silver.
66.11: You led us into the net; You laid burdens on our backs.
66.12: You let men ride over our heads; we went through fire and water, but You brought us into abundance.
66.13: I will enter Your house with burnt offerings; I will fulfill my vows to You—
66.14: the vows that my lips promised and my mouth spoke in my distress.
66.15: I will offer You fatlings as burnt offerings, with the fragrant smoke of rams; I will offer bulls and goats. Selah
66.16: Come and listen, all you who fear God, and I will declare what He has done for me.
66.17: I cried out to Him with my mouth and praised Him with my tongue.
66.18: If I had cherished iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.
66.19: But God has surely heard; He has attended to the sound of my prayer.
66.20: Blessed be God, who has not rejected my prayer or withheld from me His loving devotion!

67.1: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Psalm. A song.May God be gracious to us and bless us, and cause His face to shine upon us, Selah
67.2: that Your ways may be known on earth, Your salvation among all nations.
67.3: Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You.
67.4: Let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for You judge the peoples justly and lead the nations of the earth. Selah
67.5: Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You.
67.6: The earth has yielded its harvest; God, our God, blesses us.
67.7: God blesses us, that all the ends of the earth shall fear Him.

68.1: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. A song.God arises. His enemies are scattered, and those who hate Him flee His presence.
68.2: As smoke is blown away, You will drive them out; as wax melts before the fire, the wicked will perish in the presence of God.
68.3: But the righteous will be glad and rejoice before God; they will celebrate with joy.
68.4: Sing to God! Sing praises to His name. Exalt Him who rides on the clouds — His name is the LORD— and rejoice before Him.
68.5: A father of the fatherless and a defender of widows is God in His holy habitation.
68.6: God settles the lonely in families; He leads the prisoners out to prosperity, but the rebellious dwell in a sun-scorched land.
68.7: O God, when You went out before Your people, when You marched through the wasteland, Selah
68.8: the earth shook and the heavens poured down rain before God, the One on Sinai, before God, the God of Israel.
68.9: You sent abundant rain, O God; You refreshed Your weary inheritance.
68.10: Your flock settled therein; O God, from Your bounty You provided for the poor.
68.11: The Lord gives the command; a great company of women proclaim it:
68.12: “Kings and their armies flee in haste; she who waits at home divides the plunder.
68.13: Though you lie down among the sheepfolds, the wings of the dove are covered with silver, and her feathers with shimmering gold.”
68.14: When the Almighty scattered the kings in the land, it was like the snow falling on Zalmon.
68.15: A mountain of God is Mount Bashan; a mountain of many peaks is Mount Bashan.
68.16: Why do you gaze in envy, O mountains of many peaks? This is the mountain God chose for His dwelling, where the LORD will surely dwell forever.
68.17: The chariots of God are tens of thousands— thousands of thousands are they; the Lord is in His sanctuary as He was at Sinai.
68.18: You have ascended on high; You have led captives away. You have received gifts from men, even from the rebellious, that the LORD God may dwell there.
68.19: Blessed be the Lord, who daily bears our burden, the God of our salvation. Selah
68.20: Our God is a God of deliverance; the Lord GOD is our rescuer from death.
68.21: Surely God will crush the heads of His enemies, the hairy crowns of those who persist in guilty ways.
68.22: The Lord said, “I will retrieve them from Bashan, I will bring them up from the depths of the sea,
68.23: that your foot may be dipped in the blood of your foes— the tongues of your dogs in the same.”
68.24: They have seen Your procession, O God— the march of my God and King into the sanctuary.
68.25: The singers lead the way, the musicians follow after, among the maidens playing tambourines.
68.26: Bless God in the great congregation; bless the LORD from the fountain of Israel.
68.27: There is Benjamin, the youngest, ruling them, the princes of Judah in their company, the princes of Zebulun and of Naphtali.
68.28: Summon Your power, O God; show Your strength, O God, which You have exerted on our behalf.
68.29: Because of Your temple at Jerusalem kings will bring You gifts.
68.30: Rebuke the beast in the reeds, the herd of bulls among the calves of the nations, until it submits, bringing bars of silver. Scatter the nations who delight in war.
68.31: Envoys will arrive from Egypt; Cush will stretch out her hands to God.
68.32: Sing to God, O kingdoms of the earth; sing praises to the Lord— Selah
68.33: to Him who rides upon the highest heavens of old; behold, His mighty voice resounds.
68.34: Ascribe the power to God, whose majesty is over Israel, whose strength is in the skies.
68.35: O God, You are awesome in Your sanctuary; the God of Israel Himself gives strength and power to His people. Blessed be God!

69.1: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Lilies.” Of David.Save me, O God, for the waters are up to my neck.
69.2: I have sunk into the miry depths, where there is no footing; I have drifted into deep waters, where the flood engulfs me.
69.3: I am weary from my crying; my throat is parched. My eyes fail, looking for my God.
69.4: Those who hate me without cause outnumber the hairs of my head; many are those who would destroy me— my enemies for no reason. Though I did not steal, I must repay.
69.5: You know my folly, O God, and my guilt is not hidden from You.
69.6: May those who hope in You not be ashamed through me, O Lord GOD of Hosts; may those who seek You not be dishonored through me, O God of Israel.
69.7: For I have endured scorn for Your sake, and shame has covered my face.
69.8: I have become a stranger to my brothers and a foreigner to my mother’s sons,
69.9: because zeal for Your house has consumed me, and the insults of those who insult You have fallen on me.
69.10: I wept and fasted, but it brought me reproach.
69.11: I made sackcloth my clothing, and I was sport to them.
69.12: Those who sit at the gate mock me, and I am the song of drunkards.
69.13: But my prayer to You, O LORD, is for a time of favor. In Your abundant loving devotion, O God, answer me with Your sure salvation.
69.14: Rescue me from the mire and do not let me sink; deliver me from my foes and out of the deep waters.
69.15: Do not let the floods engulf me or the depths swallow me up; let not the Pit close its mouth over me.
69.16: Answer me, O LORD, for Your loving devotion is good; turn to me in keeping with Your great compassion.
69.17: Hide not Your face from Your servant, for I am in distress. Answer me quickly!
69.18: Draw near to my soul and redeem me; ransom me because of my foes.
69.19: You know my reproach, my shame and disgrace. All my adversaries are before You.
69.20: Insults have broken my heart, and I am in despair. I looked for sympathy, but there was none, for comforters, but I found no one.
69.21: They poisoned my food with gall and gave me vinegar to quench my thirst.
69.22: May their table become a snare; may it be a retribution and a trap.
69.23: May their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent forever.
69.24: Pour out Your wrath upon them, and let Your burning anger overtake them.
69.25: May their place be deserted; let there be no one to dwell in their tents.
69.26: For they persecute the one You struck and recount the pain of those You wounded.
69.27: Add iniquity to their iniquity; let them not share in Your righteousness.
69.28: May they be blotted out of the Book of Life and not listed with the righteous.
69.29: But I am in pain and distress; let Your salvation protect me, O God.
69.30: I will praise God’s name in song and exalt Him with thanksgiving.
69.31: And this will please the LORD more than an ox, more than a bull with horns and hooves.
69.32: The humble will see and rejoice. You who seek God, let your hearts be revived!
69.33: For the LORD listens to the needy and does not despise His captive people.
69.34: Let heaven and earth praise Him, the seas and everything that moves in them.
69.35: For God will save Zion and rebuild the cities of Judah, that they may dwell there and possess it.
69.36: The descendants of His servants will inherit it, and those who love His name will settle in it.

70.1: For the choirmaster. Of David. To bring remembrance.Make haste, O God, to deliver me! Hurry, O LORD, to help me!
70.2: May those who seek my life be ashamed and confounded; may those who wish me harm be repelled and humiliated.
70.3: May those who say, “Aha, aha!” retreat because of their shame.
70.4: May all who seek You rejoice and be glad in You; may those who love Your salvation always say, “Let God be magnified!”
70.5: But I am poor and needy; hurry to me, O God. You are my help and my deliverer; O LORD, do not delay.

71.1: In You, O LORD, I have taken refuge; let me never be put to shame.
71.2: In Your justice, rescue and deliver me; incline Your ear and save me.
71.3: Be my rock of refuge, where I can always go. Give the command to save me, for You are my rock and my fortress.
71.4: Deliver me, O my God, from the hand of the wicked, from the grasp of the unjust and ruthless.
71.5: For You are my hope, O Lord GOD, my confidence from my youth.
71.6: I have leaned on You since birth; You pulled me from my mother’s womb. My praise is always for You.
71.7: I have become a portent to many, but You are my strong refuge.
71.8: My mouth is filled with Your praise and with Your splendor all day long.
71.9: Do not discard me in my old age; do not forsake me when my strength fails.
71.10: For my enemies speak against me, and those who lie in wait for my life conspire,
71.11: saying, “God has forsaken him; pursue him and seize him, for there is no one to rescue him.”
71.12: Be not far from me, O God. Hurry, O my God, to help me.
71.13: May the accusers of my soul be ashamed and consumed; may those who seek my harm be covered with scorn and disgrace.
71.14: But I will always hope and will praise You more and more.
71.15: My mouth will declare Your righteousness and Your salvation all day long, though I cannot know their full measure.
71.16: I will come in the strength of the Lord GOD; I will proclaim Your righteousness—Yours alone.
71.17: O God, You have taught me from my youth, and to this day I proclaim Your marvelous deeds.
71.18: Even when I am old and gray, do not forsake me, O God, until I proclaim Your power to the next generation, Your might to all who are to come.
71.19: Your righteousness reaches to the heavens, O God, You who have done great things. Who, O God, is like You?
71.20: Though You have shown me many troubles and misfortunes, You will revive me once again. Even from the depths of the earth You will bring me back up.
71.21: You will increase my honor and comfort me once again.
71.22: So I will praise You with the harp for Your faithfulness, O my God; I will sing praise to You with the lyre, O Holy One of Israel.
71.23: When I sing praise to You my lips will shout for joy, along with my soul, which You have redeemed.
71.24: My tongue will indeed proclaim Your righteousness all day long, for those who seek my harm are disgraced and confounded.

72.1: Of Solomon.Endow the king with Your justice, O God, and the son of the king with Your righteousness.
72.2: May he judge Your people with righteousness and Your afflicted with justice.
72.3: May the mountains bring peace to the people, and the hills bring righteousness.
72.4: May he vindicate the afflicted among the people; may he save the children of the needy and crush the oppressor.
72.5: May they fear him as long as the sun shines, as long as the moon remains, through all generations.
72.6: May he be like rain that falls on freshly cut grass, like spring showers that water the earth.
72.7: May the righteous flourish in his days and prosperity abound until the moon is no more.
72.8: May he rule from sea to sea, and from the Euphrates to the ends of the earth.
72.9: May the nomads bow before him, and his enemies lick the dust.
72.10: May the kings of Tarshish and distant shores bring tribute; may the kings of Sheba and Seba offer gifts.
72.11: May all kings bow down to him and all nations serve him.
72.12: For he will deliver the needy who cry out and the afflicted who have no helper.
72.13: He will take pity on the poor and needy and save the lives of the oppressed.
72.14: He will redeem them from oppression and violence, for their blood is precious in his sight.
72.15: Long may he live! May gold from Sheba be given him. May people ever pray for him; may they bless him all day long.
72.16: May there be an abundance of grain in the land; may it sway atop the hills. May its fruit trees flourish like the forests of Lebanon, the people of its cities like the grass of the field.
72.17: May his name endure forever; may his name continue as long as the sun shines. In him may all nations be blessed; may they call him blessed.
72.18: Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who alone does marvelous deeds.
72.19: And blessed be His glorious name forever; may all the earth be filled with His glory. Amen and amen.
72.20: Thus conclude the prayers of David son of Jesse.

73.1: A Psalm of Asaph.Surely God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart.
73.2: But as for me, my feet had almost stumbled; my steps had nearly slipped.
73.3: For I envied the arrogant when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.
73.4: They have no struggle in their death; their bodies are well-fed.
73.5: They are free of the burdens others carry; they are not afflicted like other men.
73.6: Therefore pride is their necklace; a garment of violence covers them.
73.7: From their prosperity proceeds iniquity; the imaginations of their hearts run wild.
73.8: They mock and speak with malice; with arrogance they threaten oppression.
73.9: They set their mouths against the heavens, and their tongues strut across the earth.
73.10: So their people return to this place and drink up waters in abundance.
73.11: The wicked say, “How can God know? Does the Most High have knowledge?”
73.12: Behold, these are the wicked— always carefree as they increase their wealth.
73.13: Surely in vain I have kept my heart pure; in innocence I have washed my hands.
73.14: For I am afflicted all day long and punished every morning.
73.15: If I had said, “I will speak this way,” then I would have betrayed Your children.
73.16: When I tried to understand all this, it was troublesome in my sight
73.17: until I entered God’s sanctuary; then I discerned their end.
73.18: Surely You set them on slick ground; You cast them down into ruin.
73.19: How suddenly they are laid waste, completely swept away by terrors!
73.20: Like one waking from a dream, so You, O Lord, awaken and despise their form.
73.21: When my heart was grieved and I was pierced within,
73.22: I was senseless and ignorant; I was a brute beast before You.
73.23: Yet I am always with You; You hold my right hand.
73.24: You guide me with Your counsel, and later receive me in glory.
73.25: Whom have I in heaven but You? And on earth I desire no one besides You.
73.26: My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
73.27: Those far from You will surely perish; You destroy all who are unfaithful to You.
73.28: But as for me, it is good to draw near to God. I have made the Lord GOD my refuge, that I may proclaim all Your works.

74.1: A Maskil of Asaph.Why have You rejected us forever, O God? Why does Your anger smolder against the sheep of Your pasture?
74.2: Remember Your congregation, which You purchased long ago and redeemed as the tribe of Your inheritance— Mount Zion, where You dwell.
74.3: Turn Your steps to the everlasting ruins, to everything in the sanctuary the enemy has destroyed.
74.4: Your foes have roared within Your meeting place; they have unfurled their banners as signs,
74.5: like men wielding axes in a thicket of trees
74.6: and smashing all the carvings with hatchets and picks.
74.7: They have burned Your sanctuary to the ground; they have defiled the dwelling place of Your Name.
74.8: They said in their hearts, “We will crush them completely.” They burned down every place where God met us in the land.
74.9: There are no signs for us to see. There is no longer any prophet. And none of us knows how long this will last.
74.10: How long, O God, will the enemy taunt You? Will the foe revile Your name forever?
74.11: Why do You withdraw Your strong right hand? Stretch it out to destroy them!
74.12: Yet God is my King from ancient times, working salvation on the earth.
74.13: You divided the sea by Your strength; You smashed the heads of the dragons of the sea;
74.14: You crushed the heads of Leviathan; You fed him to the creatures of the desert.
74.15: You broke open the fountain and the flood; You dried up the ever-flowing rivers.
74.16: The day is Yours, and also the night; You established the moon and the sun.
74.17: You set all the boundaries of the earth; You made the summer and winter.
74.18: Remember how the enemy has mocked You, O LORD, how a foolish people has spurned Your name.
74.19: Do not deliver the soul of Your dove to beasts; do not forget the lives of Your afflicted forever.
74.20: Consider Your covenant, for haunts of violence fill the dark places of the land.
74.21: Do not let the oppressed retreat in shame; may the poor and needy praise Your name.
74.22: Rise up, O God; defend Your cause! Remember how the fool mocks You all day long.
74.23: Do not disregard the clamor of Your adversaries, the uproar of Your enemies that ascends continually.

75.1: For the choirmaster: To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Psalm of Asaph. A song.We give thanks to You, O God; we give thanks, for Your Name is near. The people declare Your wondrous works.
75.2: “When I choose a time, I will judge fairly.
75.3: When the earth and all its dwellers quake, it is I who bear up its pillars. Selah
75.4: I say to the proud, ‘Do not boast,’ and to the wicked, ‘Do not lift up your horn.
75.5: Do not lift up your horn against heaven or speak with an outstretched neck.’”
75.6: For exaltation comes neither from east nor west, nor out of the desert,
75.7: but it is God who judges; He brings down one and exalts another.
75.8: For a cup is in the hand of the LORD, full of foaming wine mixed with spices. He pours from His cup, and all the wicked of the earth drink it down to the dregs.
75.9: But I will proclaim Him forever; I will sing praise to the God of Jacob.
75.10: “All the horns of the wicked I will cut off, but the horns of the righteous will be exalted.”

76.1: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Psalm of Asaph. A song.God is known in Judah; His name is great in Israel.
76.2: His tent is in Salem, His dwelling place in Zion.
76.3: There He shattered the flaming arrows, the shield and sword and weapons of war. Selah
76.4: You are resplendent with light, more majestic than mountains filled with game.
76.5: The valiant lie plundered; they sleep their last sleep. No men of might could lift a hand.
76.6: At Your rebuke, O God of Jacob, both horse and rider lie stunned.
76.7: You alone are to be feared. When You are angry, who can stand before You?
76.8: From heaven You pronounced judgment, and the earth feared and was still
76.9: when God rose up to judge, to save all the lowly of the earth. Selah
76.10: Even the wrath of man shall praise You; with the survivors of wrath You will clothe Yourself.
76.11: Make and fulfill your vows to the LORD your God; let all the neighboring lands bring tribute to Him who is to be feared.
76.12: He breaks the spirits of princes; He is feared by the kings of the earth.

77.1: For the choirmaster. According to Jeduthun. A Psalm of Asaph.I cried out to God; I cried aloud to God to hear me.
77.2: In the day of trouble I sought the Lord; through the night my outstretched hands did not grow weary; my soul refused to be comforted.
77.3: I remembered You, O God, and I groaned; I mused and my spirit grew faint. Selah
77.4: You have kept my eyes from closing; I am too troubled to speak.
77.5: I considered the days of old, the years long in the past.
77.6: At night I remembered my song; in my heart I mused, and my spirit pondered:
77.7: “Will the Lord spurn us forever and never show His favor again?
77.8: Is His loving devotion gone forever? Has His promise failed for all time?
77.9: Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has His anger shut off His compassion?” Selah
77.10: So I said, “I am grieved that the right hand of the Most High has changed.”
77.11: I will remember the works of the LORD; yes, I will remember Your wonders of old.
77.12: I will reflect on all You have done and ponder Your mighty deeds.
77.13: Your way, O God, is holy. What god is so great as our God?
77.14: You are the God who works wonders; You display Your strength among the peoples.
77.15: With power You redeemed Your people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah
77.16: The waters saw You, O God; the waters saw You and swirled; even the depths were shaken.
77.17: The clouds poured down water; the skies resounded with thunder; Your arrows flashed back and forth.
77.18: Your thunder resounded in the whirlwind; the lightning lit up the world; the earth trembled and quaked.
77.19: Your path led through the sea, Your way through the mighty waters, but Your footprints were not to be found.
77.20: You led Your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

78.1: A Maskil of Asaph.Give ear, O my people, to my instruction; listen to the words of my mouth.
78.2: I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the beginning,
78.3: that we have heard and known and our fathers have relayed to us.
78.4: We will not hide them from their children but will declare to the next generation the praises of the LORD and His might and the wonders He has performed.
78.5: For He established a testimony in Jacob and appointed a law in Israel, which He commanded our fathers to teach to their children,
78.6: that the coming generation would know them— even children yet to be born— to arise and tell their own children
78.7: that they should put their confidence in God, not forgetting His works, but keeping His commandments.
78.8: Then they will not be like their fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation, whose heart was not loyal, whose spirit was not faithful to God.
78.9: The archers of Ephraim turned back on the day of battle.
78.10: They failed to keep God’s covenant and refused to live by His law.
78.11: They forgot what He had done, the wonders He had shown them.
78.12: He worked wonders before their fathers in the land of Egypt, in the region of Zoan.
78.13: He split the sea and brought them through; He set the waters upright like a wall.
78.14: He led them with a cloud by day and with a light of fire all night.
78.15: He split the rocks in the wilderness and gave them drink as abundant as the seas.
78.16: He brought streams from the stone and made water flow down like rivers.
78.17: But they continued to sin against Him, rebelling in the desert against the Most High.
78.18: They willfully tested God by demanding the food they craved.
78.19: They spoke against God, saying, “Can God really prepare a table in the wilderness?
78.20: When He struck the rock, water gushed out and torrents raged. But can He also give bread or supply His people with meat?”
78.21: Therefore the LORD heard and was filled with wrath; so a fire was kindled against Jacob, and His anger flared against Israel,
78.22: because they did not believe God or rely on His salvation.
78.23: Yet He commanded the clouds above and opened the doors of the heavens.
78.24: He rained down manna for them to eat; He gave them grain from heaven.
78.25: Man ate the bread of angels; He sent them food in abundance.
78.26: He stirred the east wind from the heavens and drove the south wind by His might.
78.27: He rained meat on them like dust, and winged birds like the sand of the sea.
78.28: He felled them in the midst of their camp, all around their dwellings.
78.29: So they ate and were well filled, for He gave them what they craved.
78.30: Yet before they had filled their desire, with the food still in their mouths,
78.31: God’s anger flared against them, and He put to death their strongest and subdued the young men of Israel.
78.32: In spite of all this, they kept on sinning; despite His wonderful works, they did not believe.
78.33: So He ended their days in futility, and their years in sudden terror.
78.34: When He slew them, they would seek Him; they repented and searched for God.
78.35: And they remembered that God was their Rock, that God Most High was their Redeemer.
78.36: But they deceived Him with their mouths, and lied to Him with their tongues.
78.37: Their hearts were disloyal to Him, and they were unfaithful to His covenant.
78.38: And yet He was compassionate; He forgave their iniquity and did not destroy them. He often restrained His anger and did not unleash His full wrath.
78.39: He remembered that they were but flesh, a passing breeze that does not return.
78.40: How often they disobeyed Him in the wilderness and grieved Him in the desert!
78.41: Again and again they tested God and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
78.42: They did not remember His power — the day He redeemed them from the adversary,
78.43: when He performed His signs in Egypt and His wonders in the fields of Zoan.
78.44: He turned their rivers to blood, and from their streams they could not drink.
78.45: He sent swarms of flies that devoured them, and frogs that devastated them.
78.46: He gave their crops to the grasshopper, the fruit of their labor to the locust.
78.47: He killed their vines with hailstones and their sycamore-figs with sleet.
78.48: He abandoned their cattle to the hail and their livestock to bolts of lightning.
78.49: He unleashed His fury against them, wrath, indignation, and calamity— a band of destroying angels.
78.50: He cleared a path for His anger; He did not spare them from death but delivered their lives to the plague.
78.51: He struck all the firstborn of Egypt, the virility in the tents of Ham.
78.52: He led out His people like sheep and guided them like a flock in the wilderness.
78.53: He led them safely, so they did not fear, but the sea engulfed their enemies.
78.54: He brought them to His holy land, to the mountain His right hand had acquired.
78.55: He drove out nations before them and apportioned their inheritance; He settled the tribes of Israel in their tents.
78.56: But they tested and disobeyed God Most High, for they did not keep His decrees.
78.57: They turned back and were faithless like their fathers, twisted like a faulty bow.
78.58: They enraged Him with their high places and provoked His jealousy with their idols.
78.59: On hearing it, God was furious and rejected Israel completely.
78.60: He abandoned the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent He had pitched among men.
78.61: He delivered His strength to captivity, and His splendor to the hand of the adversary.
78.62: He surrendered His people to the sword because He was enraged by His heritage.
78.63: Fire consumed His young men, and their maidens were left without wedding songs.
78.64: His priests fell by the sword, but their widows could not lament.
78.65: Then the Lord awoke as from sleep, like a mighty warrior overcome by wine.
78.66: He beat back His foes; He put them to everlasting shame.
78.67: He rejected the tent of Joseph and refused the tribe of Ephraim.
78.68: But He chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which He loved.
78.69: He built His sanctuary like the heights, like the earth He has established forever.
78.70: He chose David His servant and took him from the sheepfolds;
78.71: from tending the ewes He brought him to be shepherd of His people Jacob, of Israel His inheritance.
78.72: So David shepherded them with integrity of heart and guided them with skillful hands.

79.1: A Psalm of Asaph.The nations, O God, have invaded Your inheritance; they have defiled Your holy temple and reduced Jerusalem to rubble.
79.2: They have given the corpses of Your servants as food to the birds of the air, the flesh of Your saints to the beasts of the earth.
79.3: They have poured out their blood like water all around Jerusalem, and there is no one to bury the dead.
79.4: We have become a reproach to our neighbors, a scorn and derision to those around us.
79.5: How long, O LORD? Will You be angry forever? Will Your jealousy burn like fire?
79.6: Pour out Your wrath on the nations that do not acknowledge You, on the kingdoms that refuse to call on Your name,
79.7: for they have devoured Jacob and devastated his homeland.
79.8: Do not hold past sins against us; let Your compassion come quickly, for we are brought low.
79.9: Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of Your name; deliver us and atone for our sins, for the sake of Your name.
79.10: Why should the nations ask, “Where is their God?” Before our eyes, make known among the nations Your vengeance for the bloodshed of Your servants.
79.11: May the groans of the captives reach You; by the strength of Your arm preserve those condemned to death.
79.12: Pay back into the laps of our neighbors sevenfold the reproach they hurled at You, O Lord.
79.13: Then we Your people, the sheep of Your pasture, will thank You forever; from generation to generation we will declare Your praise.

80.1: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “The Lilies of the Covenant.” A Psalm of Asaph.Hear us, O Shepherd of Israel, who leads Joseph like a flock; You who sit enthroned between the cherubim, shine forth
80.2: before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh. Rally Your mighty power and come to save us.
80.3: Restore us, O God, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.
80.4: O LORD God of Hosts, how long will Your anger smolder against the prayers of Your people?
80.5: You fed them with the bread of tears and made them drink the full measure of their tears.
80.6: You make us contend with our neighbors; our enemies mock us.
80.7: Restore us, O God of Hosts, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.
80.8: You uprooted a vine from Egypt; You drove out the nations and transplanted it.
80.9: You cleared the ground for it, and it took root and filled the land.
80.10: The mountains were covered by its shade, and the mighty cedars with its branches.
80.11: It sent out its branches to the Sea, and its shoots toward the River.
80.12: Why have You broken down its walls, so that all who pass by pick its fruit?
80.13: The boar from the forest ravages it, and the creatures of the field feed upon it.
80.14: Return, O God of Hosts, we pray! Look down from heaven and see! Attend to this vine—
80.15: the root Your right hand has planted, the son You have raised up for Yourself.
80.16: Your vine has been cut down and burned; they perish at the rebuke of Your countenance.
80.17: Let Your hand be upon the man at Your right hand, on the son of man You have raised up for Yourself.
80.18: Then we will not turn away from You; revive us, and we will call on Your name.
80.19: Restore us, O LORD God of Hosts; cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.

81.1: For the choirmaster. According to Gittith. Of Asaph.Sing for joy to God our strength; make a joyful noise to the God of Jacob.
81.2: Lift up a song, strike the tambourine, play the sweet-sounding harp and lyre.
81.3: Sound the ram’s horn at the New Moon, and at the full moon on the day of our Feast.
81.4: For this is a statute for Israel, an ordinance of the God of Jacob.
81.5: He ordained it as a testimony for Joseph when he went out over the land of Egypt, where I heard an unfamiliar language:
81.6: “I relieved his shoulder of the burden; his hands were freed from the basket.
81.7: You called out in distress, and I rescued you; I answered you from the cloud of thunder; I tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah
81.8: Hear, O My people, and I will warn you: O Israel, if only you would listen to Me!
81.9: There must be no strange god among you, nor shall you bow to a foreign god.
81.10: I am the LORD your God, who brought you up out of Egypt. Open wide your mouth, and I will fill it.
81.11: But My people would not listen to Me, and Israel would not obey Me.
81.12: So I gave them up to their stubborn hearts to follow their own devices.
81.13: If only My people would listen to Me, if Israel would follow My ways,
81.14: how soon I would subdue their enemies and turn My hand against their foes!
81.15: Those who hate the LORD would feign obedience, and their doom would last forever.
81.16: But I would feed you the finest wheat; with honey from the rock I would satisfy you.”

82.1: A Psalm of Asaph.God presides in the divine assembly; He renders judgment among the gods:
82.2: “How long will you judge unjustly and show partiality to the wicked? Selah
82.3: Defend the cause of the weak and fatherless; uphold the rights of the afflicted and oppressed.
82.4: Rescue the weak and needy; save them from the hand of the wicked.
82.5: They do not know or understand; they wander in the darkness; all the foundations of the earth are shaken.
82.6: I have said, ‘You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High.’
82.7: But like mortals you will die, and like rulers you will fall.”
82.8: Arise, O God, judge the earth, for all the nations are Your inheritance.

83.1: A song. A Psalm of Asaph.O God, be not silent; be not speechless; be not still, O God.
83.2: See how Your enemies rage, how Your foes have reared their heads.
83.3: With cunning they scheme against Your people and conspire against those You cherish,
83.4: saying, “Come, let us erase them as a nation; may the name of Israel be remembered no more.”
83.5: For with one mind they plot together; they form an alliance against You—
83.6: the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, of Moab and the Hagrites,
83.7: of Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek, of Philistia with the people of Tyre.
83.8: Even Assyria has joined them, lending strength to the sons of Lot. Selah
83.9: Do to them as You did to Midian, as to Sisera and Jabin at the River Kishon,
83.10: who perished at Endor and became like dung on the ground.
83.11: Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, and all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,
83.12: who said, “Let us possess for ourselves the pastures of God.”
83.13: Make them like tumbleweed, O my God, like chaff before the wind.
83.14: As fire consumes a forest, as a flame sets the mountains ablaze,
83.15: so pursue them with Your tempest, and terrify them with Your storm.
83.16: Cover their faces with shame, that they may seek Your name, O LORD.
83.17: May they be ever ashamed and terrified; may they perish in disgrace.
83.18: May they know that You alone, whose name is the LORD, are Most High over all the earth.

84.1: For the choirmaster. According to Gittith. A Psalm of the sons of Korah.How lovely is Your dwelling place, O LORD of Hosts!
84.2: My soul longs, even faints, for the courts of the LORD; my heart and my flesh cry out for the living God.
84.3: Even the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she places her young near Your altars, O LORD of Hosts, my King and my God.
84.4: How blessed are those who dwell in Your house! They are ever praising You. Selah
84.5: Blessed are those whose strength is in You, whose hearts are set on pilgrimage.
84.6: As they pass through the Valley of Baca, they make it a place of springs; even the autumn rain covers it with pools.
84.7: They go from strength to strength, until each appears before God in Zion.
84.8: O LORD God of Hosts, hear my prayer; give ear, O God of Jacob. Selah
84.9: Take notice of our shield, O God, and look with favor on the face of Your anointed.
84.10: For better is one day in Your courts than a thousand elsewhere. I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God than dwell in the tents of the wicked.
84.11: For the LORD God is a sun and a shield; the LORD gives grace and glory; He withholds no good thing from those who walk with integrity.
84.12: O LORD of Hosts, how blessed is the man who trusts in You!

85.1: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of the sons of Korah.You showed favor to Your land, O LORD; You restored Jacob from captivity.
85.2: You forgave the iniquity of Your people; You covered all their sin. Selah
85.3: You withheld all Your fury; You turned from Your burning anger.
85.4: Restore us, O God of our salvation, and put away Your displeasure toward us.
85.5: Will You be angry with us forever? Will You draw out Your anger to all generations?
85.6: Will You not revive us again, that Your people may rejoice in You?
85.7: Show us Your loving devotion, O LORD, and grant us Your salvation.
85.8: I will listen to what God the LORD will say; for He will surely speak peace to His people and His saints; He will not let them return to folly.
85.9: Surely His salvation is near to those who fear Him, that His glory may dwell in our land.
85.10: Loving devotion and faithfulness have joined together; righteousness and peace have kissed.
85.11: Faithfulness sprouts from the earth, and righteousness looks down from heaven.
85.12: The LORD will indeed provide what is good, and our land will yield its increase.
85.13: Righteousness will go before Him to prepare the way for His steps.

86.1: A prayer of David.Incline Your ear, O LORD, and answer me, for I am poor and needy.
86.2: Preserve my soul, for I am godly. You are my God; save Your servant who trusts in You.
86.3: Be merciful to me, O Lord, for I call to You all day long.
86.4: Bring joy to Your servant, for to You, O Lord, I lift up my soul.
86.5: For You, O Lord, are kind and forgiving, rich in loving devotion to all who call on You.
86.6: Hear my prayer, O LORD, and attend to my plea for mercy.
86.7: In the day of my distress I call on You, because You answer me.
86.8: O Lord, there is none like You among the gods, nor any works like Yours.
86.9: All the nations You have made will come and bow before You, O Lord, and they will glorify Your name.
86.10: For You are great and perform wonders; You alone are God.
86.11: Teach me Your way, O LORD, that I may walk in Your truth. Give me an undivided heart, that I may fear Your name.
86.12: I will praise You, O Lord my God, with all my heart; I will glorify Your name forever.
86.13: For great is Your loving devotion to me; You have delivered me from the depths of Sheol.
86.14: The arrogant rise against me, O God; a band of ruthless men seeks my life; they have no regard for You.
86.15: But You, O Lord, are a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion and faithfulness.
86.16: Turn to me and have mercy; grant Your strength to Your servant; save the son of Your maidservant.
86.17: Show me a sign of Your goodness, that my enemies may see and be ashamed; for You, O LORD, have helped me and comforted me.

87.1: A Psalm of the sons of Korah. A song.He has founded His city on the holy mountains.
87.2: The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
87.3: Glorious things are ascribed to you, O city of God. Selah
87.4: “I will mention Rahab and Babylon among those who know Me— along with Philistia, Tyre, and Cush — when I say, ‘This one was born in Zion.’”
87.5: And it will be said of Zion: “This one and that one were born in her, and the Most High Himself will establish her.”
87.6: The LORD will record in the register of the peoples: “This one was born in Zion.” Selah
87.7: Singers and pipers will proclaim, “All my springs of joy are in You.”

88.1: A song. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. For the choirmaster. According to Mahalath Leannoth. A Maskil of Heman the Ezrahite.O LORD, the God of my salvation, day and night I cry out before You.
88.2: May my prayer come before You; incline Your ear to my cry.
88.3: For my soul is full of troubles, and my life draws near to Sheol.
88.4: I am counted among those descending to the Pit. I am like a man without strength.
88.5: I am forsaken among the dead, like the slain who lie in the grave, whom You remember no more, who are cut off from Your care.
88.6: You have laid me in the lowest Pit, in the darkest of the depths.
88.7: Your wrath weighs heavily upon me; all Your waves have submerged me. Selah
88.8: You have removed my friends from me; You have made me repulsive to them; I am confined and cannot escape.
88.9: My eyes grow dim with grief. I call to You daily, O LORD; I spread out my hands to You.
88.10: Do You work wonders for the dead? Do departed spirits rise up to praise You? Selah
88.11: Can Your loving devotion be proclaimed in the grave, Your faithfulness in Abaddon ?
88.12: Will Your wonders be known in the darkness, or Your righteousness in the land of oblivion?
88.13: But to You, O LORD, I cry for help; in the morning my prayer comes before You.
88.14: Why, O LORD, do You reject me? Why do You hide Your face from me?
88.15: From my youth I was afflicted and near death. I have borne Your terrors; I am in despair.
88.16: Your wrath has swept over me; Your terrors have destroyed me.
88.17: All day long they engulf me like water; they enclose me on every side.
88.18: You have removed my beloved and my friend; darkness is my closest companion.

89.1: A Maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite.I will sing of the loving devotion of the LORD forever; with my mouth I will proclaim Your faithfulness to all generations.
89.2: For I have said, “Loving devotion is built up forever; in the heavens You establish Your faithfulness.”
89.3: You said, “I have made a covenant with My chosen one, I have sworn to David My servant:
89.4: ‘I will establish your offspring forever and build up your throne for all generations.’” Selah
89.5: The heavens praise Your wonders, O LORD— Your faithfulness as well— in the assembly of the holy ones.
89.6: For who in the skies can compare with the LORD? Who among the heavenly beings is like the LORD?
89.7: In the council of the holy ones, God is greatly feared, and awesome above all who surround Him.
89.8: O LORD God of Hosts, who is like You? O mighty LORD, Your faithfulness surrounds You.
89.9: You rule the raging sea; when its waves mount up, You still them.
89.10: You crushed Rahab like a carcass; You scattered Your enemies with Your mighty arm.
89.11: The heavens are Yours, and also the earth. The earth and its fullness You founded.
89.12: North and south You created; Tabor and Hermon shout for joy at Your name.
89.13: Mighty is Your arm; strong is Your hand. Your right hand is exalted.
89.14: Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne; loving devotion and faithfulness go before You.
89.15: Blessed are those who know the joyful sound, who walk, O LORD, in the light of Your presence.
89.16: They rejoice in Your name all day long, and in Your righteousness they exult.
89.17: For You are the glory of their strength, and by Your favor our horn is exalted.
89.18: Surely our shield belongs to the LORD, and our king to the Holy One of Israel.
89.19: You once spoke in a vision; to Your godly ones You said, “I have bestowed help on a warrior; I have exalted one chosen from the people.
89.20: I have found My servant David; with My sacred oil I have anointed him.
89.21: My hand will sustain him; surely My arm will strengthen him.
89.22: No enemy will exact tribute; no wicked man will oppress him.
89.23: I will crush his foes before him and strike down those who hate him.
89.24: My faithfulness and loving devotion will be with him, and through My name his horn will be exalted.
89.25: I will set his hand over the sea, and his right hand upon the rivers.
89.26: He will call to Me, ‘You are my Father, my God, the Rock of my salvation.’
89.27: I will indeed appoint him as My firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth.
89.28: I will forever preserve My loving devotion for him, and My covenant with him will stand fast.
89.29: I will establish his line forever, his throne as long as the heavens endure.
89.30: If his sons forsake My law and do not walk in My judgments,
89.31: if they violate My statutes and fail to keep My commandments,
89.32: I will attend to their transgression with the rod, and to their iniquity with stripes.
89.33: But I will not withdraw My loving devotion from him, nor ever betray My faithfulness.
89.34: I will not violate My covenant or alter the utterance of My lips.
89.35: Once and for all I have sworn by My holiness— I will not lie to David—
89.36: his offspring shall endure forever, and his throne before Me like the sun,
89.37: like the moon, established forever, a faithful witness in the sky.” Selah
89.38: Now, however, You have spurned and rejected him; You are enraged by Your anointed one.
89.39: You have renounced the covenant with Your servant and sullied his crown in the dust.
89.40: You have broken down all his walls; You have reduced his strongholds to rubble.
89.41: All who pass by plunder him; he has become a reproach to his neighbors.
89.42: You have exalted the right hand of his foes; You have made all his enemies rejoice.
89.43: You have bent the edge of his sword and have not sustained him in battle.
89.44: You have ended his splendor and cast his throne to the ground.
89.45: You have cut short the days of his youth; You have covered him with shame. Selah
89.46: How long, O LORD? Will You hide Yourself forever? Will Your wrath keep burning like fire?
89.47: Remember the briefness of my lifespan! For what futility You have created all men!
89.48: What man can live and never see death? Can he deliver his soul from the power of Sheol? Selah
89.49: Where, O Lord, is Your loving devotion of old, which You faithfully swore to David?
89.50: Remember, O Lord, the reproach of Your servants, which I bear in my heart from so many people—
89.51: how Your enemies have taunted, O LORD, and have mocked every step of Your anointed one!
89.52: Blessed be the LORD forever! Amen and amen.

90.1: A prayer of Moses the man of God.Lord, You have been our dwelling place through all generations.
90.2: Before the mountains were born or You brought forth the earth and the world, from everlasting to everlasting You are God.
90.3: You return man to dust, saying, “Return, O sons of mortals.”
90.4: For in Your sight a thousand years are but a day that passes, or a watch of the night.
90.5: You sweep them away in their sleep; they are like the new grass of the morning—
90.6: in the morning it springs up new, but by evening it fades and withers.
90.7: For we are consumed by Your anger and terrified by Your wrath.
90.8: You have set our iniquities before You, our secret sins in the light of Your presence.
90.9: For all our days decline in Your fury; we finish our years with a sigh.
90.10: The length of our days is seventy years— or eighty if we are strong— yet their pride is but labor and sorrow, for they quickly pass, and we fly away.
90.11: Who knows the power of Your anger? Your wrath matches the fear You are due.
90.12: So teach us to number our days, that we may present a heart of wisdom.
90.13: Return, O LORD! How long will it be? Have compassion on Your servants.
90.14: Satisfy us in the morning with Your loving devotion, that we may sing for joy and be glad all our days.
90.15: Make us glad for as many days as You have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen evil.
90.16: May Your work be shown to Your servants, and Your splendor to their children.
90.17: May the favor of the Lord our God rest upon us; establish for us the work of our hands— yes, establish the work of our hands!

91.1: He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High will abide in the shadow of the Almighty.
91.2: I will say to the LORD, “You are my refuge and my fortress, my God, in whom I trust.”
91.3: Surely He will deliver you from the snare of the fowler, and from the deadly plague.
91.4: He will cover you with His feathers; under His wings you will find refuge; His faithfulness is a shield and rampart.
91.5: You will not fear the terror of the night, nor the arrow that flies by day,
91.6: nor the pestilence that stalks in the darkness, nor the calamity that destroys at noon.
91.7: Though a thousand may fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right hand, no harm will come near you.
91.8: You will only see it with your eyes and witness the punishment of the wicked.
91.9: Because you have made the LORD your dwelling— my refuge, the Most High—
91.10: no evil will befall you, no plague will approach your tent.
91.11: For He will command His angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways.
91.12: They will lift you up in their hands, so that you will not strike your foot against a stone.
91.13: You will tread on the lion and cobra; you will trample the young lion and serpent.
91.14: “Because he loves Me, I will deliver him; because he knows My name, I will protect him.
91.15: When he calls out to Me, I will answer him; I will be with him in trouble. I will deliver him and honor him.
91.16: With long life I will satisfy him and show him My salvation.”

92.1: A Psalm. A song for the Sabbath day.It is good to praise the LORD, and to sing praises to Your name, O Most High,
92.2: to proclaim Your loving devotion in the morning and Your faithfulness at night
92.3: with the ten-stringed harp and the melody of the lyre.
92.4: For You, O LORD, have made me glad by Your deeds; I sing for joy at the works of Your hands.
92.5: How great are Your works, O LORD, how deep are Your thoughts!
92.6: A senseless man does not know, and a fool does not understand,
92.7: that though the wicked sprout like grass, and all evildoers flourish, they will be forever destroyed.
92.8: But You, O LORD, are exalted forever!
92.9: For surely Your enemies, O LORD, surely Your enemies will perish; all evildoers will be scattered.
92.10: But You have exalted my horn like that of a wild ox; with fine oil I have been anointed.
92.11: My eyes see the downfall of my enemies; my ears hear the wailing of my wicked foes.
92.12: The righteous will flourish like a palm tree, and grow like a cedar in Lebanon.
92.13: Planted in the house of the LORD, they will flourish in the courts of our God.
92.14: In old age they will still bear fruit; healthy and green they will remain,
92.15: to proclaim, “The LORD is upright; He is my Rock, and in Him there is no unrighteousness.”

93.1: The LORD reigns! He is robed in majesty; the LORD has clothed and armed Himself with strength. The world indeed is firmly established; it cannot be moved.
93.2: Your throne was established long ago; You are from all eternity.
93.3: The floodwaters have risen, O LORD; the rivers have raised their voice; the seas lift up their pounding waves.
93.4: Above the roar of many waters— the mighty breakers of the sea— the LORD on high is majestic.
93.5: Your testimonies are fully confirmed; holiness adorns Your house, O LORD, for all the days to come.

94.1: O LORD, God of vengeance, O God of vengeance, shine forth.
94.2: Rise up, O Judge of the earth; render a reward to the proud.
94.3: How long will the wicked, O LORD, how long will the wicked exult?
94.4: They pour out arrogant words; all workers of iniquity boast.
94.5: They crush Your people, O LORD; they oppress Your heritage.
94.6: They kill the widow and the foreigner; they murder the fatherless.
94.7: They say, “The LORD does not see; the God of Jacob pays no heed.”
94.8: Take notice, O senseless among the people! O fools, when will you be wise?
94.9: He who affixed the ear, can He not hear? He who formed the eye, can He not see?
94.10: He who admonishes the nations, does He not discipline? He who teaches man, does He lack knowledge?
94.11: The LORD knows the thoughts of man, that they are futile.
94.12: Blessed is the man You discipline, O LORD, and teach from Your law,
94.13: to grant him relief from days of trouble, until a pit is dug for the wicked.
94.14: For the LORD will not forsake His people; He will never abandon His heritage.
94.15: Surely judgment will again be righteous, and all the upright in heart will follow it.
94.16: Who will rise up for me against the wicked? Who will stand for me against the workers of iniquity?
94.17: Unless the LORD had been my helper, I would soon have dwelt in the abode of silence.
94.18: If I say, “My foot is slipping,” Your loving devotion, O LORD, supports me.
94.19: When anxiety overwhelms me, Your consolation delights my soul.
94.20: Can a corrupt throne be Your ally— one devising mischief by decree?
94.21: They band together against the righteous and condemn the innocent to death.
94.22: But the LORD has been my stronghold, and my God is my rock of refuge.
94.23: He will bring upon them their own iniquity and destroy them for their wickedness. The LORD our God will destroy them.

95.1: Come, let us sing for joy to the LORD; let us shout to the Rock of our salvation!
95.2: Let us enter His presence with thanksgiving; let us make a joyful noise to Him in song.
95.3: For the LORD is a great God, a great King above all gods.
95.4: In His hand are the depths of the earth, and the mountain peaks belong to Him.
95.5: The sea is His, for He made it, and His hands formed the dry land.
95.6: O come, let us worship and bow down; let us kneel before the LORD our Maker.
95.7: For He is our God, and we are the people of His pasture, the sheep under His care. Today, if you hear His voice,
95.8: do not harden your hearts as you did at Meribah, in the day at Massah in the wilderness,
95.9: where your fathers tested and tried Me, though they had seen My work.
95.10: For forty years I was angry with that generation, and I said, “They are a people whose hearts go astray, and they have not known My ways.”
95.11: So I swore on oath in My anger, “They shall never enter My rest.”

96.1: Sing to the LORD a new song; sing to the LORD, all the earth.
96.2: Sing to the LORD, bless His name; proclaim His salvation day after day.
96.3: Declare His glory among the nations, His wonders among all peoples.
96.4: For great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; He is to be feared above all gods.
96.5: For all the gods of the nations are idols, but it is the LORD who made the heavens.
96.6: Splendor and majesty are before Him; strength and beauty fill His sanctuary.
96.7: Ascribe to the LORD, O families of the nations, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
96.8: Ascribe to the LORD the glory due His name; bring an offering and enter His courts.
96.9: Worship the LORD in the splendor of His holiness; tremble before Him, all the earth.
96.10: Declare among the nations: “The LORD reigns!” The world is firmly established; it cannot be moved; He will judge the peoples with equity.
96.11: Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice; let the sea resound, and all that fills it.
96.12: Let the fields exult, and all that is in them. Then all the trees of the forest will sing for joy
96.13: before the LORD, for He is coming— He is coming to judge the earth. He will judge the world in righteousness and the peoples in His faithfulness.

97.1: The LORD reigns, let the earth rejoice; let the distant shores be glad.
97.2: Clouds and darkness surround Him; righteousness and justice are His throne’s foundation.
97.3: Fire goes before Him and consumes His foes on every side.
97.4: His lightning illuminates the world; the earth sees and trembles.
97.5: The mountains melt like wax at the presence of the LORD, before the Lord of all the earth.
97.6: The heavens proclaim His righteousness; all the peoples see His glory.
97.7: All worshipers of images are put to shame— those who boast in idols. Worship Him, all you gods!
97.8: Zion hears and rejoices, and the towns of Judah exult because of Your judgments, O LORD.
97.9: For You, O LORD, are Most High over all the earth; You are exalted far above all gods.
97.10: Hate evil, O you who love the LORD! He preserves the souls of His saints; He delivers them from the hand of the wicked.
97.11: Light shines on the righteous, gladness on the upright in heart.
97.12: Rejoice in the LORD, you righteous ones, and praise His holy name.

98.1: A Psalm.Sing to the LORD a new song, for He has done wonders; His right hand and holy arm have gained Him the victory.
98.2: The LORD has proclaimed His salvation and revealed His righteousness to the nations.
98.3: He has remembered His love and faithfulness to the house of Israel; all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
98.4: Make a joyful noise to the LORD, all the earth; break forth—let your cry ring out, and sing praises!
98.5: Sing praises to the LORD with the lyre, in melodious song with the harp.
98.6: With trumpets and the blast of the ram’s horn shout for joy before the LORD, the King.
98.7: Let the sea resound, and all that fills it, the world, and all who dwell in it.
98.8: Let the rivers clap their hands, let the mountains sing together for joy
98.9: before the LORD, for He comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with equity.

99.1: The LORD reigns; let the nations tremble! He is enthroned above the cherubim; let the earth quake!
99.2: Great is the LORD in Zion; He is exalted above all the peoples.
99.3: Let them praise Your great and awesome name— He is holy!
99.4: The mighty King loves justice. You have established equity; You have exercised justice and righteousness in Jacob.
99.5: Exalt the LORD our God, and worship at His footstool; He is holy!
99.6: Moses and Aaron were among His priests; Samuel was among those who called on His name. They called to the LORD and He answered.
99.7: He spoke to them from the pillar of cloud; they kept His decrees and the statutes He gave them.
99.8: O LORD our God, You answered them. You were a forgiving God to them, yet an avenger of their misdeeds.
99.9: Exalt the LORD our God and worship at His holy mountain, for the LORD our God is holy.

100.1: A Psalm of thanksgiving.Make a joyful noise to the LORD, all the earth.
100.2: Serve the LORD with gladness; come into His presence with joyful songs.
100.3: Know that the LORD is God. It is He who made us, and we are His; we are His people, and the sheep of His pasture.
100.4: Enter His gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise; give thanks to Him and bless His name.
100.5: For the LORD is good, and His loving devotion endures forever; His faithfulness continues to all generations.

101.1: A Psalm of David.I will sing of Your loving devotion and justice; to You, O LORD, I will sing praises.
101.2: I will ponder the way that is blameless— when will You come to me? I will walk in my house with integrity of heart.
101.3: I will set no worthless thing before my eyes. I hate the work of those who fall away; it shall not cling to me.
101.4: A perverse heart shall depart from me; I will know nothing of evil.
101.5: Whoever slanders his neighbor in secret, I will put to silence; the one with haughty eyes and a proud heart, I will not endure.
101.6: My eyes favor the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with me; he who walks in the way of integrity shall minister to me.
101.7: No one who practices deceit shall dwell in my house; no one who tells lies shall stand in my presence.
101.8: Every morning I will remove all the wicked of the land, that I may cut off every evildoer from the city of the LORD.

102.1: A prayer of one who is afflicted, when he grows faint and pours out his lament before the LORD.Hear my prayer, O LORD; let my cry for help come before You.
102.2: Do not hide Your face from me in my day of distress. Incline Your ear to me; answer me quickly when I call.
102.3: For my days vanish like smoke, and my bones burn like glowing embers.
102.4: My heart is afflicted, and withered like grass; I even forget to eat my bread.
102.5: Through my loud groaning my skin hangs on my bones.
102.6: I am like a desert owl, like an owl among the ruins.
102.7: I lie awake; I am like a lone bird on a housetop.
102.8: All day long my enemies taunt me; they ridicule me and curse me.
102.9: For I have eaten ashes like bread and mixed my drink with tears
102.10: because of Your indignation and wrath, for You have picked me up and cast me aside.
102.11: My days are like lengthening shadows, and I wither away like grass.
102.12: But You, O LORD, sit enthroned forever; Your renown endures to all generations.
102.13: You will rise up and have compassion on Zion, for it is time to show her favor— the appointed time has come.
102.14: For Your servants delight in her stones and take pity on her dust.
102.15: So the nations will fear the name of the LORD, and all the kings of the earth will fear Your glory.
102.16: For the LORD will rebuild Zion; He has appeared in His glory.
102.17: He will turn toward the prayer of the destitute; He will not despise their prayer.
102.18: Let this be written for the generation to come, so that a people not yet created may praise the LORD.
102.19: For He looked down from the heights of His sanctuary; the LORD gazed out from heaven to earth
102.20: to hear a prisoner’s groaning, to release those condemned to death,
102.21: that they may proclaim the name of the LORD in Zion and praise Him in Jerusalem,
102.22: when peoples and kingdoms assemble to serve the LORD.
102.23: He has broken my strength on the way; He has cut short my days.
102.24: I say: “O my God, do not take me in the midst of my days! Your years go on through all generations.
102.25: In the beginning You laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of Your hands.
102.26: They will perish, but You remain; they will all wear out like a garment. Like clothing You will change them, and they will be passed on.
102.27: But You remain the same, and Your years will never end.
102.28: The children of Your servants will dwell securely, and their descendants will be established before You.”

103.1: Of David.Bless the LORD, O my soul; all that is within me, bless His holy name.
103.2: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and do not forget all His kind deeds—
103.3: He who forgives all your iniquities and heals all your diseases,
103.4: who redeems your life from the Pit and crowns you with loving devotion and compassion,
103.5: who satisfies you with good things, so that your youth is renewed like the eagle’s.
