1.5: Therefore the wicked will not stand up in the judgment, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous.
1.6: For the LORD watches over the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked leads to ruin.

2.1: Why do the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain?
2.2: The kings of the earth take their stand, and the rulers conspire together against the LORD and his Anointed One:
2.3: “Let’s tear off their chains and throw their ropes off of us.”
2.4: The one enthroned in heaven laughs; the Lord ridicules them.
2.5: Then he speaks to them in his anger and terrifies them in his wrath:
2.6: “I have installed my king on Zion, my holy mountain.”
2.7: I will declare the LORD’s decree. He said to me, “You are my Son; today I have become your Father.
2.8: Ask of me, and I will make the nations your inheritance and the ends of the earth your possession.
2.9: You will break them with an iron scepter; you will shatter them like pottery.”
2.10: So now, kings, be wise; receive instruction, you judges of the earth.
2.11: Serve the LORD with reverential awe and rejoice with trembling.
2.12: Pay homage to the Son or he will be angry and you will perish in your rebellion, for his anger may ignite at any moment. All who take refuge in him are happy.

3.1: A psalm of David when he fled from his son Absalom.LORD, how my foes increase! There are many who attack me.
3.2: Many say about me, “There is no help for him in God.” Selah
3.3: But you, LORD, are a shield around me, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head.
3.4: I cry aloud to the LORD, and he answers me from his holy mountain. Selah
3.5: I lie down and sleep; I wake again because the LORD sustains me.
3.6: I will not be afraid of thousands of people who have taken their stand against me on every side.
3.7: Rise up, LORD! Save me, my God! You strike all my enemies on the cheek; you break the teeth of the wicked.
3.8: Salvation belongs to the LORD; may your blessing be on your people. Selah

4.1: For the choir director: with stringed instruments. A psalm of David.Answer me when I call, God, who vindicates me. You freed me from affliction; be gracious to me and hear my prayer.
4.2: How long, exalted ones, will my honor be insulted? How long will you love what is worthless and pursue a lie? Selah
4.3: Know that the LORD has set apart the faithful for himself; the LORD will hear when I call to him.
4.4: Be angry and do not sin; on your bed, reflect in your heart and be still. Selah
4.5: Offer sacrifices in righteousness and trust in the LORD.
4.6: Many are asking, “Who can show us anything good?” Let the light of your face shine on us, LORD.
4.7: You have put more joy in my heart than they have when their grain and new wine abound.
4.8: I will both lie down and sleep in peace, for you alone, LORD, make me live in safety.

5.1: For the choir director: with the flutes. A psalm of David.Listen to my words, LORD; consider my sighing.
5.2: Pay attention to the sound of my cry, my King and my God, for I pray to you.
5.3: In the morning, LORD, you hear my voice; in the morning I plead my case to you and watch expectantly.
5.4: For you are not a God who delights in wickedness; evil cannot dwell with you.
5.5: The boastful cannot stand in your sight; you hate all evildoers.
5.6: You destroy those who tell lies; the LORD abhors violent and treacherous people.
5.7: But I enter your house by the abundance of your faithful love; I bow down toward your holy temple in reverential awe of you.
5.8: LORD, lead me in your righteousness because of my adversaries; make your way straight before me.
5.9: For there is nothing reliable in what they say; destruction is within them; their throat is an open grave; they flatter with their tongues.
5.10: Punish them, God; let them fall by their own schemes. Drive them out because of their many crimes, for they rebel against you.
5.11: But let all who take refuge in you rejoice; let them shout for joy forever. May you shelter them, and may those who love your name boast about you.
5.12: For you, LORD, bless the righteous one; you surround him with favor like a shield.

6.1: For the choir director: with stringed instruments, according to . A psalm of David.LORD, do not rebuke me in your anger; do not discipline me in your wrath.
6.2: Be gracious to me, LORD, for I am weak; heal me, LORD, for my bones are shaking;
6.3: my whole being is shaken with terror. And you, LORD — how long?
6.4: Turn, LORD! Rescue me; save me because of your faithful love.
6.5: For there is no remembrance of you in death; who can thank you in Sheol?
6.6: I am weary from my groaning; with my tears I dampen my bed and drench my couch every night.
6.7: My eyes are swollen from grief; they grow old because of all my enemies.
6.8: Depart from me, all evildoers, for the LORD has heard the sound of my weeping.
6.9: The LORD has heard my plea for help; the LORD accepts my prayer.
6.10: All my enemies will be ashamed and shake with terror; they will turn back and suddenly be disgraced.

7.1: A of David, which he sang to the LORD concerning the words of Cush, a Benjaminite.LORD my God, I seek refuge in you; save me from all my pursuers and rescue me
7.2: or they will tear me like a lion, ripping me apart with no one to rescue me.
7.3: LORD my God, if I have done this, if there is injustice on my hands,
7.4: if I have done harm to one at peace with me or have plundered my adversary without cause,
7.5: may an enemy pursue and overtake me; may he trample me to the ground and leave my honor in the dust. Selah
7.6: Rise up, LORD, in your anger; lift yourself up against the fury of my adversaries; awake for me; you have ordained a judgment.
7.7: Let the assembly of peoples gather around you; take your seat on high over it.
7.8: The LORD judges the peoples; vindicate me, LORD, according to my righteousness and my integrity.
7.9: Let the evil of the wicked come to an end, but establish the righteous. The one who examines the thoughts and emotions is a righteous God.
7.10: My shield is with God, who saves the upright in heart.
7.11: God is a righteous judge and a God who shows his wrath every day.
7.12: If anyone does not repent, he will sharpen his sword; he has strung his bow and made it ready.
7.13: He has prepared his deadly weapons; he tips his arrows with fire.
7.14: See, the wicked one is pregnant with evil, conceives trouble, and gives birth to deceit.
7.15: He dug a pit and hollowed it out but fell into the hole he had made.
7.16: His trouble comes back on his own head; his own violence comes down on top of his head.
7.17: I will thank the LORD for his righteousness; I will sing about the name of the LORD Most High.

8.1: For the choir director: on the . A psalm of David.LORD, our Lord, how magnificent is your name throughout the earth! You have covered the heavens with your majesty.
8.2: From the mouths of infants and nursing babies, you have established a stronghold on account of your adversaries in order to silence the enemy and the avenger.
8.3: When I observe your heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars, which you set in place,
8.4: what is a human being that you remember him, a son of man that you look after him?
8.5: You made him little less than God and crowned him with glory and honor.
8.6: You made him ruler over the works of your hands; you put everything under his feet:
8.7: all the sheep and oxen, as well as the animals in the wild,
8.8: the birds of the sky, and the fish of the sea that pass through the currents of the seas.
8.9: LORD, our Lord, how magnificent is your name throughout the earth!

9.1: For the choir director: according to . A psalm of David.I will thank the LORD with all my heart; I will declare all your wondrous works.
9.2: I will rejoice and boast about you; I will sing about your name, Most High.
9.3: When my enemies retreat, they stumble and perish before you.
9.4: For you have upheld my just cause; you are seated on your throne as a righteous judge.
9.5: You have rebuked the nations: You have destroyed the wicked; you have erased their name forever and ever.
9.6: The enemy has come to eternal ruin. You have uprooted the cities, and the very memory of them has perished.
9.7: But the LORD sits enthroned forever; he has established his throne for judgment.
9.8: And he judges the world with righteousness; he executes judgment on the nations with fairness.
9.9: The LORD is a refuge for the persecuted, a refuge in times of trouble.
9.10: Those who know your name trust in you because you have not abandoned those who seek you, LORD.
9.11: Sing to the LORD, who dwells in Zion; proclaim his deeds among the nations.
9.12: For the one who seeks an accounting for bloodshed remembers them; he does not forget the cry of the oppressed.
9.13: Be gracious to me, LORD; consider my affliction at the hands of those who hate me. Lift me up from the gates of death,
9.14: so that I may declare all your praises. I will rejoice in your salvation within the gates of Daughter Zion.
9.15: The nations have fallen into the pit they made; their foot is caught in the net they have concealed.
9.16: The LORD has made himself known; he has executed justice, snaring the wicked by the work of their hands. Higgaion. Selah
9.17: The wicked will return to Sheol — all the nations that forget God.
9.18: For the needy will not always be forgotten; the hope of the oppressed will not perish forever.
9.19: Rise up, LORD! Do not let mere humans prevail; let the nations be judged in your presence.
9.20: Put terror in them, LORD; let the nations know they are only humans. Selah

10.1: LORD, why do you stand so far away? Why do you hide in times of trouble?
10.2: In arrogance the wicked relentlessly pursue their victims; let them be caught in the schemes they have devised.
10.3: For the wicked one boasts about his own cravings; the one who is greedy curses and despises the LORD.
10.4: In all his scheming, the wicked person arrogantly thinks, “There’s no accountability, since there’s no God.”
10.5: His ways are always secure; your lofty judgments have no effect on him; he scoffs at all his adversaries.
10.6: He says to himself, “I will never be moved — from generation to generation without calamity.”
10.7: Cursing, deceit, and violence fill his mouth; trouble and malice are under his tongue.
10.8: He waits in ambush near settlements; he kills the innocent in secret places. His eyes are on the lookout for the helpless;
10.9: he lurks in secret like a lion in a thicket. He lurks in order to seize a victim; he seizes a victim and drags him in his net.
10.10: So he is oppressed and beaten down; helpless people fall because of the wicked one’s strength.
10.11: He says to himself, “God has forgotten; he hides his face and will never see.”
10.12: Rise up, LORD God! Lift up your hand. Do not forget the oppressed.
10.13: Why has the wicked person despised God? He says to himself, “You will not demand an account.”
10.14: But you yourself have seen trouble and grief, observing it in order to take the matter into your hands. The helpless one entrusts himself to you; you are a helper of the fatherless.
10.15: Break the arm of the wicked, evil person, until you look for his wickedness, but it can’t be found.
10.16: The LORD is King forever and ever; the nations will perish from his land.
10.17: LORD, you have heard the desire of the humble; you will strengthen their hearts. You will listen carefully,
10.18: doing justice for the fatherless and the oppressed so that mere humans from the earth may terrify them no more.

11.1: For the choir director. Of David.I have taken refuge in the LORD. How can you say to me, “Escape to the mountains like a bird!
11.2: For look, the wicked string bows; they put their arrows on bowstrings to shoot from the shadows at the upright in heart.
11.3: When the foundations are destroyed, what can the righteous do?”
11.4: The LORD is in his holy temple; the LORD—his throne is in heaven. His eyes watch; his gaze examines everyone.
11.5: The LORD examines the righteous, but he hates the wicked and those who love violence.
11.6: Let him rain burning coals and sulfur on the wicked; let a scorching wind be the portion in their cup.
11.7: For the LORD is righteous; he loves righteous deeds. The upright will see his face.

12.1: For the choir director: according to . A psalm of David.Help, LORD, for no faithful one remains; the loyal have disappeared from the human race.
12.2: They lie to one another; they speak with flattering lips and deceptive hearts.
12.3: May the LORD cut off all flattering lips and the tongue that speaks boastfully.
12.4: They say, “Through our tongues we have power; our lips are our own — who can be our master?”
12.5: “Because of the devastation of the needy and the groaning of the poor, I will now rise up,” says the LORD. “I will provide safety for the one who longs for it.”
12.6: The words of the LORD are pure words, like silver refined in an earthen furnace, purified seven times.
12.7: You, LORD, will guard us; you will protect us from this generation forever.
12.8: The wicked prowl all around, and what is worthless is exalted by the human race.

13.1: For the choir director. A psalm of David.How long, LORD? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me?
13.2: How long will I store up anxious concerns within me, agony in my mind every day? How long will my enemy dominate me?
13.3: Consider me and answer, LORD my God. Restore brightness to my eyes; otherwise, I will sleep in death.
13.4: My enemy will say, “I have triumphed over him,” and my foes will rejoice because I am shaken.
13.5: But I have trusted in your faithful love; my heart will rejoice in your deliverance.
13.6: I will sing to the LORD because he has treated me generously.

14.1: For the choir director. Of David.The fool says in his heart, “There’s no God.” They are corrupt; they do vile deeds. There is no one who does good.
14.2: The LORD looks down from heaven on the human race to see if there is one who is wise, one who seeks God.
14.3: All have turned away; all alike have become corrupt. There is no one who does good, not even one.
14.4: Will evildoers never understand? They consume my people as they consume bread; they do not call on the LORD.
14.5: Then they will be filled with dread, for God is with those who are righteous.
14.6: You sinners frustrate the plans of the oppressed, but the LORD is his refuge.
14.7: Oh, that Israel’s deliverance would come from Zion! When the LORD restores the fortunes of his people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad.

15.1: A psalm of David.LORD, who can dwell in your tent? Who can live on your holy mountain?
15.2: The one who lives blamelessly, practices righteousness, and acknowledges the truth in his heart —
15.3: who does not slander with his tongue, who does not harm his friend or discredit his neighbor,
15.4: who despises the one rejected by the LORD but honors those who fear the LORD, who keeps his word whatever the cost,
15.5: who does not lend his silver at interest or take a bribe against the innocent — the one who does these things will never be shaken.

16.1: A of David.Protect me, God, for I take refuge in you.
16.2: I said to the LORD, “You are my Lord; I have nothing good besides you.”
16.3: As for the holy people who are in the land, they are the noble ones. All my delight is in them.
16.4: The sorrows of those who take another god for themselves will multiply; I will not pour out their drink offerings of blood, and I will not speak their names with my lips.
16.5: LORD, you are my portion and my cup of blessing; you hold my future.
16.6: The boundary lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; indeed, I have a beautiful inheritance.
16.7: I will bless the LORD who counsels me — even at night when my thoughts trouble me.
16.8: I always let the LORD guide me. Because he is at my right hand, I will not be shaken.
16.9: Therefore my heart is glad and my whole being rejoices; my body also rests securely.
16.10: For you will not abandon me to Sheol; you will not allow your faithful one to see decay.
16.11: You reveal the path of life to me; in your presence is abundant joy; at your right hand are eternal pleasures.

17.1: A prayer of David.LORD, hear a just cause; pay attention to my cry; listen to my prayer — from lips free of deceit.
17.2: Let my vindication come from you, for you see what is right.
17.3: You have tested my heart; you have examined me at night. You have tried me and found nothing evil; I have determined that my mouth will not sin.
17.4: Concerning what people do: by the words from your lips I have avoided the ways of the violent.
17.5: My steps are on your paths; my feet have not slipped.
17.6: I call on you, God, because you will answer me; listen closely to me; hear what I say.
17.7: Display the wonders of your faithful love, Savior of all who seek refuge from those who rebel against your right hand.
17.8: Protect me as the pupil of your eye; hide me in the shadow of your wings
17.9: from the wicked who treat me violently, my deadly enemies who surround me.
17.10: They are uncaring; their mouths speak arrogantly.
17.11: They advance against me; now they surround me. They are determined to throw me to the ground.
17.12: They are like a lion eager to tear, like a young lion lurking in ambush.
17.13: Rise up, LORD! Confront him; bring him down. With your sword, save me from the wicked.
17.14: With your hand, LORD, save me from men, from men of the world whose portion is in this life: You fill their bellies with what you have in store; their sons are satisfied, and they leave their surplus to their children.
17.15: But I will see your face in righteousness; when I awake, I will be satisfied with your presence.

18.1: For the choir director. Of the servant of the LORD, David, who spoke the words of this song to the LORD on the day the LORD rescued him from the grasp of all his enemies and from the power of Saul. He said:I love you, LORD, my strength.
18.2: The LORD is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer, my God, my rock where I seek refuge, my shield and the horn of my salvation, my stronghold.
18.3: I called to the LORD, who is worthy of praise, and I was saved from my enemies.
18.4: The ropes of death were wrapped around me; the torrents of destruction terrified me.
18.5: The ropes of Sheol entangled me; the snares of death confronted me.
18.6: I called to the LORD in my distress, and I cried to my God for help. From his temple he heard my voice, and my cry to him reached his ears.
18.7: Then the earth shook and quaked; the foundations of the mountains trembled; they shook because he burned with anger.
18.8: Smoke rose from his nostrils, and consuming fire came from his mouth; coals were set ablaze by it.
18.9: He bent the heavens and came down, total darkness beneath his feet.
18.10: He rode on a cherub and flew, soaring on the wings of the wind.
18.11: He made darkness his hiding place, dark storm clouds his canopy around him.
18.12: From the radiance of his presence, his clouds swept onward with hail and blazing coals.
18.13: The LORD thundered from heaven; the Most High made his voice heard.
18.14: He shot his arrows and scattered them; he hurled lightning bolts and routed them.
18.15: The depths of the sea became visible, the foundations of the world were exposed, at your rebuke, LORD, at the blast of the breath of your nostrils.
18.16: He reached down from on high and took hold of me; he pulled me out of deep water.
18.17: He rescued me from my powerful enemy and from those who hated me, for they were too strong for me.
18.18: They confronted me in the day of my calamity, but the LORD was my support.
18.19: He brought me out to a spacious place; he rescued me because he delighted in me.
18.20: The LORD rewarded me according to my righteousness; he repaid me according to the cleanness of my hands.
18.21: For I have kept the ways of the LORD and have not turned from my God to wickedness.
18.22: Indeed, I let all his ordinances guide me and have not disregarded his statutes.
18.23: I was blameless toward him and kept myself from my iniquity.
18.24: So the LORD repaid me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands in his sight.
18.25: With the faithful you prove yourself faithful, with the blameless you prove yourself blameless,
18.26: with the pure you prove yourself pure; but with the crooked you prove yourself shrewd.
18.27: For you rescue an oppressed people, but you humble those with haughty eyes.
18.28: LORD, you light my lamp; my God illuminates my darkness.
18.29: With you I can attack a barricade, and with my God I can leap over a wall.
18.30: God — his way is perfect; the word of the LORD is pure. He is a shield to all who take refuge in him.
18.31: For who is God besides the LORD? And who is a rock? Only our God.
18.32: God — he clothes me with strength and makes my way perfect.
18.33: He makes my feet like the feet of a deer and sets me securely on the heights.
18.34: He trains my hands for war; my arms can bend a bow of bronze.
18.35: You have given me the shield of your salvation; your right hand upholds me, and your humility exalts me.
18.36: You make a spacious place beneath me for my steps, and my ankles do not give way.
18.37: I pursue my enemies and overtake them; I do not turn back until they are wiped out.
18.38: I crush them, and they cannot get up; they fall beneath my feet.
18.39: You have clothed me with strength for battle; you subdue my adversaries beneath me.
18.40: You have made my enemies retreat before me; I annihilate those who hate me.
18.41: They cry for help, but there is no one to save them — they cry to the LORD, but he does not answer them.
18.42: I pulverize them like dust before the wind; I trample them like mud in the streets.
18.43: You have freed me from the feuds among the people; you have appointed me the head of nations; a people I had not known serve me.
18.44: Foreigners submit to me cringing; as soon as they hear they obey me.
18.45: Foreigners lose heart and come trembling from their fortifications.
18.46: The LORD lives — blessed be my rock! The God of my salvation is exalted.
18.47: God — he grants me vengeance and subdues peoples under me.
18.48: He frees me from my enemies. You exalt me above my adversaries; you rescue me from violent men.
18.49: Therefore I will give thanks to you among the nations, LORD; I will sing praises about your name.
18.50: He gives great victories to his king; he shows loyalty to his anointed, to David and his descendants forever.

19.1: For the choir director. A psalm of David.The heavens declare the glory of God, and the expanse proclaims the work of his hands.
19.2: Day after day they pour out speech; night after night they communicate knowledge.
19.3: There is no speech; there are no words; their voice is not heard.
19.4: Their message has gone out to the whole earth, and their words to the ends of the world. In the heavens he has pitched a tent for the sun.
19.5: It is like a bridegroom coming from his home; it rejoices like an athlete running a course.
19.6: It rises from one end of the heavens and circles to their other end; nothing is hidden from its heat.
19.7: The instruction of the LORD is perfect, renewing one’s life; the testimony of the LORD is trustworthy, making the inexperienced wise.
19.8: The precepts of the LORD are right, making the heart glad; the command of the LORD is radiant, making the eyes light up.
19.9: The fear of the LORD is pure, enduring forever; the ordinances of the LORD are reliable and altogether righteous.
19.10: They are more desirable than gold — than an abundance of pure gold; and sweeter than honey dripping from a honeycomb.
19.11: In addition, your servant is warned by them, and in keeping them there is an abundant reward.
19.12: Who perceives his unintentional sins? Cleanse me from my hidden faults.
19.13: Moreover, keep your servant from willful sins; do not let them rule me. Then I will be blameless and cleansed from blatant rebellion.
19.14: May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable to you, LORD, my rock and my Redeemer.

20.1: For the choir director. A psalm of David.May the LORD answer you in a day of trouble; may the name of Jacob’s God protect you.
20.2: May he send you help from the sanctuary and sustain you from Zion.
20.3: May he remember all your offerings and accept your burnt offering. Selah
20.4: May he give you what your heart desires and fulfill your whole purpose.
20.5: Let us shout for joy at your victory and lift the banner in the name of our God. May the LORD fulfill all your requests.
20.6: Now I know that the LORD gives victory to his anointed; he will answer him from his holy heaven with mighty victories from his right hand.
20.7: Some take pride in chariots, and others in horses, but we take pride in the name of the LORD our God.
20.8: They collapse and fall, but we rise and stand firm.
20.9: LORD, give victory to the king! May he answer us on the day that we call.

21.1: For the choir director. A psalm of David.LORD, the king finds joy in your strength. How greatly he rejoices in your victory!
21.2: You have given him his heart’s desire and have not denied the request of his lips. Selah
21.3: For you meet him with rich blessings; you place a crown of pure gold on his head.
21.4: He asked you for life, and you gave it to him — length of days forever and ever.
21.5: His glory is great through your victory; you confer majesty and splendor on him.
21.6: You give him blessings forever; you cheer him with joy in your presence.
21.7: For the king relies on the LORD; through the faithful love of the Most High he is not shaken.
21.8: Your hand will capture all your enemies; your right hand will seize those who hate you.
21.9: You will make them burn like a fiery furnace when you appear; the LORD will engulf them in his wrath, and fire will devour them.
21.10: You will wipe their progeny from the earth and their offspring from the human race.
21.11: Though they intend to harm you and devise a wicked plan, they will not prevail.
21.12: Instead, you will put them to flight when you ready your bowstrings to shoot at them.
21.13: Be exalted, LORD, in your strength; we will sing and praise your might.

22.1: For the choir director: according to “The Deer of the Dawn.” A psalm of David.My God, my God, why have you abandoned me? Why are you so far from my deliverance and from my words of groaning?
22.2: My God, I cry by day, but you do not answer, by night, yet I have no rest.
22.3: But you are holy, enthroned on the praises of Israel.
22.4: Our fathers trusted in you; they trusted, and you rescued them.
22.5: They cried to you and were set free; they trusted in you and were not disgraced.
22.6: But I am a worm and not a man, scorned by mankind and despised by people.
22.7: Everyone who sees me mocks me; they sneer and shake their heads:
22.8: “He relies on the LORD; let him save him; let the LORD rescue him, since he takes pleasure in him.”
22.9: It was you who brought me out of the womb, making me secure at my mother’s breast.
22.10: I was given over to you at birth; you have been my God from my mother’s womb.
22.11: Don’t be far from me, because distress is near and there’s no one to help.
22.12: Many bulls surround me; strong ones of Bashan encircle me.
22.13: They open their mouths against me — lions, mauling and roaring.
22.14: I am poured out like water, and all my bones are disjointed; my heart is like wax, melting within me.
22.15: My strength is dried up like baked clay; my tongue sticks to the roof of my mouth. You put me into the dust of death.
22.16: For dogs have surrounded me; a gang of evildoers has closed in on me; they pierced my hands and my feet.
22.17: I can count all my bones; people look and stare at me.
22.18: They divided my garments among themselves, and they cast lots for my clothing.
22.19: But you, LORD, don’t be far away. My strength, come quickly to help me.
22.20: Rescue my life from the sword, my only life from the power of these dogs.
22.21: Save me from the lion’s mouth, from the horns of wild oxen. You answered me!
22.22: I will proclaim your name to my brothers and sisters; I will praise you in the assembly.
22.23: You who fear the LORD, praise him! All you descendants of Jacob, honor him! All you descendants of Israel, revere him!
22.24: For he has not despised or abhorred the torment of the oppressed. He did not hide his face from him but listened when he cried to him for help.
22.25: I will give praise in the great assembly because of you; I will fulfill my vows before those who fear you.
22.26: The humble will eat and be satisfied; those who seek the LORD will praise him. May your hearts live forever!
22.27: All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the LORD. All the families of the nations will bow down before you,
22.28: for kingship belongs to the LORD; he rules the nations.
22.29: All who prosper on earth will eat and bow down; all those who go down to the dust will kneel before him — even the one who cannot preserve his life.
22.30: Their descendants will serve him; the next generation will be told about the Lord.
22.31: They will come and declare his righteousness; to a people yet to be born they will declare what he has done.

23.1: A psalm of David.The LORD is my shepherd; I have what I need.
23.2: He lets me lie down in green pastures; he leads me beside quiet waters.
23.3: He renews my life; he leads me along the right paths for his name’s sake.
23.4: Even when I go through the darkest valley, I fear no danger, for you are with me; your rod and your staff — they comfort me.
23.5: You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies; you anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows.
23.6: Only goodness and faithful love will pursue me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the LORD as long as I live.

24.1: A psalm of David.The earth and everything in it, the world and its inhabitants, belong to the LORD;
24.2: for he laid its foundation on the seas and established it on the rivers.
24.3: Who may ascend the mountain of the LORD? Who may stand in his holy place?
24.4: The one who has clean hands and a pure heart, who has not appealed to what is false, and who has not sworn deceitfully.
24.5: He will receive blessing from the LORD, and righteousness from the God of his salvation.
24.6: Such is the generation of those who inquire of him, who seek the face of the God of Jacob. Selah
24.7: Lift up your heads, you gates! Rise up, ancient doors! Then the King of glory will come in.
24.8: Who is this King of glory? The LORD, strong and mighty, the LORD, mighty in battle.
24.9: Lift up your heads, you gates! Rise up, ancient doors! Then the King of glory will come in.
24.10: Who is he, this King of glory? The LORD of Armies, he is the King of glory. Selah

25.1: Of David.LORD, I appeal to you.
25.2: My God, I trust in you. Do not let me be disgraced; do not let my enemies gloat over me.
25.3: No one who waits for you will be disgraced; those who act treacherously without cause will be disgraced.
25.4: Make your ways known to me, LORD; teach me your paths.
25.5: Guide me in your truth and teach me, for you are the God of my salvation; I wait for you all day long.
25.6: Remember, LORD, your compassion and your faithful love, for they have existed from antiquity.
25.7: Do not remember the sins of my youth or my acts of rebellion; in keeping with your faithful love, remember me because of your goodness, LORD.
25.8: The LORD is good and upright; therefore he shows sinners the way.
25.9: He leads the humble in what is right and teaches them his way.
25.10: All the LORD’s ways show faithful love and truth to those who keep his covenant and decrees.
25.11: LORD, for the sake of your name, forgive my iniquity, for it is immense.
25.12: Who is this person who fears the LORD? He will show him the way he should choose.
25.13: He will live a good life, and his descendants will inherit the land.
25.14: The secret counsel of the LORD is for those who fear him, and he reveals his covenant to them.
25.15: My eyes are always on the LORD, for he will pull my feet out of the net.
25.16: Turn to me and be gracious to me, for I am alone and afflicted.
25.17: The distresses of my heart increase; bring me out of my sufferings.
25.18: Consider my affliction and trouble, and forgive all my sins.
25.19: Consider my enemies; they are numerous, and they hate me violently.
25.20: Guard me and rescue me; do not let me be put to shame, for I take refuge in you.
25.21: May integrity and what is right watch over me, for I wait for you.
25.22: God, redeem Israel, from all its distresses.

26.1: Of David.Vindicate me, LORD, because I have lived with integrity and have trusted in the LORD without wavering.
26.2: Test me, LORD, and try me; examine my heart and mind.
26.3: For your faithful love guides me, and I live by your truth.
26.4: I do not sit with the worthless or associate with hypocrites.
26.5: I hate a crowd of evildoers, and I do not sit with the wicked.
26.6: I wash my hands in innocence and go around your altar, LORD,
26.7: raising my voice in thanksgiving and telling about your wondrous works.
26.8: LORD, I love the house where you dwell, the place where your glory resides.
26.9: Do not destroy me along with sinners, or my life along with men of bloodshed
26.10: in whose hands are evil schemes and whose right hands are filled with bribes.
26.11: But I live with integrity; redeem me and be gracious to me.
26.12: My foot stands on level ground; I will bless the LORD in the assemblies.

27.1: Of David.The LORD is my light and my salvation — whom should I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life — whom should I dread?
27.2: When evildoers came against me to devour my flesh, my foes and my enemies stumbled and fell.
27.3: Though an army deploys against me, my heart will not be afraid; though a war breaks out against me, I will still be confident.
27.4: I have asked one thing from the LORD; it is what I desire: to dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, gazing on the beauty of the LORD and seeking him in his temple.
27.5: For he will conceal me in his shelter in the day of adversity; he will hide me under the cover of his tent; he will set me high on a rock.
27.6: Then my head will be high above my enemies around me; I will offer sacrifices in his tent with shouts of joy. I will sing and make music to the LORD.
27.7: LORD, hear my voice when I call; be gracious to me and answer me.
27.8: My heart says this about you: “Seek his face.” LORD, I will seek your face.
27.9: Do not hide your face from me; do not turn your servant away in anger. You have been my helper; do not leave me or abandon me, God of my salvation.
27.10: Even if my father and mother abandon me, the LORD cares for me.
27.11: Because of my adversaries, show me your way, LORD, and lead me on a level path.
27.12: Do not give me over to the will of my foes, for false witnesses rise up against me, breathing violence.
27.13: I am certain that I will see the LORD’s goodness in the land of the living.
27.14: Wait for the LORD; be strong, and let your heart be courageous. Wait for the LORD.

28.1: Of David.LORD, I call to you; my rock, do not be deaf to me. If you remain silent to me, I will be like those going down to the Pit.
28.2: Listen to the sound of my pleading when I cry to you for help, when I lift up my hands toward your holy sanctuary.
28.3: Do not drag me away with the wicked, with the evildoers, who speak in friendly ways with their neighbors while malice is in their hearts.
28.4: Repay them according to what they have done — according to the evil of their deeds. Repay them according to the work of their hands; give them back what they deserve.
28.5: Because they do not consider what the LORD has done or the work of his hands, he will tear them down and not rebuild them.
28.6: Blessed be the LORD, for he has heard the sound of my pleading.
28.7: The LORD is my strength and my shield; my heart trusts in him, and I am helped. Therefore my heart celebrates, and I give thanks to him with my song.
28.8: The LORD is the strength of his people; he is a stronghold of salvation for his anointed.
28.9: Save your people, bless your possession, shepherd them, and carry them forever.

29.1: A psalm of David.Ascribe to the LORD, you heavenly beings, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
29.2: Ascribe to the LORD the glory due his name; worship the LORD in the splendor of his holiness.
29.3: The voice of the LORD is above the waters. The God of glory thunders — the LORD, above the vast water,
29.4: the voice of the LORD in power, the voice of the LORD in splendor.
29.5: The voice of the LORD breaks the cedars; the LORD shatters the cedars of Lebanon.
29.6: He makes Lebanon skip like a calf, and Sirion, like a young wild ox.
29.7: The voice of the LORD flashes flames of fire.
29.8: The voice of the LORD shakes the wilderness; the LORD shakes the wilderness of Kadesh.
29.9: The voice of the LORD makes the deer give birth and strips the woodlands bare. In his temple all cry, “Glory!”
29.10: The LORD sits enthroned over the flood; the LORD sits enthroned, King forever.
29.11: The LORD gives his people strength; the LORD blesses his people with peace.

30.1: A psalm; a dedication song for the house. Of David.I will exalt you, LORD, because you have lifted me up and have not allowed my enemies to triumph over me.
30.2: LORD my God, I cried to you for help, and you healed me.
30.3: LORD, you brought me up from Sheol; you spared me from among those going down to the Pit.
30.4: Sing to the LORD, you his faithful ones, and praise his holy name.
30.5: For his anger lasts only a moment, but his favor, a lifetime. Weeping may stay overnight, but there is joy in the morning.
30.6: When I was secure, I said, “I will never be shaken.”
30.7: LORD, when you showed your favor, you made me stand like a strong mountain; when you hid your face, I was terrified.
30.8: LORD, I called to you; I sought favor from my Lord:
30.9: “What gain is there in my death, if I go down to the Pit? Will the dust praise you? Will it proclaim your truth?
30.10: LORD, listen and be gracious to me; LORD, be my helper.”
30.11: You turned my lament into dancing; you removed my sackcloth and clothed me with gladness,
30.12: so that I can sing to you and not be silent. LORD my God, I will praise you forever.

31.1: For the choir director. A psalm of David.LORD, I seek refuge in you; let me never be disgraced. Save me by your righteousness.
31.2: Listen closely to me; rescue me quickly. Be a rock of refuge for me, a mountain fortress to save me.
31.3: For you are my rock and my fortress; you lead and guide me for your name’s sake.
31.4: You will free me from the net that is secretly set for me, for you are my refuge.
31.5: Into your hand I entrust my spirit; you have redeemed me, LORD, God of truth.
31.6: I hate those who are devoted to worthless idols, but I trust in the LORD.
31.7: I will rejoice and be glad in your faithful love because you have seen my affliction. You know the troubles of my soul
31.8: and have not handed me over to the enemy. You have set my feet in a spacious place.
31.9: Be gracious to me, LORD, because I am in distress; my eyes are worn out from frustration — my whole being as well.
31.10: Indeed, my life is consumed with grief and my years with groaning; my strength has failed because of my iniquity, and my bones waste away.
31.11: I am ridiculed by all my adversaries and even by my neighbors. I am dreaded by my acquaintances; those who see me in the street run from me.
31.12: I am forgotten: gone from memory like a dead person — like broken pottery.
31.13: I have heard the gossip of many; terror is on every side. When they conspired against me, they plotted to take my life.
31.14: But I trust in you, LORD; I say, “You are my God.”
31.15: The course of my life is in your power; rescue me from the power of my enemies and from my persecutors.
31.16: Make your face shine on your servant; save me by your faithful love.
31.17: LORD, do not let me be disgraced when I call on you. Let the wicked be disgraced; let them be quiet in Sheol.
31.18: Let lying lips that arrogantly speak against the righteous in proud contempt be silenced.
31.19: How great is your goodness that you have stored up for those who fear you and accomplished in the sight of everyone for those who take refuge in you.
31.20: You hide them in the protection of your presence; you conceal them in a shelter from human schemes, from quarrelsome tongues.
31.21: Blessed be the LORD, for he has wondrously shown his faithful love to me in a city under siege.
31.22: In my alarm I said, “I am cut off from your sight.” But you heard the sound of my pleading when I cried to you for help.
31.23: Love the LORD, all his faithful ones. The LORD protects the loyal, but fully repays the arrogant.
31.24: Be strong, and let your heart be courageous, all you who put your hope in the LORD.

32.1: Of David. A .How joyful is the one whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered!
32.2: How joyful is a person whom the LORD does not charge with iniquity and in whose spirit is no deceit!
32.3: When I kept silent, my bones became brittle from my groaning all day long.
32.4: For day and night your hand was heavy on me; my strength was drained as in the summer’s heat. Selah
32.5: Then I acknowledged my sin to you and did not conceal my iniquity. I said, “I will confess my transgressions to the LORD,” and you forgave the guilt of my sin. Selah
32.6: Therefore let everyone who is faithful pray to you immediately. When great floodwaters come, they will not reach him.
32.7: You are my hiding place; you protect me from trouble. You surround me with joyful shouts of deliverance. Selah
32.8: I will instruct you and show you the way to go; with my eye on you, I will give counsel.
32.9: Do not be like a horse or mule, without understanding, that must be controlled with bit and bridle or else it will not come near you.
32.10: Many pains come to the wicked, but the one who trusts in the LORD will have faithful love surrounding him.
32.11: Be glad in the LORD and rejoice, you righteous ones; shout for joy, all you upright in heart.

33.1: Rejoice in the LORD, you righteous ones; praise from the upright is beautiful.
33.2: Praise the LORD with the lyre; make music to him with a ten-stringed harp.
33.3: Sing a new song to him; play skillfully on the strings, with a joyful shout.
33.4: For the word of the LORD is right, and all his work is trustworthy.
33.5: He loves righteousness and justice; the earth is full of the LORD’s unfailing love.
33.6: The heavens were made by the word of the LORD, and all the stars, by the breath of his mouth.
33.7: He gathers the water of the sea into a heap; he puts the depths into storehouses.
33.8: Let the whole earth fear the LORD; let all the inhabitants of the world stand in awe of him.
33.9: For he spoke, and it came into being; he commanded, and it came into existence.
33.10: The LORD frustrates the counsel of the nations; he thwarts the plans of the peoples.
33.11: The counsel of the LORD stands forever, the plans of his heart from generation to generation.
33.12: Happy is the nation whose God is the LORD — the people he has chosen to be his own possession!
33.13: The LORD looks down from heaven; he observes everyone.
33.14: He gazes on all the inhabitants of the earth from his dwelling place.
33.15: He forms the hearts of them all; he considers all their works.
33.16: A king is not saved by a large army; a warrior will not be rescued by great strength.
33.17: The horse is a false hope for safety; it provides no escape by its great power.
33.18: But look, the LORD keeps his eye on those who fear him — those who depend on his faithful love
33.19: to rescue them from death and to keep them alive in famine.
33.20: We wait for the LORD; he is our help and shield.
33.21: For our hearts rejoice in him because we trust in his holy name.
33.22: May your faithful love rest on us, LORD, for we put our hope in you.

34.1: Concerning David, when he pretended to be insane in the presence of Abimelech, who drove him out, and he departed.I will bless the LORD at all times; his praise will always be on my lips.
34.2: I will boast in the LORD; the humble will hear and be glad.
34.3: Proclaim the LORD’s greatness with me; let us exalt his name together.
34.4: I sought the LORD, and he answered me and rescued me from all my fears.
34.5: Those who look to him are radiant with joy; their faces will never be ashamed.
34.6: This poor man cried, and the LORD heard him and saved him from all his troubles.
34.7: The angel of the LORD encamps around those who fear him, and rescues them.
34.8: Taste and see that the LORD is good. How happy is the person who takes refuge in him!
34.9: You who are his holy ones, fear the LORD, for those who fear him lack nothing.
34.10: Young lions lack food and go hungry, but those who seek the LORD will not lack any good thing.
34.11: Come, children, listen to me; I will teach you the fear of the LORD.
34.12: Who is someone who desires life, loving a long life to enjoy what is good?
34.13: Keep your tongue from evil and your lips from deceitful speech.
34.14: Turn away from evil and do what is good; seek peace and pursue it.
34.15: The eyes of the LORD are on the righteous, and his ears are open to their cry for help.
34.16: The face of the LORD is set against those who do what is evil, to remove all memory of them from the earth.
34.17: The righteous cry out, and the LORD hears, and rescues them from all their troubles.
34.18: The LORD is near the brokenhearted; he saves those crushed in spirit.
34.19: One who is righteous has many adversities, but the LORD rescues him from them all.
34.20: He protects all his bones; not one of them is broken.
34.21: Evil brings death to the wicked, and those who hate the righteous will be punished.
34.22: The LORD redeems the life of his servants, and all who take refuge in him will not be punished.

35.1: Of David.Oppose my opponents, LORD; fight those who fight me.
35.2: Take your shields — large and small — and come to my aid.
35.3: Draw the spear and javelin against my pursuers, and assure me: “I am your deliverance.”
35.4: Let those who intend to take my life be disgraced and humiliated; let those who plan to harm me be turned back and ashamed.
35.5: Let them be like chaff in the wind, with the angel of the LORD driving them away.
35.6: Let their way be dark and slippery, with the angel of the LORD pursuing them.
35.7: They hid their net for me without cause; they dug a pit for me without cause.
35.8: Let ruin come on him unexpectedly, and let the net that he hid ensnare him; let him fall into it — to his ruin.
35.9: Then I will rejoice in the LORD; I will delight in his deliverance.
35.10: All my bones will say, “LORD, who is like you, rescuing the poor from one too strong for him, the poor or the needy from one who robs him?”
35.11: Malicious witnesses come forward; they question me about things I do not know.
35.12: They repay me evil for good, making me desolate.
35.13: Yet when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth; I humbled myself with fasting, and my prayer was genuine.
35.14: I went about mourning as if for my friend or brother; I was bowed down with grief, like one mourning for a mother.
35.15: But when I stumbled, they gathered in glee; they gathered against me. Assailants I did not know tore at me and did not stop.
35.16: With godless mockery they gnashed their teeth at me.
35.17: Lord, how long will you look on? Rescue me from their ravages; rescue my precious life from the young lions.
35.18: I will praise you in the great assembly; I will exalt you among many people.
35.19: Do not let my deceitful enemies rejoice over me; do not let those who hate me without cause wink at me maliciously.
35.20: For they do not speak in friendly ways, but contrive fraudulent schemes against those who live peacefully in the land.
35.21: They open their mouths wide against me and say, “Aha, aha! We saw it!”
35.22: You saw it, LORD; do not be silent. Lord, do not be far from me.
35.23: Wake up and rise to my defense, to my cause, my God and my Lord!
35.24: Vindicate me, LORD my God, in keeping with your righteousness, and do not let them rejoice over me.
35.25: Do not let them say in their hearts, “Aha! Just what we wanted.” Do not let them say, “We have swallowed him up!”
35.26: Let those who rejoice at my misfortune be disgraced and humiliated; let those who exalt themselves over me be clothed with shame and reproach.
35.27: Let those who want my vindication shout for joy and be glad; let them continually say, “The LORD be exalted. He takes pleasure in his servant’s well-being.”
35.28: And my tongue will proclaim your righteousness, your praise all day long.

36.1: For the choir director. Of David, the LORD’s servant.An oracle within my heart concerning the transgression of the wicked person: Dread of God has no effect on him.
36.2: For with his flattering opinion of himself, he does not discover and hate his iniquity.
36.3: The words from his mouth are malicious and deceptive; he has stopped acting wisely and doing good.
36.4: Even on his bed he makes malicious plans. He sets himself on a path that is not good, and he does not reject evil.
36.5: LORD, your faithful love reaches to heaven, your faithfulness to the clouds.
36.6: Your righteousness is like the highest mountains, your judgments like the deepest sea. LORD, you preserve people and animals.
36.7: How priceless your faithful love is, God! People take refuge in the shadow of your wings.
36.8: They are filled from the abundance of your house. You let them drink from your refreshing stream.
36.9: For the wellspring of life is with you. By means of your light we see light.
36.10: Spread your faithful love over those who know you, and your righteousness over the upright in heart.
36.11: Do not let the foot of the arrogant come near me or the hand of the wicked drive me away.
36.12: There! The evildoers have fallen. They have been thrown down and cannot rise.

37.1: Of David.Do not be agitated by evildoers; do not envy those who do wrong.
37.2: For they wither quickly like grass and wilt like tender green plants.
37.3: Trust in the LORD and do what is good; dwell in the land and live securely.
37.4: Take delight in the LORD, and he will give you your heart’s desires.
37.5: Commit your way to the LORD; trust in him, and he will act,
37.6: making your righteousness shine like the dawn, your justice like the noonday.
37.7: Be silent before the LORD and wait expectantly for him; do not be agitated by one who prospers in his way, by the person who carries out evil plans.
37.8: Refrain from anger and give up your rage; do not be agitated — it can only bring harm.
37.9: For evildoers will be destroyed, but those who put their hope in the LORD will inherit the land.
37.10: A little while, and the wicked person will be no more; though you look for him, he will not be there.
37.11: But the humble will inherit the land and will enjoy abundant prosperity.
37.12: The wicked person schemes against the righteous and gnashes his teeth at him.
37.13: The Lord laughs at him because he sees that his day is coming.
37.14: The wicked have drawn the sword and strung the bow to bring down the poor and needy and to slaughter those whose way is upright.
37.15: Their swords will enter their own hearts, and their bows will be broken.
37.16: The little that the righteous person has is better than the abundance of many wicked people.
37.17: For the arms of the wicked will be broken, but the LORD supports the righteous.
37.18: The LORD watches over the blameless all their days, and their inheritance will last forever.
37.19: They will not be disgraced in times of adversity; they will be satisfied in days of hunger.
37.20: But the wicked will perish; the LORD’s enemies, like the glory of the pastures, will fade away — they will fade away like smoke.
37.21: The wicked person borrows and does not repay, but the righteous one is gracious and giving.
37.22: Those who are blessed by the LORD will inherit the land, but those cursed by him will be destroyed.
37.23: A person’s steps are established by the LORD, and he takes pleasure in his way.
37.24: Though he falls, he will not be overwhelmed, because the LORD supports him with his hand.
37.25: I have been young and now I am old, yet I have not seen the righteous abandoned or his children begging for bread.
37.26: He is always generous, always lending, and his children are a blessing.
37.27: Turn away from evil, do what is good, and settle permanently.
37.28: For the LORD loves justice and will not abandon his faithful ones. They are kept safe forever, but the children of the wicked will be destroyed.
37.29: The righteous will inherit the land and dwell in it permanently.
37.30: The mouth of the righteous utters wisdom; his tongue speaks what is just.
37.31: The instruction of his God is in his heart; his steps do not falter.
37.32: The wicked one lies in wait for the righteous and intends to kill him;
37.33: the LORD will not leave him in the power of the wicked one or allow him to be condemned when he is judged.
37.34: Wait for the LORD and keep his way, and he will exalt you to inherit the land. You will watch when the wicked are destroyed.
37.35: I have seen a wicked, violent person well-rooted, like a flourishing native tree.
37.36: Then I passed by and noticed he was gone; I searched for him, but he could not be found.
37.37: Watch the blameless and observe the upright, for the person of peace will have a future.
37.38: But transgressors will all be eliminated; the future of the wicked will be destroyed.
37.39: The salvation of the righteous is from the LORD, their refuge in a time of distress.
37.40: The LORD helps and delivers them; he will deliver them from the wicked and will save them because they take refuge in him.

38.1: A psalm of David for remembrance.LORD, do not punish me in your anger or discipline me in your wrath.
38.2: For your arrows have sunk into me, and your hand has pressed down on me.
38.3: There is no soundness in my body because of your indignation; there is no health in my bones because of my sin.
38.4: For my iniquities have flooded over my head; they are a burden too heavy for me to bear.
38.5: My wounds are foul and festering because of my foolishness.
38.6: I am bent over and brought very low; all day long I go around in mourning.
38.7: For my insides are full of burning pain, and there is no soundness in my body.
38.8: I am faint and severely crushed; I groan because of the anguish of my heart.
38.9: Lord, my every desire is in front of you; my sighing is not hidden from you.
38.10: My heart races, my strength leaves me, and even the light of my eyes has faded.
38.11: My loved ones and friends stand back from my affliction, and my relatives stand at a distance.
38.12: Those who intend to kill me set traps, and those who want to harm me threaten to destroy me; they plot treachery all day long.
38.13: I am like a deaf person; I do not hear. I am like a speechless person who does not open his mouth.
38.14: I am like a man who does not hear and has no arguments in his mouth.
38.15: For I put my hope in you, LORD; you will answer me, my Lord, my God.
38.16: For I said, “Don’t let them rejoice over me — those who are arrogant toward me when I stumble.”
38.17: For I am about to fall, and my pain is constantly with me.
38.18: So I confess my iniquity; I am anxious because of my sin.
38.19: But my enemies are vigorous and powerful; many hate me for no reason.
38.20: Those who repay evil for good attack me for pursuing good.
38.21: LORD, do not abandon me; my God, do not be far from me.
38.22: Hurry to help me, my Lord, my salvation.

39.1: For the choir director, for Jeduthun. A psalm of David.I said, “I will guard my ways so that I may not sin with my tongue; I will guard my mouth with a muzzle as long as the wicked are in my presence.”
39.2: I was speechless and quiet; I kept silent, even from speaking good, and my pain intensified.
39.3: My heart grew hot within me; as I mused, a fire burned. I spoke with my tongue:
39.4: “LORD, make me aware of my end and the number of my days so that I will know how short-lived I am.
39.5: In fact, you have made my days just inches long, and my life span is as nothing to you. Yes, every human being stands as only a vapor. Selah
39.6: Yes, a person goes about like a mere shadow. Indeed, they rush around in vain, gathering possessions without knowing who will get them.
39.7: “Now, Lord, what do I wait for? My hope is in you.
39.8: Rescue me from all my transgressions; do not make me the taunt of fools.
39.9: I am speechless; I do not open my mouth because of what you have done.
39.10: Remove your torment from me. Because of the force of your hand I am finished.
39.11: You discipline a person with punishment for iniquity, consuming like a moth what is precious to him; yes, every human being is only a vapor. Selah
39.12: “Hear my prayer, LORD, and listen to my cry for help; do not be silent at my tears. For I am here with you as an alien, a temporary resident like all my ancestors.
39.13: Turn your angry gaze from me so that I may be cheered up before I die and am gone.”

40.1: For the choir director. A psalm of David.I waited patiently for the LORD, and he turned to me and heard my cry for help.
40.2: He brought me up from a desolate pit, out of the muddy clay, and set my feet on a rock, making my steps secure.
40.3: He put a new song in my mouth, a hymn of praise to our God. Many will see and fear, and they will trust in the LORD.
40.4: How happy is anyone who has put his trust in the LORD and has not turned to the proud or to those who run after lies!
40.5: LORD my God, you have done many things — your wondrous works and your plans for us; none can compare with you. If I were to report and speak of them, they are more than can be told.
40.6: You do not delight in sacrifice and offering; you open my ears to listen. You do not ask for a whole burnt offering or a sin offering.
40.7: Then I said, “See, I have come; in the scroll it is written about me.
40.8: I delight to do your will, my God, and your instruction is deep within me.”
40.9: I proclaim righteousness in the great assembly; see, I do not keep my mouth closed — as you know, LORD.
40.10: I did not hide your righteousness in my heart; I spoke about your faithfulness and salvation; I did not conceal your constant love and truth from the great assembly.
40.11: LORD, you do not withhold your compassion from me. Your constant love and truth will always guard me.
40.12: For troubles without number have surrounded me; my iniquities have overtaken me; I am unable to see. They are more than the hairs of my head, and my courage leaves me.
40.13: LORD, be pleased to rescue me; hurry to help me, LORD.
40.14: Let those who intend to take my life be disgraced and confounded. Let those who wish me harm be turned back and humiliated.
40.15: Let those who say to me, “Aha, aha!” be appalled because of their shame.
40.16: Let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you; let those who love your salvation continually say, “The LORD is great!”
40.17: I am oppressed and needy; may the Lord think of me. You are my helper and my deliverer; my God, do not delay.

41.1: For the choir director. A psalm of David.Happy is one who is considerate of the poor; the LORD will save him in a day of adversity.
41.2: The LORD will keep him and preserve him; he will be blessed in the land. You will not give him over to the desire of his enemies.
41.3: The LORD will sustain him on his sickbed; you will heal him on the bed where he lies.
41.4: I said, “LORD, be gracious to me; heal me, for I have sinned against you.”
41.5: My enemies speak maliciously about me: “When will he die and be forgotten?”
41.6: When one of them comes to visit, he speaks deceitfully; he stores up evil in his heart; he goes out and talks.
41.7: All who hate me whisper together about me; they plan to harm me.
41.8: “Something awful has overwhelmed him, and he won’t rise again from where he lies!”
41.9: Even my friend in whom I trusted, one who ate my bread, has raised his heel against me.
41.10: But you, LORD, be gracious to me and raise me up; then I will repay them.
41.11: By this I know that you delight in me: my enemy does not shout in triumph over me.
41.12: You supported me because of my integrity and set me in your presence forever.
41.13: Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Amen and amen.

42.1: For the choir director. A of the sons of Korah.As a deer longs for flowing streams, so I long for you, God.
42.2: I thirst for God, the living God. When can I come and appear before God?
42.3: My tears have been my food day and night, while all day long people say to me, “Where is your God?”
42.4: I remember this as I pour out my heart: how I walked with many, leading the festive procession to the house of God, with joyful and thankful shouts.
42.5: Why, my soul, are you so dejected? Why are you in such turmoil? Put your hope in God, for I will still praise him, my Savior and my God.
42.6: I am deeply depressed; therefore I remember you from the land of Jordan and the peaks of Hermon, from Mount Mizar.
42.7: Deep calls to deep in the roar of your waterfalls; all your breakers and your billows have swept over me.
42.8: The LORD will send his faithful love by day; his song will be with me in the night — a prayer to the God of my life.
42.9: I will say to God, my rock, “Why have you forgotten me? Why must I go about in sorrow because of the enemy’s oppression?”
42.10: My adversaries taunt me, as if crushing my bones, while all day long they say to me, “Where is your God?”
42.11: Why, my soul, are you so dejected? Why are you in such turmoil? Put your hope in God, for I will still praise him, my Savior and my God.

43.1: Vindicate me, God, and champion my cause against an unfaithful nation; rescue me from the deceitful and unjust person.
43.2: For you are the God of my refuge. Why have you rejected me? Why must I go about in sorrow because of the enemy’s oppression?
43.3: Send your light and your truth; let them lead me. Let them bring me to your holy mountain, to your dwelling place.
43.4: Then I will come to the altar of God, to God, my greatest joy. I will praise you with the lyre, God, my God.
43.5: Why, my soul, are you so dejected? Why are you in such turmoil? Put your hope in God, for I will still praise him, my Savior and my God.

44.1: For the choir director. A of the sons of Korah.God, we have heard with our ears — our ancestors have told us — the work you accomplished in their days, in days long ago:
44.2: In order to plant them, you displaced the nations by your hand; in order to settle them, you brought disaster on the peoples.
44.3: For they did not take the land by their sword — their arm did not bring them victory — but by your right hand, your arm, and the light of your face, because you were favorable toward them.
44.4: You are my King, my God, who ordains victories for Jacob.
44.5: Through you we drive back our foes; through your name we trample our enemies.
44.6: For I do not trust in my bow, and my sword does not bring me victory.
44.7: But you give us victory over our foes and let those who hate us be disgraced.
44.8: We boast in God all day long; we will praise your name forever. Selah
44.9: But you have rejected and humiliated us; you do not march out with our armies.
44.10: You make us retreat from the foe, and those who hate us have taken plunder for themselves.
44.11: You hand us over to be eaten like sheep and scatter us among the nations.
44.12: You sell your people for nothing; you make no profit from selling them.
44.13: You make us an object of reproach to our neighbors, a source of mockery and ridicule to those around us.
44.14: You make us a joke among the nations, a laughingstock among the peoples.
44.15: My disgrace is before me all day long, and shame has covered my face,
44.16: because of the taunts of the scorner and reviler, because of the enemy and avenger.
44.17: All this has happened to us, but we have not forgotten you or betrayed your covenant.
44.18: Our hearts have not turned back; our steps have not strayed from your path.
44.19: But you have crushed us in a haunt of jackals and have covered us with deepest darkness.
44.20: If we had forgotten the name of our God and spread out our hands to a foreign god,
44.21: wouldn’t God have found this out, since he knows the secrets of the heart?
44.22: Because of you we are being put to death all day long; we are counted as sheep to be slaughtered.
44.23: Wake up, LORD! Why are you sleeping? Get up! Don’t reject us forever!
44.24: Why do you hide and forget our affliction and oppression?
44.25: For we have sunk down to the dust; our bodies cling to the ground.
44.26: Rise up! Help us! Redeem us because of your faithful love.

45.1: For the choir director: according to “The Lilies.” A of the sons of Korah. A love song.My heart is moved by a noble theme as I recite my verses to the king; my tongue is the pen of a skillful writer.
45.2: You are the most handsome of men; grace flows from your lips. Therefore God has blessed you forever.
45.3: Mighty warrior, strap your sword at your side. In your majesty and splendor —
45.4: in your splendor ride triumphantly in the cause of truth, humility, and justice. May your right hand show your awe-inspiring acts.
45.5: Your sharpened arrows pierce the hearts of the king’s enemies; the peoples fall under you.
45.6: Your throne, God, is forever and ever; the scepter of your kingdom is a scepter of justice.
45.7: You love righteousness and hate wickedness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of joy more than your companions.
45.8: Myrrh, aloes, and cassia perfume all your garments; from ivory palaces harps bring you joy.
45.9: Kings’ daughters are among your honored women; the queen, adorned with gold from Ophir, stands at your right hand.
45.10: Listen, daughter, pay attention and consider: forget your people and your father’s house,
45.11: and the king will desire your beauty. Bow down to him, for he is your lord.
45.12: The daughter of Tyre, the wealthy people, will seek your favor with gifts.
45.13: In her chamber, the royal daughter is all glorious, her clothing embroidered with gold.
45.14: In colorful garments she is led to the king; after her, the virgins, her companions, are brought to you.
45.15: They are led in with gladness and rejoicing; they enter the king’s palace.
45.16: Your sons will succeed your ancestors; you will make them princes throughout the land.
45.17: I will cause your name to be remembered for all generations; therefore the peoples will praise you forever and ever.

46.1: For the choir director. A song of the sons of Korah. According to .God is our refuge and strength, a helper who is always found in times of trouble.
46.2: Therefore we will not be afraid, though the earth trembles and the mountains topple into the depths of the seas,
46.3: though its water roars and foams and the mountains quake with its turmoil. Selah
46.4: There is a river — its streams delight the city of God, the holy dwelling place of the Most High.
46.5: God is within her; she will not be toppled. God will help her when the morning dawns.
46.6: Nations rage, kingdoms topple; the earth melts when he lifts his voice.
46.7: The LORD of Armies is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold. Selah
46.8: Come, see the works of the LORD, who brings devastation on the earth.
46.9: He makes wars cease throughout the earth. He shatters bows and cuts spears to pieces; he sets wagons ablaze.
46.10: “Stop your fighting, and know that I am God, exalted among the nations, exalted on the earth.”
46.11: The LORD of Armies is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold. Selah

47.1: For the choir director. A psalm of the sons of Korah.Clap your hands, all you peoples; shout to God with a jubilant cry.
47.2: For the LORD, the Most High, is awe-inspiring, a great King over the whole earth.
47.3: He subdues peoples under us and nations under our feet.
47.4: He chooses for us our inheritance — the pride of Jacob, whom he loves. Selah
47.5: God ascends among shouts of joy, the LORD, with the sound of trumpets.
47.6: Sing praise to God, sing praise; sing praise to our King, sing praise!
47.7: Sing a song of wisdom, for God is King of the whole earth.
47.8: God reigns over the nations; God is seated on his holy throne.
47.9: The nobles of the peoples have assembled with the people of the God of Abraham. For the leaders of the earth belong to God; he is greatly exalted.

48.1: A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah.The LORD is great and highly praised in the city of our God. His holy mountain,
48.2: rising splendidly, is the joy of the whole earth. Mount Zion — the summit of Zaphon — is the city of the great King.
48.3: God is known as a stronghold in its citadels.
48.4: Look! The kings assembled; they advanced together.
48.5: They looked and froze with fear; they fled in terror.
48.6: Trembling seized them there, agony like that of a woman in labor,
48.7: as you wrecked the ships of Tarshish with the east wind.
48.8: Just as we heard, so we have seen in the city of the LORD of Armies, in the city of our God; God will establish it forever. Selah
48.9: God, within your temple, we contemplate your faithful love.
48.10: Like your name, God, so your praise reaches to the ends of the earth; your right hand is filled with justice.
48.11: Mount Zion is glad. Judah’s villages rejoice because of your judgments.
48.12: Go around Zion, encircle it; count its towers,
48.13: note its ramparts; tour its citadels so that you can tell a future generation:
48.14: “This God, our God forever and ever — he will always lead us.”

49.1: For the choir director. A psalm of the sons of Korah.Hear this, all you peoples; listen, all who inhabit the world,
49.2: both low and high, rich and poor together.
49.3: My mouth speaks wisdom; my heart’s meditation brings understanding.
49.4: I turn my ear to a proverb; I explain my riddle with a lyre.
49.5: Why should I fear in times of trouble? The iniquity of my foes surrounds me.
49.6: They trust in their wealth and boast of their abundant riches.
49.7: Yet these cannot redeem a person or pay his ransom to God —
49.8: since the price of redeeming him is too costly, one should forever stop trying —
49.9: so that he may live forever and not see the Pit.
49.10: For one can see that the wise die; the foolish and stupid also pass away. Then they leave their wealth to others.
49.11: Their graves are their permanent homes, their dwellings from generation to generation, though they have named estates after themselves.
49.12: But despite his assets, mankind will not last; he is like the animals that perish.
49.13: This is the way of those who are arrogant, and of their followers, who approve of their words. Selah
49.14: Like sheep they are headed for Sheol; Death will shepherd them. The upright will rule over them in the morning, and their form will waste away in Sheol, far from their lofty abode.
49.15: But God will redeem me from the power of Sheol, for he will take me. Selah
49.16: Do not be afraid when a person gets rich, when the wealth of his house increases.
49.17: For when he dies, he will take nothing at all; his wealth will not follow him down.
49.18: Though he blesses himself during his lifetime — and you are acclaimed when you do well for yourself —
49.19: he will go to the generation of his fathers; they will never see the light.
49.20: Mankind, with his assets but without understanding, is like the animals that perish.

50.1: A psalm of Asaph.The Mighty One, God, the LORD, speaks; he summons the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting.
50.2: From Zion, the perfection of beauty, God appears in radiance.
50.3: Our God is coming; he will not be silent! Devouring fire precedes him, and a storm rages around him.
50.4: On high, he summons heaven and earth in order to judge his people:
50.5: “Gather my faithful ones to me, those who made a covenant with me by sacrifice.”
50.6: The heavens proclaim his righteousness, for God is the Judge. Selah
50.7: “Listen, my people, and I will speak; I will testify against you, Israel. I am God, your God.
50.8: I do not rebuke you for your sacrifices or for your burnt offerings, which are continually before me.
50.9: I will not take a bull from your household or male goats from your pens,
50.10: for every animal of the forest is mine, the cattle on a thousand hills.
50.11: I know every bird of the mountains, and the creatures of the field are mine.
50.12: If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world and everything in it is mine.
50.13: Do I eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats?
50.14: Sacrifice a thank offering to God, and pay your vows to the Most High.
50.15: Call on me in a day of trouble; I will rescue you, and you will honor me.”
50.16: But God says to the wicked: “What right do you have to recite my statutes and to take my covenant on your lips?
50.17: You hate instruction and fling my words behind you.
50.18: When you see a thief, you make friends with him, and you associate with adulterers.
50.19: You unleash your mouth for evil and harness your tongue for deceit.
50.20: You sit, maligning your brother, slandering your mother’s son.
50.21: You have done these things, and I kept silent; you thought I was just like you. But I will rebuke you and lay out the case before you.
50.22: “Understand this, you who forget God, or I will tear you apart, and there will be no one to rescue you.
50.23: Whoever sacrifices a thank offering honors me, and whoever orders his conduct, I will show him the salvation of God.”

51.1: For the choir director. A psalm of David, when the prophet Nathan came to him after he had gone to Bathsheba.Be gracious to me, God, according to your faithful love; according to your abundant compassion, blot out my rebellion.
51.2: Completely wash away my guilt and cleanse me from my sin.
51.3: For I am conscious of my rebellion, and my sin is always before me.
51.4: Against you — you alone — I have sinned and done this evil in your sight. So you are right when you pass sentence; you are blameless when you judge.
51.5: Indeed, I was guilty when I was born; I was sinful when my mother conceived me.
51.6: Surely you desire integrity in the inner self, and you teach me wisdom deep within.
51.7: Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean; wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.
51.8: Let me hear joy and gladness; let the bones you have crushed rejoice.
51.9: Turn your face away from my sins and blot out all my guilt.
51.10: God, create a clean heart for me and renew a steadfast spirit within me.
51.11: Do not banish me from your presence or take your Holy Spirit from me.
51.12: Restore the joy of your salvation to me, and sustain me by giving me a willing spirit.
51.13: Then I will teach the rebellious your ways, and sinners will return to you.
51.14: Save me from the guilt of bloodshed, God — God of my salvation — and my tongue will sing of your righteousness.
51.15: Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare your praise.
51.16: You do not want a sacrifice, or I would give it; you are not pleased with a burnt offering.
51.17: The sacrifice pleasing to God is a broken spirit. You will not despise a broken and humbled heart, God.
51.18: In your good pleasure, cause Zion to prosper; build the walls of Jerusalem.
51.19: Then you will delight in righteous sacrifices, whole burnt offerings; then bulls will be offered on your altar.

52.1: For the choir director. A of David. When Doeg the Edomite went and reported to Saul, telling him, “David went to Ahimelech’s house.”Why boast about evil, you hero! God’s faithful love is constant.
52.2: Like a sharpened razor, your tongue devises destruction, working treachery.
52.3: You love evil instead of good, lying instead of speaking truthfully. Selah
52.4: You love any words that destroy, you treacherous tongue!
52.5: This is why God will bring you down forever. He will take you, ripping you out of your tent; he will uproot you from the land of the living. Selah
52.6: The righteous will see and fear, and they will derisively say about that hero,
52.7: “Here is the man who would not make God his refuge, but trusted in the abundance of his riches, taking refuge in his destructive behavior.”
52.8: But I am like a flourishing olive tree in the house of God; I trust in God’s faithful love forever and ever.
52.9: I will praise you forever for what you have done. In the presence of your faithful people, I will put my hope in your name, for it is good.

53.1: For the choir director: on . A of David.The fool says in his heart, “There’s no God.” They are corrupt, and they do vile deeds. There is no one who does good.
53.2: God looks down from heaven on the human race to see if there is one who is wise, one who seeks God.
53.3: All have turned away; all alike have become corrupt. There is no one who does good, not even one.
53.4: Will evildoers never understand? They consume my people as they consume bread; they do not call on God.
53.5: Then they will be filled with dread — dread like no other — because God will scatter the bones of those who besiege you. You will put them to shame, for God has rejected them.
53.6: Oh, that Israel’s deliverance would come from Zion! When God restores the fortunes of his people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad.

54.1: For the choir director: with stringed instruments. A of David. When the Ziphites went and said to Saul, “Is David not hiding among us?”God, save me by your name, and vindicate me by your might!
54.2: God, hear my prayer; listen to the words from my mouth.
54.3: For strangers rise up against me, and violent men intend to kill me. They do not let God guide them. Selah
54.4: God is my helper; the Lord is the sustainer of my life.
54.5: He will repay my adversaries for their evil. Because of your faithfulness, annihilate them.
54.6: I will sacrifice a freewill offering to you. I will praise your name, LORD, because it is good.
54.7: For he has rescued me from every trouble, and my eye has looked down on my enemies.

55.1: For the choir director: with stringed instruments. A of David.God, listen to my prayer and do not hide from my plea for help.
55.2: Pay attention to me and answer me. I am restless and in turmoil with my complaint,
55.3: because of the enemy’s words, because of the pressure of the wicked. For they bring down disaster on me and harass me in anger.
55.4: My heart shudders within me; terrors of death sweep over me.
55.5: Fear and trembling grip me; horror has overwhelmed me.
55.6: I said, “If only I had wings like a dove! I would fly away and find rest.
55.7: How far away I would flee; I would stay in the wilderness. Selah
55.8: I would hurry to my shelter from the raging wind and the storm.”
55.9: Lord, confuse and confound their speech, for I see violence and strife in the city;
55.10: day and night they make the rounds on its walls. Crime and trouble are within it;
55.11: destruction is inside it; oppression and deceit never leave its marketplace.
55.12: Now it is not an enemy who insults me — otherwise I could bear it; it is not a foe who rises up against me — otherwise I could hide from him.
55.13: But it is you, a man who is my peer, my companion and good friend!
55.14: We used to have close fellowship; we walked with the crowd into the house of God.
55.15: Let death take them by surprise; let them go down to Sheol alive, because evil is in their homes and within them.
