55.16: But I call to God, and the LORD will save me.
55.17: I complain and groan morning, noon, and night, and he hears my voice.
55.18: Though many are against me, he will redeem me from my battle unharmed.
55.19: God, the one enthroned from long ago, will hear and will humiliate them Selah because they do not change and do not fear God.
55.20: My friend acts violently against those at peace with him; he violates his covenant.
55.21: His buttery words are smooth, but war is in his heart. His words are softer than oil, but they are drawn swords.
55.22: Cast your burden on the LORD, and he will sustain you; he will never allow the righteous to be shaken.
55.23: God, you will bring them down to the Pit of destruction; men of bloodshed and treachery will not live out half their days. But I will trust in you.

56.1: For the choir director: according to “A Silent Dove Far Away.” A of David. When the Philistines seized him in Gath.Be gracious to me, God, for a man is trampling me; he fights and oppresses me all day long.
56.2: My adversaries trample me all day, for many arrogantly fight against me.
56.3: When I am afraid, I will trust in you.
56.4: In God, whose word I praise, in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can mere mortals do to me?
56.5: They twist my words all day long; all their thoughts against me are evil.
56.6: They stir up strife, they lurk; they watch my steps while they wait to take my life.
56.7: Will they escape in spite of such sin? God, bring down the nations in wrath.
56.8: You yourself have recorded my wanderings. Put my tears in your bottle. Are they not in your book?
56.9: Then my enemies will retreat on the day when I call. This I know: God is for me.
56.10: In God, whose word I praise, in the LORD, whose word I praise,
56.11: in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can mere humans do to me?
56.12: I am obligated by vows to you, God; I will make my thank offerings to you.
56.13: For you rescued me from death, even my feet from stumbling, to walk before God in the light of life.

57.1: For the choir director: “Do Not Destroy.” A of David. When he fled before Saul into the cave.Be gracious to me, God, be gracious to me, for I take refuge in you. I will seek refuge in the shadow of your wings until danger passes.
57.2: I call to God Most High, to God who fulfills his purpose for me.
57.3: He reaches down from heaven and saves me, challenging the one who tramples me. Selah God sends his faithful love and truth.
57.4: I am surrounded by lions; I lie down among devouring lions — people whose teeth are spears and arrows, whose tongues are sharp swords.
57.5: God, be exalted above the heavens; let your glory be over the whole earth.
57.6: They prepared a net for my steps; I was despondent. They dug a pit ahead of me, but they fell into it! Selah
57.7: My heart is confident, God, my heart is confident. I will sing; I will sing praises.
57.8: Wake up, my soul! Wake up, harp and lyre! I will wake up the dawn.
57.9: I will praise you, Lord, among the peoples; I will sing praises to you among the nations.
57.10: For your faithful love is as high as the heavens; your faithfulness reaches the clouds.
57.11: God, be exalted above the heavens; let your glory be over the whole earth.

58.1: For the choir director: “Do Not Destroy.” A of David.Do you really speak righteously, you mighty ones? Do you judge people fairly?
58.2: No, you practice injustice in your hearts; with your hands you weigh out violence in the land.
58.3: The wicked go astray from the womb; liars wander about from birth.
58.4: They have venom like the venom of a snake, like the deaf cobra that stops up its ears,
58.5: that does not listen to the sound of the charmers who skillfully weave spells.
58.6: God, knock the teeth out of their mouths; LORD, tear out the young lions’ fangs.
58.7: May they vanish like water that flows by; may they aim their blunted arrows.
58.8: Like a slug that moves along in slime, like a woman’s miscarried child, may they not see the sun.
58.9: Before your pots can feel the heat of the thorns — whether green or burning — he will sweep them away.
58.10: The righteous one will rejoice when he sees the retribution; he will wash his feet in the blood of the wicked.
58.11: Then people will say, “Yes, there is a reward for the righteous! There is a God who judges on earth!”

59.1: For the choir director: “Do Not Destroy.” A of David. When Saul sent agents to watch the house and kill him.Rescue me from my enemies, my God; protect me from those who rise up against me.
59.2: Rescue me from those who practice sin, and save me from men of bloodshed.
59.3: Because look, LORD, they set an ambush for me. Powerful men attack me, but not because of any sin or rebellion of mine.
59.4: For no fault of mine, they run and take up a position. Awake to help me, and take notice.
59.5: LORD God of Armies, you are the God of Israel. Rise up to punish all the nations; do not show favor to any wicked traitors. Selah
59.6: They return at evening, snarling like dogs and prowling around the city.
59.7: Look, they spew from their mouths — sharp words from their lips. “For who,” they say, “will hear?”
59.8: But you laugh at them, LORD; you ridicule all the nations.
59.9: I will keep watch for you, my strength, because God is my stronghold.
59.10: My faithful God will come to meet me; God will let me look down on my adversaries.
59.11: Do not kill them; otherwise, my people will forget. By your power, make them homeless wanderers and bring them down, Lord, our shield.
59.12: For the sin of their mouths and the words of their lips, let them be caught in their pride. They utter curses and lies.
59.13: Consume them in rage; consume them until they are gone. Then people will know throughout the earth that God rules over Jacob. Selah
59.14: And they return at evening, snarling like dogs and prowling around the city.
59.15: They scavenge for food; they growl if they are not satisfied.
59.16: But I will sing of your strength and will joyfully proclaim your faithful love in the morning. For you have been a stronghold for me, a refuge in my day of trouble.
59.17: To you, my strength, I sing praises, because God is my stronghold — my faithful God.

60.1: For the choir director: according to “The Lily of Testimony.” A of David for teaching. When he fought with Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab returned and struck Edom in Salt Valley, killing twelve thousand.God, you have rejected us; you have broken us down; you have been angry. Restore us!
60.2: You have shaken the land and split it open. Heal its fissures, for it shudders.
60.3: You have made your people suffer hardship; you have given us wine to drink that made us stagger.
60.4: You have given a signal flag to those who fear you, so that they can flee before the archers. Selah
60.5: Save with your right hand, and answer me, so that those you love may be rescued.
60.6: God has spoken in his sanctuary: “I will celebrate! I will divide up Shechem. I will apportion the Valley of Succoth.
60.7: Gilead is mine, Manasseh is mine, and Ephraim is my helmet; Judah is my scepter.
60.8: Moab is my washbasin. I throw my sandal on Edom; I shout in triumph over Philistia.”
60.9: Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?
60.10: God, haven’t you rejected us? God, you do not march out with our armies.
60.11: Give us aid against the foe, for human help is worthless.
60.12: With God we will perform valiantly; he will trample our foes.

61.1: For the choir director: on stringed instruments. Of David.God, hear my cry; pay attention to my prayer.
61.2: I call to you from the ends of the earth when my heart is without strength. Lead me to a rock that is high above me,
61.3: for you have been a refuge for me, a strong tower in the face of the enemy.
61.4: I will dwell in your tent forever and take refuge under the shelter of your wings. Selah
61.5: God, you have heard my vows; you have given a heritage to those who fear your name.
61.6: Add days to the king’s life; may his years span many generations.
61.7: May he sit enthroned before God forever. Appoint faithful love and truth to guard him.
61.8: Then I will continually sing of your name, fulfilling my vows day by day.

62.1: For the choir director: according to Jeduthun. A psalm of David.I am at rest in God alone; my salvation comes from him.
62.2: He alone is my rock and my salvation, my stronghold; I will never be shaken.
62.3: How long will you threaten a man? Will all of you attack as if he were a leaning wall or a tottering fence?
62.4: They only plan to bring him down from his high position. They take pleasure in lying; they bless with their mouths, but they curse inwardly. Selah
62.5: Rest in God alone, my soul, for my hope comes from him.
62.6: He alone is my rock and my salvation, my stronghold; I will not be shaken.
62.7: My salvation and glory depend on God, my strong rock. My refuge is in God.
62.8: Trust in him at all times, you people; pour out your hearts before him. God is our refuge. Selah
62.9: Common people are only a vapor; important people, an illusion. Together on a scale, they weigh less than a vapor.
62.10: Place no trust in oppression, or false hope in robbery. If wealth increases, don’t set your heart on it.
62.11: God has spoken once; I have heard this twice: strength belongs to God,
62.12: and faithful love belongs to you, LORD. For you repay each according to his works.

63.1: A psalm of David. When he was in the Wilderness of Judah.God, you are my God; I eagerly seek you. I thirst for you; my body faints for you in a land that is dry, desolate, and without water.
63.2: So I gaze on you in the sanctuary to see your strength and your glory.
63.3: My lips will glorify you because your faithful love is better than life.
63.4: So I will bless you as long as I live; at your name, I will lift up my hands.
63.5: You satisfy me as with rich food; my mouth will praise you with joyful lips.
63.6: When I think of you as I lie on my bed, I meditate on you during the night watches
63.7: because you are my helper; I will rejoice in the shadow of your wings.
63.8: I follow close to you; your right hand holds on to me.
63.9: But those who intend to destroy my life will go into the depths of the earth.
63.10: They will be given over to the power of the sword; they will become a meal for jackals.
63.11: But the king will rejoice in God; all who swear by him will boast, for the mouths of liars will be shut.

64.1: For the choir director. A psalm of David.God, hear my voice when I am in anguish. Protect my life from the terror of the enemy.
64.2: Hide me from the scheming of wicked people, from the mob of evildoers,
64.3: who sharpen their tongues like swords and aim bitter words like arrows,
64.4: shooting from concealed places at the blameless. They shoot at him suddenly and are not afraid.
64.5: They adopt an evil plan; they talk about hiding traps and say, “Who will see them?”
64.6: They devise crimes and say, “We have perfected a secret plan.” The inner man and the heart are mysterious.
64.7: But God will shoot them with arrows; suddenly, they will be wounded.
64.8: They will be made to stumble; their own tongues work against them. All who see them will shake their heads.
64.9: Then everyone will fear and will tell about God’s work, for they will understand what he has done.
64.10: The righteous one rejoices in the LORD and takes refuge in him; all those who are upright in heart will offer praise.

65.1: For the choir director. A psalm of David. A song.Praise is rightfully yours, God, in Zion; vows to you will be fulfilled.
65.2: All humanity will come to you, the one who hears prayer.
65.3: Iniquities overwhelm me; only you can atone for our rebellions.
65.4: How happy is the one you choose and bring near to live in your courts! We will be satisfied with the goodness of your house, the holiness of your temple.
65.5: You answer us in righteousness, with awe-inspiring works, God of our salvation, the hope of all the ends of the earth and of the distant seas.
65.6: You establish the mountains by your power; you are robed with strength.
65.7: You silence the roar of the seas, the roar of their waves, and the tumult of the nations.
65.8: Those who live far away are awed by your signs; you make east and west shout for joy.
65.9: You visit the earth and water it abundantly, enriching it greatly. God’s stream is filled with water, for you prepare the earth in this way, providing people with grain.
65.10: You soften it with showers and bless its growth, soaking its furrows and leveling its ridges.
65.11: You crown the year with your goodness; your carts overflow with plenty.
65.12: The wilderness pastures overflow, and the hills are robed with joy.
65.13: The pastures are clothed with flocks and the valleys covered with grain. They shout in triumph; indeed, they sing.

66.1: For the choir director. A song. A psalm.Let the whole earth shout joyfully to God!
66.2: Sing about the glory of his name; make his praise glorious.
66.3: Say to God, “How awe-inspiring are your works! Your enemies will cringe before you because of your great strength.
66.4: The whole earth will worship you and sing praise to you. They will sing praise to your name.” Selah
66.5: Come and see the wonders of God; his acts for humanity are awe-inspiring.
66.6: He turned the sea into dry land, and they crossed the river on foot. There we rejoiced in him.
66.7: He rules forever by his might; he keeps his eye on the nations. The rebellious should not exalt themselves. Selah
66.8: Bless our God, you peoples; let the sound of his praise be heard.
66.9: He keeps us alive and does not allow our feet to slip.
66.10: For you, God, tested us; you refined us as silver is refined.
66.11: You lured us into a trap; you placed burdens on our backs.
66.12: You let men ride over our heads; we went through fire and water, but you brought us out to abundance.
66.13: I will enter your house with burnt offerings; I will pay you my vows
66.14: that my lips promised and my mouth spoke during my distress.
66.15: I will offer you fattened sheep as burnt offerings, with the fragrant smoke of rams; I will sacrifice bulls with goats. Selah
66.16: Come and listen, all who fear God, and I will tell what he has done for me.
66.17: I cried out to him with my mouth, and praise was on my tongue.
66.18: If I had been aware of malice in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.
66.19: However, God has listened; he has paid attention to the sound of my prayer.
66.20: Blessed be God! He has not turned away my prayer or turned his faithful love from me.

67.1: For the choir director: with stringed instruments. A psalm. A song.May God be gracious to us and bless us; may he make his face shine upon us Selah
67.2: so that your way may be known on earth, your salvation among all nations.
67.3: Let the peoples praise you, God; let all the peoples praise you.
67.4: Let the nations rejoice and shout for joy, for you judge the peoples with fairness and lead the nations on earth. Selah
67.5: Let the peoples praise you, God, let all the peoples praise you.
67.6: The earth has produced its harvest; God, our God, blesses us.
67.7: God will bless us, and all the ends of the earth will fear him.

68.1: For the choir director. A psalm of David. A song.God arises. His enemies scatter, and those who hate him flee from his presence.
68.2: As smoke is blown away, so you blow them away. As wax melts before the fire, so the wicked are destroyed before God.
68.3: But the righteous are glad; they rejoice before God and celebrate with joy.
68.4: Sing to God! Sing praises to his name. Exalt him who rides on the clouds — his name is the LORD — and celebrate before him.
68.5: God in his holy dwelling is a father of the fatherless and a champion of widows.
68.6: God provides homes for those who are deserted. He leads out the prisoners to prosperity, but the rebellious live in a scorched land.
68.7: God, when you went out before your people, when you marched through the desert, Selah
68.8: the earth trembled and the skies poured rain before God, the God of Sinai, before God, the God of Israel.
68.9: You, God, showered abundant rain; you revived your inheritance when it languished.
68.10: Your people settled in it; God, you provided for the poor by your goodness.
68.11: The Lord gave the command; a great company of women brought the good news:
68.12: “The kings of the armies flee — they flee!” She who stays at home divides the spoil.
68.13: While you lie among the sheep pens, the wings of a dove are covered with silver, and its feathers with glistening gold.
68.14: When the Almighty scattered kings in the land, it snowed on Zalmon.
68.15: Mount Bashan is God’s towering mountain; Mount Bashan is a mountain of many peaks.
68.16: Why gaze with envy, you mountain peaks, at the mountain God desired for his abode? The LORD will dwell there forever!
68.17: God’s chariots are tens of thousands, thousands and thousands; the Lord is among them in the sanctuary as he was at Sinai.
68.18: You ascended to the heights, taking away captives; you received gifts from people, even from the rebellious, so that the LORD God might dwell there.
68.19: Blessed be the Lord! Day after day he bears our burdens; God is our salvation. Selah
68.20: Our God is a God of salvation, and escape from death belongs to the LORD my Lord.
68.21: Surely God crushes the heads of his enemies, the hairy brow of one who goes on in his guilty acts.
68.22: The Lord said, “I will bring them back from Bashan; I will bring them back from the depths of the sea
68.23: so that your foot may wade in blood and your dogs’ tongues may have their share from the enemies.”
68.24: People have seen your procession, God, the procession of my God, my King, in the sanctuary.
68.25: Singers lead the way, with musicians following; among them are young women playing tambourines.
68.26: Bless God in the assemblies; bless the LORD from the fountain of Israel.
68.27: There is Benjamin, the youngest, leading them, the rulers of Judah in their assembly, the rulers of Zebulun, the rulers of Naphtali.
68.28: Your God has decreed your strength. Show your strength, God, you who have acted on our behalf.
68.29: Because of your temple at Jerusalem, kings will bring tribute to you.
68.30: Rebuke the beast in the reeds, the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples. Trample underfoot those with bars of silver. Scatter the peoples who take pleasure in war.
68.31: Ambassadors will come from Egypt; Cush will stretch out its hands to God.
68.32: Sing to God, you kingdoms of the earth; sing praise to the Lord, Selah
68.33: to him who rides in the ancient, highest heavens. Look, he thunders with his powerful voice!
68.34: Ascribe power to God. His majesty is over Israel, his power is among the clouds.
68.35: God, you are awe-inspiring in your sanctuaries. The God of Israel gives power and strength to his people. Blessed be God!

69.1: For the choir director: according to “The Lilies.” Of David.Save me, God, for the water has risen to my neck.
69.2: I have sunk in deep mud, and there is no footing; I have come into deep water, and a flood sweeps over me.
69.3: I am weary from my crying; my throat is parched. My eyes fail, looking for my God.
69.4: Those who hate me without cause are more numerous than the hairs of my head; my deceitful enemies, who would destroy me, are powerful. Though I did not steal, I must repay.
69.5: God, you know my foolishness, and my guilty acts are not hidden from you.
69.6: Do not let those who put their hope in you be disgraced because of me, Lord GOD of Armies; do not let those who seek you be humiliated because of me, God of Israel.
69.7: For I have endured insults because of you, and shame has covered my face.
69.8: I have become a stranger to my brothers and a foreigner to my mother’s sons
69.9: because zeal for your house has consumed me, and the insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.
69.10: I mourned and fasted, but it brought me insults.
69.11: I wore sackcloth as my clothing, and I was a joke to them.
69.12: Those who sit at the city gate talk about me, and drunkards make up songs about me.
69.13: But as for me, LORD, my prayer to you is for a time of favor. In your abundant, faithful love, God, answer me with your sure salvation.
69.14: Rescue me from the miry mud; don’t let me sink. Let me be rescued from those who hate me and from the deep water.
69.15: Don’t let the floodwaters sweep over me or the deep swallow me up; don’t let the Pit close its mouth over me.
69.16: Answer me, LORD, for your faithful love is good. In keeping with your abundant compassion, turn to me.
69.17: Don’t hide your face from your servant, for I am in distress. Answer me quickly!
69.18: Come near to me and redeem me; ransom me because of my enemies.
69.19: You know the insults I endure — my shame and disgrace. You are aware of all my adversaries.
69.20: Insults have broken my heart, and I am in despair. I waited for sympathy, but there was none; for comforters, but found no one.
69.21: Instead, they gave me gall for my food, and for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
69.22: Let their table set before them be a snare, and let it be a trap for their allies.
69.23: Let their eyes grow too dim to see, and let their hips continually quake.
69.24: Pour out your rage on them, and let your burning anger overtake them.
69.25: Make their fortification desolate; may no one live in their tents.
69.26: For they persecute the one you struck and talk about the pain of those you wounded.
69.27: Charge them with crime on top of crime; do not let them share in your righteousness.
69.28: Let them be erased from the book of life and not be recorded with the righteous.
69.29: But as for me — poor and in pain — let your salvation protect me, God.
69.30: I will praise God’s name with song and exalt him with thanksgiving.
69.31: That will please the LORD more than an ox, more than a bull with horns and hooves.
69.32: The humble will see it and rejoice. You who seek God, take heart!
69.33: For the LORD listens to the needy and does not despise his own who are prisoners.
69.34: Let heaven and earth praise him, the seas and everything that moves in them,
69.35: for God will save Zion and build up the cities of Judah. They will live there and possess it.
69.36: The descendants of his servants will inherit it, and those who love his name will live in it.

70.1: For the choir director. Of David. To bring remembrance.God, hurry to rescue me. LORD, hurry to help me!
70.2: Let those who seek to kill me be disgraced and confounded; let those who wish me harm be turned back and humiliated.
70.3: Let those who say, “Aha, aha!” retreat because of their shame.
70.4: Let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you; let those who love your salvation continually say, “God is great!”
70.5: I am oppressed and needy; hurry to me, God. You are my help and my deliverer; LORD, do not delay.

71.1: LORD, I seek refuge in you; let me never be disgraced.
71.2: In your justice, rescue and deliver me; listen closely to me and save me.
71.3: Be a rock of refuge for me, where I can always go. Give the command to save me, for you are my rock and fortress.
71.4: Deliver me, my God, from the power of the wicked, from the grasp of the unjust and oppressive.
71.5: For you are my hope, Lord GOD, my confidence from my youth.
71.6: I have leaned on you from birth; you took me from my mother’s womb. My praise is always about you.
71.7: I am like a miraculous sign to many, and you are my strong refuge.
71.8: My mouth is full of praise and honor to you all day long.
71.9: Don’t discard me in my old age. As my strength fails, do not abandon me.
71.10: For my enemies talk about me, and those who spy on me plot together,
71.11: saying, “God has abandoned him; chase him and catch him, for there is no one to rescue him.”
71.12: God, do not be far from me; my God, hurry to help me.
71.13: May my adversaries be disgraced and destroyed; may those who intend to harm me be covered with disgrace and humiliation.
71.14: But I will hope continually and will praise you more and more.
71.15: My mouth will tell about your righteousness and your salvation all day long, though I cannot sum them up.
71.16: I come because of the mighty acts of the Lord GOD; I will proclaim your righteousness, yours alone.
71.17: God, you have taught me from my youth, and I still proclaim your wondrous works.
71.18: Even while I am old and gray, God, do not abandon me, while I proclaim your power to another generation, your strength to all who are to come.
71.19: Your righteousness reaches the heights, God, you who have done great things; God, who is like you?
71.20: You caused me to experience many troubles and misfortunes, but you will revive me again. You will bring me up again, even from the depths of the earth.
71.21: You will increase my honor and comfort me once again.
71.22: Therefore, I will praise you with a harp for your faithfulness, my God; I will sing to you with a lyre, Holy One of Israel.
71.23: My lips will shout for joy when I sing praise to you because you have redeemed me.
71.24: Therefore, my tongue will proclaim your righteousness all day long, for those who intend to harm me will be disgraced and confounded.

72.1: Of Solomon.God, give your justice to the king and your righteousness to the king’s son.
72.2: He will judge your people with righteousness and your afflicted ones with justice.
72.3: May the mountains bring well-being to the people and the hills, righteousness.
72.4: May he vindicate the afflicted among the people, help the poor, and crush the oppressor.
72.5: May they fear you while the sun endures and as long as the moon, throughout all generations.
72.6: May the king be like rain that falls on the cut grass, like spring showers that water the earth.
72.7: May the righteous flourish in his days and well-being abound until the moon is no more.
72.8: May he rule from sea to sea and from the Euphrates to the ends of the earth.
72.9: May desert tribes kneel before him and his enemies lick the dust.
72.10: May the kings of Tarshish and the coasts and islands bring tribute, the kings of Sheba and Seba offer gifts.
72.11: Let all kings bow in homage to him, all nations serve him.
72.12: For he will rescue the poor who cry out and the afflicted who have no helper.
72.13: He will have pity on the poor and helpless and save the lives of the poor.
72.14: He will redeem them from oppression and violence, for their lives are precious in his sight.
72.15: May he live long! May gold from Sheba be given to him. May prayer be offered for him continually, and may he be blessed all day long.
72.16: May there be plenty of grain in the land; may it wave on the tops of the mountains. May its crops be like Lebanon. May people flourish in the cities like the grass of the field.
72.17: May his name endure forever; as long as the sun shines, may his fame increase. May all nations be blessed by him and call him blessed.
72.18: Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who alone does wonders.
72.19: Blessed be his glorious name forever; the whole earth is filled with his glory. Amen and amen.
72.20: The prayers of David son of Jesse are concluded.

73.1: A psalm of Asaph.God is indeed good to Israel, to the pure in heart.
73.2: But as for me, my feet almost slipped; my steps nearly went astray.
73.3: For I envied the arrogant; I saw the prosperity of the wicked.
73.4: They have an easy time until they die, and their bodies are well fed.
73.5: They are not in trouble like others; they are not afflicted like most people.
73.6: Therefore, pride is their necklace, and violence covers them like a garment.
73.7: Their eyes bulge out from fatness; the imaginations of their hearts run wild.
73.8: They mock, and they speak maliciously; they arrogantly threaten oppression.
73.9: They set their mouths against heaven, and their tongues strut across the earth.
73.10: Therefore his people turn to them and drink in their overflowing words.
73.11: The wicked say, “How can God know? Does the Most High know everything?”
73.12: Look at them — the wicked! They are always at ease, and they increase their wealth.
73.13: Did I purify my heart and wash my hands in innocence for nothing?
73.14: For I am afflicted all day long and punished every morning.
73.15: If I had decided to say these things aloud, I would have betrayed your people.
73.16: When I tried to understand all this, it seemed hopeless
73.17: until I entered God’s sanctuary. Then I understood their destiny.
73.18: Indeed, you put them in slippery places; you make them fall into ruin.
73.19: How suddenly they become a desolation! They come to an end, swept away by terrors.
73.20: Like one waking from a dream, Lord, when arising, you will despise their image.
73.21: When I became embittered and my innermost being was wounded,
73.22: I was stupid and didn’t understand; I was an unthinking animal toward you.
73.23: Yet I am always with you; you hold my right hand.
73.24: You guide me with your counsel, and afterward you will take me up in glory.
73.25: Who do I have in heaven but you? And I desire nothing on earth but you.
73.26: My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart, my portion forever.
73.27: Those far from you will certainly perish; you destroy all who are unfaithful to you.
73.28: But as for me, God’s presence is my good. I have made the Lord GOD my refuge, so I can tell about all you do.

74.1: A of Asaph.Why have you rejected us forever, God? Why does your anger burn against the sheep of your pasture?
74.2: Remember your congregation, which you purchased long ago and redeemed as the tribe for your own possession. Remember Mount Zion where you dwell.
74.3: Make your way to the perpetual ruins, to all that the enemy has destroyed in the sanctuary.
74.4: Your adversaries roared in the meeting place where you met with us. They set up their emblems as signs.
74.5: It was like men in a thicket of trees, wielding axes,
74.6: then smashing all the carvings with hatchets and picks.
74.7: They set your sanctuary on fire; they utterly desecrated the dwelling place of your name.
74.8: They said in their hearts, “Let us oppress them relentlessly.” They burned every place throughout the land where God met with us.
74.9: There are no signs for us to see. There is no longer a prophet. And none of us knows how long this will last.
74.10: God, how long will the enemy mock? Will the foe insult your name forever?
74.11: Why do you hold back your hand? Stretch out your right hand and destroy them!
74.12: God my King is from ancient times, performing saving acts on the earth.
74.13: You divided the sea with your strength; you smashed the heads of the sea monsters in the water;
74.14: you crushed the heads of Leviathan; you fed him to the creatures of the desert.
74.15: You opened up springs and streams; you dried up ever-flowing rivers.
74.16: The day is yours, also the night; you established the moon and the sun.
74.17: You set all the boundaries of the earth; you made summer and winter.
74.18: Remember this: the enemy has mocked the LORD, and a foolish people has insulted your name.
74.19: Do not give to beasts the life of your dove; do not forget the lives of your poor people forever.
74.20: Consider the covenant, for the dark places of the land are full of violence.
74.21: Do not let the oppressed turn away in shame; let the poor and needy praise your name.
74.22: Rise up, God, champion your cause! Remember the insults that fools bring against you all day long.
74.23: Do not forget the clamor of your adversaries, the tumult of your opponents that goes up constantly.

75.1: For the choir director: “Do Not Destroy.” A psalm of Asaph. A song.We give thanks to you, God; we give thanks to you, for your name is near. People tell about your wondrous works.
75.2: “When I choose a time, I will judge fairly.
75.3: When the earth and all its inhabitants shake, I am the one who steadies its pillars. Selah
75.4: I say to the boastful, ‘Do not boast,’ and to the wicked, ‘Do not lift up your horn.
75.5: Do not lift up your horn against heaven or speak arrogantly.’”
75.6: Exaltation does not come from the east, the west, or the desert,
75.7: for God is the Judge: He brings down one and exalts another.
75.8: For there is a cup in the LORD’s hand, full of wine blended with spices, and he pours from it. All the wicked of the earth will drink, draining it to the dregs.
75.9: As for me, I will tell about him forever; I will sing praise to the God of Jacob.
75.10: “I will cut off all the horns of the wicked, but the horns of the righteous will be lifted up.”

76.1: For the choir director: with stringed instruments. A psalm of Asaph. A song.God is known in Judah; his name is great in Israel.
76.2: His tent is in Salem, his dwelling place in Zion.
76.3: There he shatters the bow’s flaming arrows, the shield, the sword, and the weapons of war. Selah
76.4: You are resplendent and majestic coming down from the mountains of prey.
76.5: The brave-hearted have been plundered; they have slipped into their final sleep. None of the warriors was able to lift a hand.
76.6: At your rebuke, God of Jacob, both chariot and horse lay still.
76.7: And you — you are to be feared. When you are angry, who can stand before you?
76.8: From heaven you pronounced judgment. The earth feared and grew quiet
76.9: when God rose up to judge and to save all the lowly of the earth. Selah
76.10: Even human wrath will praise you; you will clothe yourself with the wrath that remains.
76.11: Make and keep your vows to the LORD your God; let all who are around him bring tribute to the awe-inspiring one.
76.12: He humbles the spirit of leaders; he is feared by the kings of the earth.

77.1: For the choir director: according to Jeduthun. Of Asaph. A psalm.I cry aloud to God, aloud to God, and he will hear me.
77.2: I sought the Lord in my day of trouble. My hands were continually lifted up all night long; I refused to be comforted.
77.3: I think of God; I groan; I meditate; my spirit becomes weak. Selah
77.4: You have kept me from closing my eyes; I am troubled and cannot speak.
77.5: I consider days of old, years long past.
77.6: At night I remember my music; I meditate in my heart, and my spirit ponders.
77.7: “Will the Lord reject forever and never again show favor?
77.8: Has his faithful love ceased forever? Is his promise at an end for all generations?
77.9: Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has he in anger withheld his compassion?” Selah
77.10: So I say, “I am grieved that the right hand of the Most High has changed.”
77.11: I will remember the LORD’s works; yes, I will remember your ancient wonders.
77.12: I will reflect on all you have done and meditate on your actions.
77.13: God, your way is holy. What god is great like God?
77.14: You are the God who works wonders; you revealed your strength among the peoples.
77.15: With power you redeemed your people, the descendants of Jacob and Joseph. Selah
77.16: The water saw you, God. The water saw you; it trembled. Even the depths shook.
77.17: The clouds poured down water. The storm clouds thundered; your arrows flashed back and forth.
77.18: The sound of your thunder was in the whirlwind; lightning lit up the world. The earth shook and quaked.
77.19: Your way went through the sea and your path through the vast water, but your footprints were unseen.
77.20: You led your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

78.1: A of Asaph.My people, hear my instruction; listen to the words from my mouth.
78.2: I will declare wise sayings; I will speak mysteries from the past —
78.3: things we have heard and known and that our fathers have passed down to us.
78.4: We will not hide them from their children, but will tell a future generation the praiseworthy acts of the LORD, his might, and the wondrous works he has performed.
78.5: He established a testimony in Jacob and set up a law in Israel, which he commanded our fathers to teach to their children
78.6: so that a future generation — children yet to be born — might know. They were to rise and tell their children
78.7: so that they might put their confidence in God and not forget God’s works, but keep his commands.
78.8: Then they would not be like their fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation, a generation whose heart was not loyal and whose spirit was not faithful to God.
78.9: The Ephraimite archers turned back on the day of battle.
78.10: They did not keep God’s covenant and refused to live by his law.
78.11: They forgot what he had done, the wondrous works he had shown them.
78.12: He worked wonders in the sight of their fathers in the land of Egypt, the territory of Zoan.
78.13: He split the sea and brought them across; the water stood firm like a wall.
78.14: He led them with a cloud by day and with a fiery light throughout the night.
78.15: He split rocks in the wilderness and gave them drink as abundant as the depths.
78.16: He brought streams out of the stone and made water flow down like rivers.
78.17: But they continued to sin against him, rebelling in the desert against the Most High.
78.18: They deliberately tested God, demanding the food they craved.
78.19: They spoke against God, saying, “Is God able to provide food in the wilderness?
78.20: Look! He struck the rock and water gushed out; torrents overflowed. But can he also provide bread or furnish meat for his people?”
78.21: Therefore, the LORD heard and became furious; then fire broke out against Jacob, and anger flared up against Israel
78.22: because they did not believe God or rely on his salvation.
78.23: He gave a command to the clouds above and opened the doors of heaven.
78.24: He rained manna for them to eat; he gave them grain from heaven.
78.25: People ate the bread of angels. He sent them an abundant supply of food.
78.26: He made the east wind blow in the skies and drove the south wind by his might.
78.27: He rained meat on them like dust, and winged birds like the sand of the seas.
78.28: He made them fall in the camp, all around the tents.
78.29: The people ate and were completely satisfied, for he gave them what they craved.
78.30: Before they had turned from what they craved, while the food was still in their mouths,
78.31: God’s anger flared up against them, and he killed some of their best men. He struck down Israel’s fit young men.
78.32: Despite all this, they kept sinning and did not believe his wondrous works.
78.33: He made their days end in futility, their years in sudden disaster.
78.34: When he killed some of them, the rest began to seek him; they repented and searched for God.
78.35: They remembered that God was their rock, the Most High God, their Redeemer.
78.36: But they deceived him with their mouths, they lied to him with their tongues,
78.37: their hearts were insincere toward him, and they were unfaithful to his covenant.
78.38: Yet he was compassionate; he atoned for their iniquity and did not destroy them. He often turned his anger aside and did not unleash all his wrath.
78.39: He remembered that they were only flesh, a wind that passes and does not return.
78.40: How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness and grieved him in the desert.
78.41: They constantly tested God and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
78.42: They did not remember his power shown on the day he redeemed them from the foe,
78.43: when he performed his miraculous signs in Egypt and his wonders in the territory of Zoan.
78.44: He turned their rivers into blood, and they could not drink from their streams.
78.45: He sent among them swarms of flies, which fed on them, and frogs, which devastated them.
78.46: He gave their crops to the caterpillar and the fruit of their labor to the locust.
78.47: He killed their vines with hail and their sycamore fig trees with a flood.
78.48: He handed over their livestock to hail and their cattle to lightning bolts.
78.49: He sent his burning anger against them: fury, indignation, and calamity — a band of deadly messengers.
78.50: He cleared a path for his anger. He did not spare them from death but delivered their lives to the plague.
78.51: He struck all the firstborn in Egypt, the first progeny of the tents of Ham.
78.52: He led his people out like sheep and guided them like a flock in the wilderness.
78.53: He led them safely, and they were not afraid; but the sea covered their enemies.
78.54: He brought them to his holy territory, to the mountain his right hand acquired.
78.55: He drove out nations before them. He apportioned their inheritance by lot and settled the tribes of Israel in their tents.
78.56: But they rebelliously tested the Most High God, for they did not keep his decrees.
78.57: They treacherously turned away like their fathers; they became warped like a faulty bow.
78.58: They enraged him with their high places and provoked his jealousy with their carved images.
78.59: God heard and became furious; he completely rejected Israel.
78.60: He abandoned the tabernacle at Shiloh, the tent where he resided among mankind.
78.61: He gave up his strength to captivity and his splendor to the hand of a foe.
78.62: He surrendered his people to the sword because he was enraged with his heritage.
78.63: Fire consumed his chosen young men, and his young women had no wedding songs.
78.64: His priests fell by the sword, and the widows could not lament.
78.65: The Lord awoke as if from sleep, like a warrior from the effects of wine.
78.66: He beat back his foes; he gave them lasting disgrace.
78.67: He rejected the tent of Joseph and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim.
78.68: He chose instead the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which he loved.
78.69: He built his sanctuary like the heights, like the earth that he established forever.
78.70: He chose David his servant and took him from the sheep pens;
78.71: he brought him from tending ewes to be shepherd over his people Jacob — over Israel, his inheritance.
78.72: He shepherded them with a pure heart and guided them with his skillful hands.

79.1: A psalm of Asaph.God, the nations have invaded your inheritance, desecrated your holy temple, and turned Jerusalem into ruins.
79.2: They gave the corpses of your servants to the birds of the sky for food, the flesh of your faithful ones to the beasts of the earth.
79.3: They poured out their blood like water all around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them.
79.4: We have become an object of reproach to our neighbors, a source of mockery and ridicule to those around us.
79.5: How long, LORD? Will you be angry forever? Will your jealousy keep burning like fire?
79.6: Pour out your wrath on the nations that don’t acknowledge you, on the kingdoms that don’t call on your name,
79.7: for they have devoured Jacob and devastated his homeland.
79.8: Do not hold past iniquities against us; let your compassion come to us quickly, for we have become very weak.
79.9: God of our salvation, help us — for the glory of your name. Rescue us and atone for our sins, for your name’s sake.
79.10: Why should the nations ask, “Where is their God?” Before our eyes, let vengeance for the shed blood of your servants be known among the nations.
79.11: Let the groans of the prisoners reach you; according to your great power, preserve those condemned to die.
79.12: Pay back sevenfold to our neighbors the reproach they have hurled at you, Lord.
79.13: Then we, your people, the sheep of your pasture, will thank you forever; we will declare your praise to generation after generation.

80.1: For the choir director: according to “The Lilies.” A testimony of Asaph. A psalm.Listen, Shepherd of Israel, who leads Joseph like a flock; you who sit enthroned between the cherubim, shine
80.2: on Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh. Rally your power and come to save us.
80.3: Restore us, God; make your face shine on us, so that we may be saved.
80.4: LORD God of Armies, how long will you be angry with your people’s prayers?
80.5: You fed them the bread of tears and gave them a full measure of tears to drink.
80.6: You put us at odds with our neighbors; our enemies mock us.
80.7: Restore us, God of Armies; make your face shine on us, so that we may be saved.
80.8: You dug up a vine from Egypt; you drove out the nations and planted it.
80.9: You cleared a place for it; it took root and filled the land.
80.10: The mountains were covered by its shade, and the mighty cedars with its branches.
80.11: It sent out sprouts toward the Sea and shoots toward the River.
80.12: Why have you broken down its walls so that all who pass by pick its fruit?
80.13: Boars from the forest tear at it and creatures of the field feed on it.
80.14: Return, God of Armies. Look down from heaven and see; take care of this vine,
80.15: the root your right hand planted, the son that you made strong for yourself.
80.16: It was cut down and burned; they perish at the rebuke of your countenance.
80.17: Let your hand be with the man at your right hand, with the son of man you have made strong for yourself.
80.18: Then we will not turn away from you; revive us, and we will call on your name.
80.19: Restore us, LORD, God of Armies; make your face shine on us, so that we may be saved.

81.1: For the choir director: on the . Of Asaph.Sing for joy to God our strength; shout in triumph to the God of Jacob.
81.2: Lift up a song — play the tambourine, the melodious lyre, and the harp.
81.3: Blow the horn on the day of our feasts during the new moon and during the full moon.
81.4: For this is a statute for Israel, an ordinance of the God of Jacob.
81.5: He set it up as a decree for Joseph when he went throughout the land of Egypt. I heard an unfamiliar language:
81.6: “I relieved his shoulder from the burden; his hands were freed from carrying the basket.
81.7: You called out in distress, and I rescued you; I answered you from the thundercloud. I tested you at the Waters of Meribah. Selah
81.8: Listen, my people, and I will admonish you. Israel, if you would only listen to me!
81.9: There must not be a strange god among you; you must not bow down to a foreign god.
81.10: I am the LORD your God, who brought you up from the land of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.
81.11: “But my people did not listen to my voice; Israel did not obey me.
81.12: So I gave them over to their stubborn hearts to follow their own plans.
81.13: If only my people would listen to me and Israel would follow my ways,
81.14: I would quickly subdue their enemies and turn my hand against their foes.”
81.15: Those who hate the LORD would cower to him; their doom would last forever.
81.16: But he would feed Israel with the best wheat. “I would satisfy you with honey from the rock.”

82.1: A psalm of Asaph.God stands in the divine assembly; he pronounces judgment among the gods:
82.2: “How long will you judge unjustly and show partiality to the wicked? Selah
82.3: Provide justice for the needy and the fatherless; uphold the rights of the oppressed and the destitute.
82.4: Rescue the poor and needy; save them from the power of the wicked.”
82.5: They do not know or understand; they wander in darkness. All the foundations of the earth are shaken.
82.6: I said, “You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High.
82.7: However, you will die like humans and fall like any other ruler.”
82.8: Rise up, God, judge the earth, for all the nations belong to you.

83.1: A song. A psalm of Asaph.God, do not keep silent. Do not be deaf, God; do not be quiet.
83.2: See how your enemies make an uproar; those who hate you have acted arrogantly.
83.3: They devise clever schemes against your people; they conspire against your treasured ones.
83.4: They say, “Come, let us wipe them out as a nation so that Israel’s name will no longer be remembered.”
83.5: For they have conspired with one mind; they form an alliance against you —
83.6: the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites,
83.7: Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek, Philistia with the inhabitants of Tyre.
83.8: Even Assyria has joined them; they lend support to the sons of Lot. Selah
83.9: Deal with them as you did with Midian, as you did with Sisera and Jabin at the Kishon River.
83.10: They were destroyed at En-dor; they became manure for the ground.
83.11: Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, and all their tribal leaders like Zebah and Zalmunna,
83.12: who said, “Let us seize God’s pastures for ourselves.”
83.13: Make them like tumbleweed, my God, like straw before the wind.
83.14: As fire burns a forest, as a flame blazes through mountains,
83.15: so pursue them with your tempest and terrify them with your storm.
83.16: Cover their faces with shame so that they will seek your name, LORD.
83.17: Let them be put to shame and terrified forever; let them perish in disgrace.
83.18: May they know that you alone — whose name is the LORD — are the Most High over the whole earth.

84.1: For the choir director: on the . A psalm of the sons of Korah.How lovely is your dwelling place, LORD of Armies.
84.2: I long and yearn for the courts of the LORD; my heart and flesh cry out for the living God.
84.3: Even a sparrow finds a home, and a swallow, a nest for herself where she places her young — near your altars, LORD of Armies, my King and my God.
84.4: How happy are those who reside in your house, who praise you continually. Selah
84.5: Happy are the people whose strength is in you, whose hearts are set on pilgrimage.
84.6: As they pass through the Valley of Baca, they make it a source of springwater; even the autumn rain will cover it with blessings.
84.7: They go from strength to strength; each appears before God in Zion.
84.8: LORD God of Armies, hear my prayer; listen, God of Jacob. Selah
84.9: Consider our shield, God; look on the face of your anointed one.
84.10: Better a day in your courts than a thousand anywhere else. I would rather stand at the threshold of the house of my God than live in the tents of wicked people.
84.11: For the LORD God is a sun and shield. The LORD grants favor and honor; he does not withhold the good from those who live with integrity.
84.12: Happy is the person who trusts in you, LORD of Armies!

85.1: For the choir director. A psalm of the sons of Korah.LORD, you showed favor to your land; you restored the fortunes of Jacob.
85.2: You forgave your people’s guilt; you covered all their sin. Selah
85.3: You withdrew all your fury; you turned from your burning anger.
85.4: Return to us, God of our salvation, and abandon your displeasure with us.
85.5: Will you be angry with us forever? Will you prolong your anger for all generations?
85.6: Will you not revive us again so that your people may rejoice in you?
85.7: Show us your faithful love, LORD, and give us your salvation.
85.8: I will listen to what God will say; surely the LORD will declare peace to his people, his faithful ones, and not let them go back to foolish ways.
85.9: His salvation is very near those who fear him, so that glory may dwell in our land.
85.10: Faithful love and truth will join together; righteousness and peace will embrace.
85.11: Truth will spring up from the earth, and righteousness will look down from heaven.
85.12: Also, the LORD will provide what is good, and our land will yield its crops.
85.13: Righteousness will go before him to prepare the way for his steps.

86.1: A prayer of David.Listen, LORD, and answer me, for I am poor and needy.
86.2: Protect my life, for I am faithful. You are my God; save your servant who trusts in you.
86.3: Be gracious to me, Lord, for I call to you all day long.
86.4: Bring joy to your servant’s life, because I appeal to you, Lord.
86.5: For you, Lord, are kind and ready to forgive, abounding in faithful love to all who call on you.
86.6: LORD, hear my prayer; listen to my plea for mercy.
86.7: I call on you in the day of my distress, for you will answer me.
86.8: Lord, there is no one like you among the gods, and there are no works like yours.
86.9: All the nations you have made will come and bow down before you, Lord, and will honor your name.
86.10: For you are great and perform wonders; you alone are God.
86.11: Teach me your way, LORD, and I will live by your truth. Give me an undivided mind to fear your name.
86.12: I will praise you with all my heart, Lord my God, and will honor your name forever.
86.13: For your faithful love for me is great, and you rescue my life from the depths of Sheol.
86.14: God, arrogant people have attacked me; a gang of ruthless men intends to kill me. They do not let you guide them.
86.15: But you, Lord, are a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger and abounding in faithful love and truth.
86.16: Turn to me and be gracious to me. Give your strength to your servant; save the son of your female servant.
86.17: Show me a sign of your goodness; my enemies will see and be put to shame because you, LORD, have helped and comforted me.

87.1: A psalm of the sons of Korah. A song.The city he founded is on the holy mountains.
87.2: The LORD loves Zion’s city gates more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
87.3: Glorious things are said about you, city of God. Selah
87.4: “I will make a record of those who know me: Rahab, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Cush — each one was born there.”
87.5: And it will be said of Zion, “This one and that one were born in her.” The Most High himself will establish her.
87.6: When he registers the peoples, the LORD will record, “This one was born there.” Selah
87.7: Singers and dancers alike will say, “My whole source of joy is in you.”

88.1: A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah. For the choir director: according to A of Heman the Ezrahite.LORD, God of my salvation, I cry out before you day and night.
88.2: May my prayer reach your presence; listen to my cry.
88.3: For I have had enough troubles, and my life is near Sheol.
88.4: I am counted among those going down to the Pit. I am like a man without strength,
88.5: abandoned among the dead. I am like the slain lying in the grave, whom you no longer remember, and who are cut off from your care.
88.6: You have put me in the lowest part of the Pit, in the darkest places, in the depths.
88.7: Your wrath weighs heavily on me; you have overwhelmed me with all your waves. Selah
88.8: You have distanced my friends from me; you have made me repulsive to them. I am shut in and cannot go out.
88.9: My eyes are worn out from crying. LORD, I cry out to you all day long; I spread out my hands to you.
88.10: Do you work wonders for the dead? Do departed spirits rise up to praise you? Selah
88.11: Will your faithful love be declared in the grave, your faithfulness in Abaddon?
88.12: Will your wonders be known in the darkness or your righteousness in the land of oblivion?
88.13: But I call to you for help, LORD; in the morning my prayer meets you.
88.14: LORD, why do you reject me? Why do you hide your face from me?
88.15: From my youth, I have been suffering and near death. I suffer your horrors; I am desperate.
88.16: Your wrath sweeps over me; your terrors destroy me.
88.17: They surround me like water all day long; they close in on me from every side.
88.18: You have distanced loved one and neighbor from me; darkness is my only friend.

89.1: A of Ethan the Ezrahite.I will sing about the LORD’s faithful love forever; I will proclaim your faithfulness to all generations with my mouth.
89.2: For I will declare, “Faithful love is built up forever; you establish your faithfulness in the heavens.”
89.3: The LORD said, “I have made a covenant with my chosen one; I have sworn an oath to David my servant:
89.4: ‘I will establish your offspring forever and build up your throne for all generations.’” Selah
89.5: LORD, the heavens praise your wonders — your faithfulness also — in the assembly of the holy ones.
89.6: For who in the skies can compare with the LORD? Who among the heavenly beings is like the LORD?
89.7: God is greatly feared in the council of the holy ones, more awe-inspiring than all who surround him.
89.8: LORD God of Armies, who is strong like you, LORD? Your faithfulness surrounds you.
89.9: You rule the raging sea; when its waves surge, you still them.
89.10: You crushed Rahab like one who is slain; you scattered your enemies with your powerful arm.
89.11: The heavens are yours; the earth also is yours. The world and everything in it — you founded them.
89.12: North and south — you created them. Tabor and Hermon shout for joy at your name.
89.13: You have a mighty arm; your hand is powerful; your right hand is lifted high.
89.14: Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne; faithful love and truth go before you.
89.15: Happy are the people who know the joyful shout; LORD, they walk in the light from your face.
89.16: They rejoice in your name all day long, and they are exalted by your righteousness.
89.17: For you are their magnificent strength; by your favor our horn is exalted.
89.18: Surely our shield belongs to the LORD, our king to the Holy One of Israel.
89.19: You once spoke in a vision to your faithful ones and said: “I have granted help to a warrior; I have exalted one chosen from the people.
89.20: I have found David my servant; I have anointed him with my sacred oil.
89.21: My hand will always be with him, and my arm will strengthen him.
89.22: The enemy will not oppress him; the wicked will not afflict him.
89.23: I will crush his foes before him and strike those who hate him.
89.24: My faithfulness and love will be with him, and through my name his horn will be exalted.
89.25: I will extend his power to the sea and his right hand to the rivers.
89.26: He will call to me, ‘You are my Father, my God, the rock of my salvation.’
89.27: I will also make him my firstborn, greatest of the kings of the earth.
89.28: I will always preserve my faithful love for him, and my covenant with him will endure.
89.29: I will establish his line forever, his throne as long as heaven lasts.
89.30: If his sons abandon my instruction and do not live by my ordinances,
89.31: if they dishonor my statutes and do not keep my commands,
89.32: then I will call their rebellion to account with the rod, their iniquity with blows.
89.33: But I will not withdraw my faithful love from him or betray my faithfulness.
89.34: I will not violate my covenant or change what my lips have said.
89.35: Once and for all I have sworn an oath by my holiness; I will not lie to David.
89.36: His offspring will continue forever, his throne like the sun before me,
89.37: like the moon, established forever, a faithful witness in the sky.” Selah
89.38: But you have spurned and rejected him; you have become enraged with your anointed.
89.39: You have repudiated the covenant with your servant; you have completely dishonored his crown.
89.40: You have broken down all his walls; you have reduced his fortified cities to ruins.
89.41: All who pass by plunder him; he has become an object of ridicule to his neighbors.
89.42: You have lifted high the right hand of his foes; you have made all his enemies rejoice.
89.43: You have also turned back his sharp sword and have not let him stand in battle.
89.44: You have made his splendor cease and have overturned his throne.
89.45: You have shortened the days of his youth; you have covered him with shame. Selah
89.46: How long, LORD? Will you hide forever? Will your anger keep burning like fire?
89.47: Remember how short my life is. Have you created everyone for nothing?
89.48: What courageous person can live and never see death? Who can save himself from the power of Sheol? Selah
89.49: Lord, where are the former acts of your faithful love that you swore to David in your faithfulness?
89.50: Remember, Lord, the ridicule against your servants — in my heart I carry abuse from all the peoples —
89.51: how your enemies have ridiculed, LORD, how they have ridiculed every step of your anointed.
89.52: Blessed be the LORD forever. Amen and amen.

90.1: A prayer of Moses, the man of God.Lord, you have been our refuge in every generation.
90.2: Before the mountains were born, before you gave birth to the earth and the world, from eternity to eternity, you are God.
90.3: You return mankind to the dust, saying, “Return, descendants of Adam.”
90.4: For in your sight a thousand years are like yesterday that passes by, like a few hours of the night.
90.5: You end their lives; they sleep. They are like grass that grows in the morning —
90.6: in the morning it sprouts and grows; by evening it withers and dries up.
90.7: For we are consumed by your anger; we are terrified by your wrath.
90.8: You have set our iniquities before you, our secret sins in the light of your presence.
90.9: For all our days ebb away under your wrath; we end our years like a sigh.
90.10: Our lives last seventy years or, if we are strong, eighty years. Even the best of them are struggle and sorrow; indeed, they pass quickly and we fly away.
90.11: Who understands the power of your anger? Your wrath matches the fear that is due you.
90.12: Teach us to number our days carefully so that we may develop wisdom in our hearts.
90.13: LORD — how long? Turn and have compassion on your servants.
90.14: Satisfy us in the morning with your faithful love so that we may shout with joy and be glad all our days.
90.15: Make us rejoice for as many days as you have humbled us, for as many years as we have seen adversity.
90.16: Let your work be seen by your servants, and your splendor by their children.
90.17: Let the favor of the Lord our God be on us; establish for us the work of our hands — establish the work of our hands!

91.1: The one who lives under the protection of the Most High dwells in the shadow of the Almighty.
91.2: I will say concerning the LORD, who is my refuge and my fortress, my God in whom I trust:
91.3: He himself will rescue you from the bird trap, from the destructive plague.
91.4: He will cover you with his feathers; you will take refuge under his wings. His faithfulness will be a protective shield.
91.5: You will not fear the terror of the night, the arrow that flies by day,
91.6: the plague that stalks in darkness, or the pestilence that ravages at noon.
91.7: Though a thousand fall at your side and ten thousand at your right hand, the pestilence will not reach you.
91.8: You will only see it with your eyes and witness the punishment of the wicked.
91.9: Because you have made the LORD — my refuge, the Most High — your dwelling place,
91.10: no harm will come to you; no plague will come near your tent.
91.11: For he will give his angels orders concerning you, to protect you in all your ways.
91.12: They will support you with their hands so that you will not strike your foot against a stone.
91.13: You will tread on the lion and the cobra; you will trample the young lion and the serpent.
91.14: Because he has his heart set on me, I will deliver him; I will protect him because he knows my name.
91.15: When he calls out to me, I will answer him; I will be with him in trouble. I will rescue him and give him honor.
91.16: I will satisfy him with a long life and show him my salvation.

92.1: A psalm. A song for the Sabbath day.It is good to give thanks to the LORD, to sing praise to your name, Most High,
92.2: to declare your faithful love in the morning and your faithfulness at night,
92.3: with a ten-stringed harp and the music of a lyre.
92.4: For you have made me rejoice, LORD, by what you have done; I will shout for joy because of the works of your hands.
92.5: How magnificent are your works, LORD, how profound your thoughts!
92.6: A stupid person does not know, a fool does not understand this:
92.7: though the wicked sprout like grass and all evildoers flourish, they will be eternally destroyed.
92.8: But you, LORD, are exalted forever.
92.9: For indeed, LORD, your enemies — indeed, your enemies will perish; all evildoers will be scattered.
92.10: You have lifted up my horn like that of a wild ox; I have been anointed with the finest oil.
92.11: My eyes look at my enemies; when evildoers rise against me, my ears hear them.
92.12: The righteous thrive like a palm tree and grow like a cedar tree in Lebanon.
92.13: Planted in the house of the LORD, they thrive in the courts of our God.
92.14: They will still bear fruit in old age, healthy and green,
92.15: to declare: “The LORD is just; he is my rock, and there is no unrighteousness in him.”

93.1: The LORD reigns! He is robed in majesty; the LORD is robed, enveloped in strength. The world is firmly established; it cannot be shaken.
93.2: Your throne has been established from the beginning; you are from eternity.
93.3: The floods have lifted up, LORD, the floods have lifted up their voice; the floods lift up their pounding waves.
93.4: Greater than the roar of a huge torrent — the mighty breakers of the sea — the LORD on high is majestic.
93.5: LORD, your testimonies are completely reliable; holiness adorns your house for all the days to come.

94.1: LORD, God of vengeance — God of vengeance, shine!
94.2: Rise up, Judge of the earth; repay the proud what they deserve.
94.3: LORD, how long will the wicked — how long will the wicked celebrate?
94.4: They pour out arrogant words; all the evildoers boast.
94.5: LORD, they crush your people; they oppress your heritage.
94.6: They kill the widow and the resident alien and murder the fatherless.
94.7: They say, “The LORD doesn’t see it. The God of Jacob doesn’t pay attention.”
94.8: Pay attention, you stupid people! Fools, when will you be wise?
94.9: Can the one who shaped the ear not hear, the one who formed the eye not see?
94.10: The one who instructs nations, the one who teaches mankind knowledge — does he not discipline?
94.11: The LORD knows the thoughts of mankind; they are futile.
94.12: LORD, how happy is anyone you discipline and teach from your law
94.13: to give him relief from troubled times until a pit is dug for the wicked.
94.14: The LORD will not leave his people or abandon his heritage,
94.15: for the administration of justice will again be righteous, and all the upright in heart will follow it.
94.16: Who stands up for me against the wicked? Who takes a stand for me against evildoers?
94.17: If the LORD had not been my helper, I would soon rest in the silence of death.
94.18: If I say, “My foot is slipping,” your faithful love will support me, LORD.
94.19: When I am filled with cares, your comfort brings me joy.
94.20: Can a corrupt throne be your ally, a throne that makes evil laws?
94.21: They band together against the life of the righteous and condemn the innocent to death.
94.22: But the LORD is my refuge; my God is the rock of my protection.
94.23: He will pay them back for their sins and destroy them for their evil. The LORD our God will destroy them.

95.1: Come, let us shout joyfully to the LORD, shout triumphantly to the rock of our salvation!
95.2: Let us enter his presence with thanksgiving; let us shout triumphantly to him in song.
95.3: For the LORD is a great God, a great King above all gods.
95.4: The depths of the earth are in his hand, and the mountain peaks are his.
95.5: The sea is his; he made it. His hands formed the dry land.
95.6: Come, let us worship and bow down; let us kneel before the LORD our Maker.
95.7: For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture, the sheep under his care. Today, if you hear his voice:
95.8: Do not harden your hearts as at Meribah, as on that day at Massah in the wilderness
95.9: where your fathers tested me; they tried me, though they had seen what I did.
95.10: For forty years I was disgusted with that generation; I said, “They are a people whose hearts go astray; they do not know my ways.”
95.11: So I swore in my anger, “They will not enter my rest.”

96.1: Sing a new song to the LORD; let the whole earth sing to the LORD.
96.2: Sing to the LORD, bless his name; proclaim his salvation from day to day.
96.3: Declare his glory among the nations, his wondrous works among all peoples.
96.4: For the LORD is great and is highly praised; he is feared above all gods.
96.5: For all the gods of the peoples are idols, but the LORD made the heavens.
96.6: Splendor and majesty are before him; strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.
96.7: Ascribe to the LORD, you families of the peoples, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
96.8: Ascribe to the LORD the glory of his name; bring an offering and enter his courts.
96.9: Worship the LORD in the splendor of his holiness; let the whole earth tremble before him.
96.10: Say among the nations: “The LORD reigns. The world is firmly established; it cannot be shaken. He judges the peoples fairly.”
96.11: Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice; let the sea and all that fills it resound.
96.12: Let the fields and everything in them celebrate. Then all the trees of the forest will shout for joy
96.13: before the LORD, for he is coming — for he is coming to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with his faithfulness.

97.1: The LORD reigns! Let the earth rejoice; let the many coasts and islands be glad.
97.2: Clouds and total darkness surround him; righteousness and justice are the foundation of his throne.
97.3: Fire goes before him and burns up his foes on every side.
97.4: His lightning lights up the world; the earth sees and trembles.
97.5: The mountains melt like wax at the presence of the LORD — at the presence of the Lord of the whole earth.
97.6: The heavens proclaim his righteousness; all the peoples see his glory.
97.7: All who serve carved images, those who boast in idols, will be put to shame. All the gods must worship him.
97.8: Zion hears and is glad, Judah’s villages rejoice because of your judgments, LORD.
97.9: For you, LORD, are the Most High over the whole earth; you are exalted above all the gods.
97.10: You who love the LORD, hate evil! He protects the lives of his faithful ones; he rescues them from the power of the wicked.
97.11: Light dawns for the righteous, gladness for the upright in heart.
97.12: Be glad in the LORD, you righteous ones, and give thanks to his holy name.

98.1: A psalm.Sing a new song to the LORD, for he has performed wonders; his right hand and holy arm have won him victory.
98.2: The LORD has made his victory known; he has revealed his righteousness in the sight of the nations.
98.3: He has remembered his love and faithfulness to the house of Israel; all the ends of the earth have seen our God’s victory.
98.4: Let the whole earth shout to the LORD; be jubilant, shout for joy, and sing.
98.5: Sing to the LORD with the lyre, with the lyre and melodious song.
98.6: With trumpets and the blast of the ram’s horn shout triumphantly in the presence of the LORD, our King.
98.7: Let the sea and all that fills it, the world and those who live in it, resound.
98.8: Let the rivers clap their hands; let the mountains shout together for joy
98.9: before the LORD, for he is coming to judge the earth. He will judge the world righteously and the peoples fairly.

99.1: The LORD reigns! Let the peoples tremble. He is enthroned between the cherubim. Let the earth quake.
99.2: The LORD is great in Zion; he is exalted above all the peoples.
99.3: Let them praise your great and awe-inspiring name. He is holy.
99.4: The mighty King loves justice. You have established fairness; you have administered justice and righteousness in Jacob.
99.5: Exalt the LORD our God; bow in worship at his footstool. He is holy.
99.6: Moses and Aaron were among his priests; Samuel also was among those calling on his name. They called to the LORD and he answered them.
99.7: He spoke to them in a pillar of cloud; they kept his decrees and the statutes he gave them.
99.8: LORD our God, you answered them. You were a forgiving God to them, but an avenger of their sinful actions.
99.9: Exalt the LORD our God; bow in worship at his holy mountain, for the LORD our God is holy.

100.1: A psalm of thanksgiving.Let the whole earth shout triumphantly to God!
100.2: Serve the LORD with gladness; come before him with joyful songs.
100.3: Acknowledge that the LORD is God. He made us, and we are his — his people, the sheep of his pasture.
100.4: Enter his gates with thanksgiving and his courts with praise. Give thanks to him and bless his name.
100.5: For the LORD is good, and his faithful love endures forever; his faithfulness, through all generations.

101.1: A psalm of David.I will sing of faithful love and justice; I will sing praise to you, LORD.
101.2: I will pay attention to the way of integrity. When will you come to me? I will live with a heart of integrity in my house.
101.3: I will not let anything worthless guide me. I hate the practice of transgression; it will not cling to me.
101.4: A devious heart will be far from me; I will not be involved with evil.
101.5: I will destroy anyone who secretly slanders his neighbor; I cannot tolerate anyone with haughty eyes or an arrogant heart.
101.6: My eyes favor the faithful of the land so that they may sit down with me. The one who follows the way of integrity may serve me.
101.7: No one who acts deceitfully will live in my palace; the one who tells lies will not be retained here to guide me.
101.8: Every morning I will destroy all the wicked of the land, wiping out all evildoers from the LORD’s city.

102.1: A prayer of a suffering person who is weak and pours out his lament before the LORD.LORD, hear my prayer; let my cry for help come before you.
102.2: Do not hide your face from me in my day of trouble. Listen closely to me; answer me quickly when I call.
102.3: For my days vanish like smoke, and my bones burn like a furnace.
102.4: My heart is suffering, withered like grass; I even forget to eat my food.
102.5: Because of the sound of my groaning, my flesh sticks to my bones.
102.6: I am like an eagle owl, like a little owl among the ruins.
102.7: I stay awake; I am like a solitary bird on a roof.
102.8: My enemies taunt me all day long; they ridicule and use my name as a curse.
102.9: I eat ashes like bread and mingle my drinks with tears
102.10: because of your indignation and wrath; for you have picked me up and thrown me aside.
102.11: My days are like a lengthening shadow, and I wither away like grass.
102.12: But you, LORD, are enthroned forever; your fame endures to all generations.
102.13: You will rise up and have compassion on Zion, for it is time to show favor to her — the appointed time has come.
102.14: For your servants take delight in its stones and favor its dust.
102.15: Then the nations will fear the name of the LORD, and all the kings of the earth your glory,
102.16: for the LORD will rebuild Zion; he will appear in his glory.
102.17: He will pay attention to the prayer of the destitute and will not despise their prayer.
102.18: This will be written for a later generation, and a people who have not yet been created will praise the LORD:
102.19: He looked down from his holy heights — the LORD gazed out from heaven to earth —
102.20: to hear a prisoner’s groaning, to set free those condemned to die,
102.21: so that they might declare the name of the LORD in Zion and his praise in Jerusalem,
102.22: when peoples and kingdoms are assembled to serve the LORD.
102.23: He has broken my strength in midcourse; he has shortened my days.
102.24: I say: “My God, do not take me in the middle of my life! Your years continue through all generations.
102.25: Long ago you established the earth, and the heavens are the work of your hands.
102.26: They will perish, but you will endure; all of them will wear out like clothing. You will change them like a garment, and they will pass away.
102.27: But you are the same, and your years will never end.
102.28: Your servants’ children will dwell securely, and their offspring will be established before you.”

103.1: Of David.My soul, bless the LORD, and all that is within me, bless his holy name.
103.2: My soul, bless the LORD, and do not forget all his benefits.
103.3: He forgives all your iniquity; he heals all your diseases.
103.4: He redeems your life from the Pit; he crowns you with faithful love and compassion.
103.5: He satisfies you with good things; your youth is renewed like the eagle.
103.6: The LORD executes acts of righteousness and justice for all the oppressed.
103.7: He revealed his ways to Moses, his deeds to the people of Israel.
103.8: The LORD is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in faithful love.
103.9: He will not always accuse us or be angry forever.
103.10: He has not dealt with us as our sins deserve or repaid us according to our iniquities.
103.11: For as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is his faithful love toward those who fear him.
103.12: As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us.
103.13: As a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion on those who fear him.
103.14: For he knows what we are made of, remembering that we are dust.
103.15: As for man, his days are like grass — he blooms like a flower of the field;
103.16: when the wind passes over it, it vanishes, and its place is no longer known.
103.17: But from eternity to eternity the LORD’s faithful love is toward those who fear him, and his righteousness toward the grandchildren
103.18: of those who keep his covenant, who remember to observe his precepts.
103.19: The LORD has established his throne in heaven, and his kingdom rules over all.
103.20: Bless the LORD, all his angels of great strength, who do his word, obedient to his command.
103.21: Bless the LORD, all his armies, his servants who do his will.
103.22: Bless the LORD, all his works in all the places where he rules. My soul, bless the LORD!

104.1: My soul, bless the LORD! LORD my God, you are very great; you are clothed with majesty and splendor.
104.2: He wraps himself in light as if it were a robe, spreading out the sky like a canopy,
104.3: laying the beams of his palace on the waters above, making the clouds his chariot, walking on the wings of the wind,
104.4: and making the winds his messengers, flames of fire his servants.
104.5: He established the earth on its foundations; it will never be shaken.
104.6: You covered it with the deep as if it were a garment; the water stood above the mountains.
104.7: At your rebuke the water fled; at the sound of your thunder they hurried away —
104.8: mountains rose and valleys sank — to the place you established for them.
104.9: You set a boundary they cannot cross; they will never cover the earth again.
104.10: He causes the springs to gush into the valleys; they flow between the mountains.
104.11: They supply water for every wild beast; the wild donkeys quench their thirst.
104.12: The birds of the sky live beside the springs; they make their voices heard among the foliage.
104.13: He waters the mountains from his palace; the earth is satisfied by the fruit of your labor.
104.14: He causes grass to grow for the livestock and provides crops for man to cultivate, producing food from the earth,
104.15: wine that makes human hearts glad — making his face shine with oil — and bread that sustains human hearts.
104.16: The trees of the LORD flourish, the cedars of Lebanon that he planted.
104.17: There the birds make their nests; storks make their homes in the pine trees.
104.18: The high mountains are for the wild goats; the cliffs are a refuge for hyraxes.
104.19: He made the moon to mark the festivals; the sun knows when to set.
104.20: You bring darkness, and it becomes night, when all the forest animals stir.
104.21: The young lions roar for their prey and seek their food from God.
104.22: The sun rises; they go back and lie down in their dens.
104.23: Man goes out to his work and to his labor until evening.
